      [3]            UNIVERSAL  ProdDeploy  Contoso           https://contoso.crm.dynamics.com        <application id>
  pac auth select --name Test
  pac auth who                      prints the active profile, user and environment. Run it before any import.
  pac org who                       details of the connected environment
  pac env list                      environments this identity can see
  pac env select --environment https://contoso-test.crm.dynamics.com      re-point the active profile

Target an environment per command (safer in scripts)
  pac solution export --environment https://contoso-dev.crm.dynamics.com --name RequestHub --path out/RequestHub.zip
  pac solution import --environment https://contoso-test.crm.dynamics.com --path out/RequestHub_managed.zip
  The --environment argument overrides the profile's default for that one command.

A guarded deployment script (PowerShell)
  param([Parameter(Mandatory)][ValidateSet("Test","Prod")] [string]$Target)
  pac auth select --name $Target
  $who = pac auth who | Out-String
  Write-Host $who
  if ($Target -eq "Prod") {
      $answer = Read-Host "Type PROD to import into production"
      if ($answer -ne "PROD") { throw "Cancelled" }
  }
  pac solution import --path "out/RequestHub_managed.zip" --settings-file "settings/$Target.json" --async --max-async-wait-time 60
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Import failed" }

Clean up
  pac auth delete --name Prod
  pac auth clear                    removes every stored profile. Run at the end of build agent jobs.

Where profiles live
  Stored per user on the machine in the PAC CLI profile folder, with tokens in the operating system's
  credential store. They are not part of a repository.
stepByStepInstructions: Install or update the PAC CLI.
Create one named profile per environment.
Use a service principal profile for production deployment.
Run pac auth who before any command that changes an environment.
Pass the environment explicitly in scripts.
Clear profiles on shared or build machines after use.
commonMistakes: Leaving default profile names so the list is unreadable.
Assuming the active profile without checking.
Writing a client secret into a script committed to Git.
Using a personal admin sign-in for automated production deployments.
troubleshooting: If a command hits the wrong environment, run pac auth who and select the right profile.
If sign-in loops or fails, delete the profile and create it again, or use device code.
If the service principal cannot connect, add it as an application user in that environment.
If commands are missing or behave differently, update the CLI to the current version.
seoTitle: Manage PAC CLI sign-ins for several environments
seoDescription: Create named authentication profiles for development, test and production, switch between them safely and check which one a command will use.

faqs.question: How do I connect PAC CLI to an environment?
faqs.answer: Run pac auth create with a name and the environment URL, then sign in. The profile is stored for later commands.

faqs.question: How do I switch environments in PAC CLI?
faqs.answer: Use pac auth select with the profile name, or pass an environment URL on the individual command.

faqs.question: How do I check which environment PAC CLI is using?
faqs.answer: Run pac auth who, which shows the active profile, the signed-in identity and the environment.

title: Give each maker a development environment and merge through Git
shortDescription: Stop makers overwriting each other in a shared Dev environment by giving each a personal developer environment, a branch and a build from source.
fullDescription: In a shared development environment, every maker's unfinished work ships with the next export. With one developer environment per maker, each person works in isolation, commits their change to a branch and merges through a pull request. An integration environment is built from the main branch, and releases come from that.
problemStatement: Two makers work in the same Dev environment. A release exports one maker's finished feature along with the other's half-built form, and the half-built form reaches test.
whenToUse: Teams of three or more makers on one solution
Features that take longer than one release cycle
Teams comfortable with Git and pull requests
whenNotToUse: A single maker or a pair who can coordinate by talking
Teams with no Git experience, where a shared Dev plus pipelines is safer
formulaOrCode:
Environments
  dev-<maker>      Developer type, one per maker. Free with the Power Apps Developer Plan, up to three per user.
                   Admins can create them for makers:
                   pac admin create --name "Dev - Priya" --type Developer --region unitedstates --user <object id>
  integration      Sandbox. Built from the main branch only. Nobody edits it by hand.
  test, prod       Managed solution imports from the build output.

Flow of a change
  1. Refresh the personal environment from main
       git checkout main && git pull
       pac solution pack   --folder src/RequestHub --zipfile out/RequestHub.zip --packagetype Unmanaged
       pac solution import --path out/RequestHub.zip --environment https://dev-priya.crm.dynamics.com \
           --force-overwrite --publish-changes
  2. Branch
       git checkout -b feature/escalation-screen
  3. Build the change in dev-priya, inside the solution.
  4. Bring it back to source
       pac solution export --name RequestHub --path out/RequestHub.zip --environment https://dev-priya.crm.dynamics.com
       pac solution unpack --zipfile out/RequestHub.zip --folder src/RequestHub --packagetype Unmanaged --allowDelete
       git add -A && git commit -m "Add escalation screen" && git push -u origin feature/escalation-screen
  5. Pull request into main. Reviewers read the diff. A validation build packs the branch and runs solution checker.
  6. On merge, the pipeline packs main, imports to integration, then produces the managed zip for test.

With Dataverse Git integration (no CLI for makers)
  Each developer environment is connected to the same repository and folder, on its own branch.
  Solutions > Source control: Commit pushes changes, Pull brings in others' merged work.
  Merging between branches still happens in Azure DevOps through pull requests.

What merges cleanly and what does not
  Clean: separate tables, columns, views, flows, new forms, new canvas apps, security roles for other tables.
  Conflict-prone: the same form XML, the same canvas app, the same flow, the sitemap, the same security role.
  Rule: one owner per conflict-prone component at a time. Record it on the work item
  ("locks: Request main form"). For a canvas app, split work by using components in a component library.

Version and identity
  All environments use the same publisher and the same solution unique name.
  Environment variables and connection references get personal values in each developer environment and are
  excluded from source by removing current values before export.

Keeping personal environments healthy
  Re-import from main at the start of each piece of work.
  If an environment drifts badly, delete it and create a new one. Developer environments are disposable.
  Reference data: load with the Configuration Migration Tool data set kept in the repository.

Lighter alternative
  One shared Dev, one solution per feature holding only the changed components, deployed with pipelines.
  Less isolation, far less tooling.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a developer environment for each maker and an integration environment.
Put the unpacked solution in a Git repository with a protected main branch.
Start each change by importing main into the personal environment and creating a branch.
Export and unpack the change, then open a pull request.
Validate each pull request by packing and running solution checker.
Build integration and release artefacts from main only.
commonMistakes: Editing the integration environment by hand.
Two makers changing the same form or canvas app in parallel.
Never refreshing personal environments, so exports carry stale components.
Different publishers in personal environments.
troubleshooting: If a merge conflict appears in form XML, take one side entirely and reapply the other change in the designer.
If import to the personal environment fails, reset or recreate it and import main again.
If unrelated changes appear in a pull request, the environment was not refreshed before the work started.
If makers find the cycle too heavy, move to Dataverse Git integration or the feature-solution approach.
seoTitle: Give each maker a development environment and merge through Git
seoDescription: Stop makers overwriting each other in a shared Dev environment by giving each a personal developer environment, a branch and a build from source.
primaryKeyword: Power Platform developer environment per maker branching

faqs.question: Should every maker have their own environment?
faqs.answer: For teams of several makers on one solution, yes. It isolates unfinished work, provided changes are merged through source control.

faqs.question: Are developer environments free?
faqs.answer: Each user can have up to three developer environments under the Power Apps Developer Plan, for building and testing only.

faqs.question: Can two people edit the same canvas app?
faqs.answer: Studio supports co-authoring in one environment, but parallel edits in separate environments cannot be merged reliably. Assign one owner at a time.

title: Add an approval step before a Power Platform pipeline deploys to production
shortDescription: Turn on the pre-deployment step for a pipeline stage and use a flow to request approval, then complete or reject the deployment from the result.
fullDescription: Power Platform pipelines can pause before a stage deploys and wait for an external decision. A cloud flow in the pipelines host environment receives the request, runs an approval and calls an action to continue or stop. This gives a recorded sign-off for production without leaving the product.
problemStatement: Any maker with access to the pipeline can push a solution to production at any time, with no second pair of eyes and no record of who agreed.
whenToUse: Production stages that need sign-off
Change control that requires a named approver
Adding automated checks before deployment
whenNotToUse: Development-to-test stages, where a gate only slows feedback
Using approval as the only control when makers also hold admin rights in production
formulaOrCode:
Turn on the gate
  Deployment Pipeline Configuration app (in the pipelines host environment)
    Pipelines > open the pipeline > Deployment Stages > open the Production stage
      Pre-Deployment Step Required: Yes
      (optional) Pre-Export Step Required: Yes       runs before the solution is exported from Dev
      (optional) Is Delegated Deployment: Yes        deploy as a service principal or stage owner instead of the maker

Flow (create it in the host environment, in a solution)
  Trigger: Microsoft Dataverse > When an action is performed
    Catalog: Microsoft Dataverse Common        Category: Power Platform Pipelines
    Table name: (none)
    Action name: OnPreDeploymentStarted
  Useful trigger outputs (OutputParameters):
    StageRunId, DeploymentPipelineName, DeploymentStageName, ArtifactName, ArtifactVersion, DeploymentNotes

  Condition: only handle the production stage
    triggerOutputs()?['body/OutputParameters/DeploymentStageName']   is equal to   Production
    (If no: Terminate, Succeeded. Other stages with the step enabled need their own handling.)

  Get the requester
    Dataverse > Get a row by ID: Deployment Stage Runs, Row ID = StageRunId, Expand: createdby($select=fullname,internalemailaddress)

  Approvals > Start and wait for an approval (Approve/Reject - First to respond)
    Title:   Deploy @{ArtifactName} @{ArtifactVersion} to Production
    Assigned to: release-approvers@contoso.com
    Details: Requested by @{outputs('Get_stage_run')?['body/createdby/fullname']}
             Notes: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/OutputParameters/DeploymentNotes']}
    Item link: link to the stage run or the work item

  Condition: Outcome is equal to Approve
    Yes > Dataverse > Perform an unbound action
            Action name: UpdatePreDeploymentStepStatus
            StageRunId: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/OutputParameters/StageRunId']}
            PreDeploymentStepStatus: 20                  (20 = Completed, 30 = Failed)
    No  > same action with PreDeploymentStepStatus: 30
            Comments from the approver can be written to the stage run's notes.

  Timeout: Start and wait > Settings > Timeout P3D. Configure run after "has timed out" > set status 30.

What the maker sees
  After choosing Deploy, the stage shows "Pending pre-deployment step". On approval it continues without
  further action. On rejection it shows Failed with the pre-deployment step as the reason.

Other triggers in the same category
  OnDeploymentRequested, OnPreDeploymentStarted, OnPreDeploymentCompleted, OnDeploymentStarted,
  OnDeploymentCompleted          use the last one to post release notes to Teams or tag the Git commit.

Automated checks before approval
  In the same flow, before the approval: confirm the version is higher than production, that solution checker
  results have no critical issues, and that a change ticket number is present in the notes. Fail fast with status 30.

Permissions
  Approvers do not need access to the target environment. The flow's Dataverse connection needs the Deployment
  Pipeline Administrator role in the host.
stepByStepInstructions: Open the pipeline's production stage in the configuration app and require the pre-deployment step.
Create a flow in the host environment triggered by OnPreDeploymentStarted.
Filter to the stage you want to gate.
Start an approval with the solution name, version and notes.
Call UpdatePreDeploymentStepStatus with 20 on approval or 30 on rejection.
Handle timeouts so deployments never wait indefinitely.
commonMistakes: Enabling the step with no flow, which leaves deployments pending.
Not filtering by stage, so one flow answers for every pipeline.
Letting the requester approve their own deployment.
No timeout path.
troubleshooting: If deployments stay pending, check the flow ran and that the unbound action received the right StageRunId.
If the trigger never fires, the flow is in the wrong environment. It must be in the pipelines host.
If the action fails with privileges, give the connection's user the pipeline administrator role.
If approvers cannot see the request, check the Approvals connector's environment and their email addresses.
seoTitle: Add an approval step before a Power Platform pipeline deploys to production
seoDescription: Turn on the pre-deployment step for a pipeline stage and use a flow to request approval, then complete or reject the deployment from the result.

faqs.question: Can Power Platform pipelines require approval?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enable the pre-deployment step on a stage and use a flow to approve or reject the deployment.

faqs.question: Where does the approval flow live?
faqs.answer: In the pipelines host environment, triggered by the OnPreDeploymentStarted Dataverse action.

faqs.question: What is delegated deployment?
faqs.answer: A stage setting that runs the deployment as a service principal or the stage owner, so makers do not need rights in production.

title: Ship an urgent production fix without releasing unfinished work
shortDescription: A hotfix route for managed solutions: rebuild production's version in a clean environment, apply the fix, deploy it and merge it back into development.
fullDescription: When production has a fault, the development environment usually already contains next month's half-finished features. Exporting from it would ship them. A hotfix needs a copy of exactly what is in production, a minimal change, a fast test and a guaranteed merge back so the fix is not lost at the next release.
problemStatement: A flow fails in production. The fix takes five minutes in Dev, but Dev also holds an unfinished form redesign, so exporting the solution would release that too.
whenToUse: Urgent faults in production between planned releases
Teams whose development environment runs ahead of production
Managed solutions with source control or stored release zips
whenNotToUse: Problems that can wait for the next scheduled release
Editing production directly, which creates unmanaged layers and is lost or hidden later
formulaOrCode:
Prerequisites that make hotfixes possible
  Every release's managed AND unmanaged zip is kept (pipeline artefacts or a release library), or the unpacked
  source is tagged in Git:  git tag v1.4.0.0
  A spare sandbox, or the ability to create or reset one quickly.

Route A: from source control (preferred)
  1. Branch from the production tag
       git checkout -b hotfix/1.4.0.1 v1.4.0.0
  2. Build a hotfix environment
       pac admin reset --environment https://contoso-hotfix.crm.dynamics.com   (or create a new sandbox)
       pac solution pack   --folder src/RequestHub --zipfile out/RequestHub.zip --packagetype Unmanaged
       pac solution import --path out/RequestHub.zip --environment https://contoso-hotfix.crm.dynamics.com --publish-changes
  3. Make the fix in the hotfix environment. Change only what is needed.
  4. Set version 1.4.0.1, export, unpack, commit to the hotfix branch
       pac solution online-version --solution-name RequestHub --solution-version 1.4.0.1
       pac solution export --name RequestHub --path out/RequestHub.zip
       pac solution export --name RequestHub --path out/RequestHub_managed.zip --managed
       pac solution unpack --zipfile out/RequestHub.zip --folder src/RequestHub --allowDelete
  5. Import managed to Test (or a copy of production), run the smoke test and the specific case.
  6. Import managed to Production as an update.
  7. Merge the hotfix branch into main, and apply the same change in Dev (import or repeat by hand).
       git checkout main && git merge hotfix/1.4.0.1

Route B: no source control, release zips kept
  Import the unmanaged zip of the production version into a clean sandbox, then continue from step 3.

Route C: a solution patch
  In an environment holding the production version unmanaged: Solutions > select > Clone a patch.
  Add only the fixed component, export managed, import to production. Version 1.4.1.0 style numbering.
  The next full release must be at a higher version and include the fix. Patches lock the parent solution
  against edits in that environment until rolled up, which is why Route A is usually simpler.

Route D: fix forward from Dev (only when Dev equals production plus the fix)
  Acceptable just after a release when nothing else has changed. Check with a diff of unpacked source.

Emergency mitigation while the fix is built
  Turn off the failing flow, or use a feature flag (environment variable) to hide the broken feature.
  Document any direct production change and remove its unmanaged layer after the hotfix lands.

Version numbers
  major.minor.build.revision: planned releases raise build, hotfixes raise revision.
  1.4.0.0 (release) > 1.4.0.1 (hotfix) > 1.5.0.0 (next release, must include the fix).

After the hotfix
  Confirm the fix is in main and in Dev before the next export. A regression test for the fault is added to
  the smoke test list. Record the incident and the release in the release notes.
stepByStepInstructions: Keep each release's source tag or zips so production's version can be rebuilt.
Create a hotfix environment from the production version.
Make the smallest change that fixes the fault and raise the revision number.
Test the managed build against the failing case and the smoke tests.
Import to production as an update.
Merge the fix back into main and development before the next release.
commonMistakes: Exporting from Dev and shipping unfinished work.
Fixing directly in production and forgetting the unmanaged layer.
Not merging the hotfix back, so the next release reintroduces the fault.
Skipping test because the change is small.
troubleshooting: If you cannot rebuild the production version, note that a managed solution cannot be exported as unmanaged. Restore a copy of Dev from a backup taken at release time.
If the next release fails to import, its version is lower than the hotfix. Raise it.
If the fix disappears after the next release, it was never merged into main.
If an unmanaged layer hides the hotfix in production, remove the active layer on that component.
seoTitle: Ship an urgent production fix without releasing unfinished work
seoDescription: A hotfix route for managed solutions: rebuild production's version in a clean environment, apply the fix, deploy it and merge it back into development.

faqs.question: How do I hotfix a managed solution?
faqs.answer: Rebuild the production version in a clean environment, apply the fix, export it as managed with a higher revision and import it as an update.

faqs.question: Can I just fix it in production?
faqs.answer: Only as a recorded emergency mitigation. Direct edits create an unmanaged layer that hides later releases until removed.

faqs.question: How do I avoid losing the hotfix?
faqs.answer: Merge the hotfix branch into main and apply the change in development before the next export.

title: Write repeatable tests for a canvas app with Test Studio
shortDescription: Record and write test cases for a canvas app's key journeys, assert on results with Power Fx and run the suite from a link or a pipeline before each release.
fullDescription: Test Studio stores test cases inside the canvas app. Each case is a list of Power Fx steps that set control values, select buttons and assert what should be true. Suites can be played in the browser or opened by URL from a pipeline, which makes a regression check before release a matter of minutes.
problemStatement: Before each release someone clicks through the app by hand, skips the parts that seem unchanged, and a broken submit button reaches production.
whenToUse: Apps with a few critical journeys such as submit, approve and search
Regression checks before each release
Apps maintained by more than one maker
whenNotToUse: Visual layout checking, which tests cannot judge
Flows and server logic, which need their own tests
Apps built mostly from unsupported controls or nested galleries
formulaOrCode:
Open
  Power Apps Studio > Advanced tools > Open tests          (the app must be saved and published once)

Structure
  Test suite: "Request submission"
    Test case: "Submit a valid request"
    Test case: "Required title blocks submit"
  Each step is one Power Fx formula. Record adds steps as you use the app. Edit them afterwards.

Functions available in tests
  SetProperty(Control.Property, value)        set an input
  Select(Control)  /  Select(Gallery, row, ChildControl)
  Assert(condition, "message when it fails")
  Trace("message", TraceSeverity.Information)  appears in results and Monitor

Test case: Submit a valid request
  Step 1  Select(btnNewRequest)
  Step 2  SetProperty(txtTitle.Text, "Test request " & Text(Now(), "yyyymmdd-hhmmss"))
  Step 3  SetProperty(drpCategory.Selected, LookUp(Categories, Title = "Hardware"))
  Step 4  SetProperty(txtAmount.Text, "250")
  Step 5  Assert(btnSubmit.DisplayMode = DisplayMode.Edit, "Submit should be enabled when the form is valid")
  Step 6  Select(btnSubmit)
  Step 7  Assert(lblConfirmation.Visible, "Confirmation should show after submit")
  Step 8  Assert(!IsBlank(LookUp(Requests, Title = txtTitle.Text)), "The request should exist in the data source")

Test case: Required title blocks submit
  Step 1  Select(btnNewRequest)
  Step 2  SetProperty(txtTitle.Text, "")
  Step 3  Assert(btnSubmit.DisplayMode = DisplayMode.Disabled, "Submit should be disabled without a title")
  Step 4  Assert(lblTitleError.Visible, "Title error should be visible")

Gallery row
  Select(galRequests, 1, btnOpen)
  Assert(lblDetailTitle.Text = First(colVisibleRequests).Title, "Detail should show the selected request")

Set-up and results (Test > properties)
  OnTestCaseStart:   Set(gblTestMode, true)                         let the app skip emails or use a test list
  OnTestCaseComplete: Patch(TestResults, Defaults(TestResults), { Title: TestCaseResult.TestCaseName,
                        Passed: TestCaseResult.Success, Message: TestCaseResult.TestFailureMessage })
  OnTestSuiteComplete: Notify("Suite finished: " & TestSuiteResult.TestsPassed & " passed, " &
                        TestSuiteResult.TestsFailed & " failed")

Run
  Test Studio > Play: opens the published app in a new tab and runs the steps.
  Copy play link: a URL that runs the suite. Open it in a pipeline with a browser automation step, then read the
  outcome from the TestResults list written by OnTestCaseComplete.
  Publish the app after changing tests. Play runs the published version.

Keep test data clean
  Create rows with a recognisable title prefix and remove them in a final step:
  RemoveIf(Requests, StartsWith(Title, "Test request "))

Limits
  No support for every control (some modern controls, code components, media and some nested galleries).
  Tests run as the signed-in user, with that user's permissions.

Power Apps Test Engine
  For pipeline-first testing: YAML test plans run with pac test run against canvas and model-driven apps, using
  the same Power Fx assertions with browser automation underneath.
stepByStepInstructions: Name the controls used in the app's main journeys.
Open Test Studio and create a suite for each journey.
Record the steps, then replace recorded values with deliberate test data.
Add Assert steps for each expected result.
Write results to a list in OnTestCaseComplete.
Publish and run the suite before each release.
commonMistakes: Recording without adding assertions, so the test cannot fail.
Depending on existing data that changes.
Forgetting to publish after editing tests.
Letting test runs send real emails or approvals.
troubleshooting: If a step fails on a control, check the control is supported and visible on the current screen.
If the test passes when the feature is broken, the Assert checks the wrong thing. Assert on the data source.
If timing causes failures, assert on a variable the app sets when the operation finishes.
If test rows pile up, add a clean-up step or a separate test list.
seoTitle: Write repeatable tests for a canvas app with Test Studio
seoDescription: Record and write test cases for a canvas app's key journeys, assert on results with Power Fx and run the suite from a link or a pipeline before each release.

faqs.question: Can I automate testing of a Power Apps canvas app?
faqs.answer: Yes. Test Studio records and plays Power Fx test steps with assertions, and Test Engine runs YAML test plans from a pipeline.

faqs.question: Do tests run against the editor version of the app?
faqs.answer: No. They run against the published version, so publish after changing the app or its tests.

faqs.question: Can Test Studio test flows?
faqs.answer: Not directly. It can assert on what a flow changed in the data source once the app triggers it.

title: Run a smoke test after every deployment
shortDescription: A flow that checks the essentials straight after an import: solution version, flows turned on, environment variables set, connections healthy and a test row processed.
fullDescription: A successful import only means the files went in. A smoke test confirms the system actually works: the right version is installed, flows are running, settings have values and one end-to-end case completes. Run automatically after deployment, it finds a broken release in minutes instead of when users report it.
problemStatement: The import reports success on Friday evening. On Monday it emerges that the approval flow was off and an environment variable was empty all weekend.
whenToUse: Every deployment to test and production
Releases done out of hours
Solutions with several flows and environment-specific settings
whenNotToUse: Replacing proper acceptance testing of new features
Checks that create visible noise for real users, such as real approval emails
formulaOrCode:
Trigger
  Manual (run by the release owner), or an HTTP request called by the pipeline's last step, or the pipelines
  host trigger OnDeploymentCompleted.
  Input: expectedVersion (text), for example 1.5.0.0

Initialise  varResults (Array)       each check appends { "check": "...", "ok": true/false, "detail": "..." }

Check 1: solution version
  Dataverse > List rows: Solutions      Filter rows: uniquename eq 'RequestHub'      Select: version,ismanaged
  ok:  first(body('List_solutions')?['value'])?['version'] equals expectedVersion  and  ismanaged is true

Check 2: flows are on
  Dataverse > List rows: Processes
    Fetch Xml Query:
      <fetch><entity name="workflow"><attribute name="name" /><attribute name="statecode" />
        <filter><condition attribute="category" operator="eq" value="5" />
                <condition attribute="statecode" operator="ne" value="1" /></filter>
        <link-entity name="solutioncomponent" from="objectid" to="workflowid">
          <link-entity name="solution" from="solutionid" to="solutionid">
            <filter><condition attribute="uniquename" operator="eq" value="RequestHub" /></filter>
          </link-entity></link-entity></entity></fetch>
  ok:  length(body('List_flows_off')?['value']) equals 0        detail: join of the names that are off

Check 3: environment variables have values
  Dataverse > List rows: Environment Variable Definitions
    Filter rows: startswith(schemaname,'cnt_')
    Expand Query: environmentvariabledefinition_environmentvariablevalue($select=value)
  For each definition: effective value = coalesce(first(values)?['value'], defaultvalue)
  ok:  no definition with an empty effective value

Check 4: connections work (one cheap read per connector)
  SharePoint > Get items, Top Count 1 on the app's main list
  Dataverse > List rows, Row count 1 on the main table
  Office 365 Users > Get my profile
  Put each in its own Scope. A following action with run after "has failed" appends ok: false.

Check 5: end-to-end case
  Dataverse > Add a new row: Service Requests
    Title: SMOKE TEST @{utcNow()}       Category: Test       cnt_issmoketest: Yes
  Delay 2 minutes (or Do until status changes, limit 10 checks, 30 seconds apart)
  Get a row by ID > ok: status equals the value your automation should have set (for example Assigned)
  Clean up: Delete the row. Automations should skip notifications when cnt_issmoketest is Yes.

Check 6: app is reachable
  Power Apps for Admins > Get App (or List rows: Canvas Apps filtered by name) > ok: the app exists and its
  last published time is after the deployment started.

Report
  Filter array: varResults where ok is false
  Create HTML table from varResults
  Teams > Post message in a channel:
    @{if(equals(length(body('Filter_failed')),0),'PASSED','FAILED')}: RequestHub @{expectedVersion} in Production
    followed by the table
  If any failed: Terminate with status Failed, so a calling pipeline stage fails as well.

Run it
  Azure DevOps or GitHub: call the flow's HTTP trigger after the import step and fail the job when the
  response reports failures. Keep the trigger URL in a secret variable.

Keep it short
  Target under five minutes and under ten checks. Add a check whenever an incident shows a gap.
stepByStepInstructions: List what must be true for the system to work after a release.
Build a flow that runs each check and records pass or fail.
Include one end-to-end test row that automations treat as a test.
Post the results to the release channel.
Fail the flow when any check fails.
Call the flow from the pipeline or run it straight after each import.
commonMistakes: Treating a successful import as proof the release works.
Smoke tests that send real approvals or emails to users.
No clean-up of test rows.
A test so long that nobody waits for it.
troubleshooting: If the flows check reports false failures, exclude flows that are intentionally off by name.
If the end-to-end check times out, lengthen the wait or check that the trigger flow is on.
If the smoke test itself is off after import, it is in the same solution. Keep it in a separate solution in each environment.
If results are ignored, make the pipeline stage depend on the result.
seoTitle: Run a smoke test after every deployment
seoDescription: A flow that checks the essentials straight after an import: solution version, flows turned on, environment variables set, connections healthy and a test row processed.
primaryKeyword: Power Platform post deployment smoke test

faqs.question: What should a Power Platform smoke test check?
faqs.answer: The installed solution version, that flows are on, that environment variables have values, that connections work and that one end-to-end case completes.

faqs.question: When should it run?
faqs.answer: Immediately after every import to test and production, ideally triggered by the pipeline.

faqs.question: Should the smoke test be part of the solution?
faqs.answer: Keep it in its own small solution so a failed deployment of the main solution cannot disable the check.

title: Turn on Managed Environments and set sharing limits
shortDescription: Enable Managed Environments on an environment, cap how widely canvas apps and flows can be shared, and switch on the weekly usage digest and solution checker enforcement.
fullDescription: Managed Environments is a set of admin controls applied per environment. It adds sharing limits, a weekly digest of app and flow usage, solution checker enforcement on import, maker welcome content and access to pipelines as a target. Each user of a managed environment needs a premium licence, so it is turned on deliberately, not everywhere.
problemStatement: A canvas app in production is shared with Everyone by its maker, and admins only find out when a support call arrives from a department that was never meant to use it.
whenToUse: Production and test environments under release control
Environments where sharing needs a ceiling
Organisations that want weekly usage figures without building reports
whenNotToUse: Environments used by people on Microsoft 365 seeded licences only, who would lose access to apps
Treating it as a replacement for DLP policies and security roles
formulaOrCode:
Enable
  Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > select the environment > Enable Managed Environments
  PowerShell:
    Install-Module Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell
    Add-PowerAppsAccount
    $gov = [pscustomobject]@{ protectionLevel = "Standard" }
    Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <environment id> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $gov

Licensing check before enabling
  Every active user of apps, flows and Copilot Studio agents in a managed environment needs a standalone
  premium licence (Power Apps Premium, per app, Power Automate Premium, or Dynamics 365).
  Users on Microsoft 365 licences alone get a licence prompt.

Settings (Edit Managed Environments)
  Limit sharing
    Canvas apps:      Exclude sharing with security groups        On for personal-productivity environments
                      Limit total individuals who can be shared to: 20
    Solution-aware cloud flows:  Don't allow sharing / limit to a number
    Copilot Studio agents:       limit editors and viewers
    Applies to new shares. Existing shares stay until removed.
  Solution checker enforcement
    None | Warn | Block          Block stops imports with critical issues. Start at Warn.
    Exclude specific rules if one produces accepted findings.
  Usage insights
    Include insights for this environment in the weekly email digest: On
    Recipients: tenant and environment admins by default. Add others under Tenant settings > Weekly digest.
  Maker welcome content
    A short message and a "Learn more" link shown when a maker first opens Power Apps in the environment.
    Example: "This is Production. Changes arrive through pipelines only. Build in your Developer environment."
  Data policies
    Shows the DLP policies applied to this environment.

Suggested values by environment type
                      Sharing limit        Checker     Digest
  Developer/personal  No groups, max 5     None        Off
  Shared Dev          No limit             Warn        On
  Test                No limit             Warn        Off
  Production          Groups allowed       Block       On

What sharing limits do not cover
  Model-driven apps (controlled by security roles), non-solution flows' run-only sharing, and SharePoint
  permissions behind an app.

Related controls unlocked
  Power Platform pipelines targets, environment groups and rules, IP firewall and IP cookie binding,
  customer-managed keys, extended backup retention, Block unmanaged customizations.

Turn off
  Edit Managed Environments > disable. Remove dependent settings first (pipelines targets, IP firewall).
stepByStepInstructions: Confirm users of the environment hold premium licences.
Enable Managed Environments on the environment.
Set sharing limits appropriate to the environment's purpose.
Set solution checker enforcement to Warn, then Block once imports are clean.
Turn on the weekly digest and add recipients.
Write maker welcome content that states the environment's rules.
commonMistakes: Enabling on the default environment without checking licences.
Expecting sharing limits to remove existing shares.
Going straight to Block and stopping a release.
Assuming it restricts model-driven app access.
troubleshooting: If users see a licence prompt after enabling, assign premium licences or disable the setting.
If an import is blocked, read the solution checker results on the import and fix or exclude the rule.
If the digest does not arrive, check recipients and that insights are enabled for the environment.
If a maker cannot share with a group, the group exclusion is on. Share with individuals or relax the rule.
seoTitle: Turn on Managed Environments and set sharing limits
seoDescription: Enable Managed Environments on an environment, cap how widely canvas apps and flows can be shared, and switch on the weekly usage digest and solution checker enforcement.
primaryKeyword: Power Platform Managed Environments sharing limits

faqs.question: What are Managed Environments in Power Platform?
faqs.answer: A per-environment set of governance features including sharing limits, usage insights, solution checker enforcement and pipelines.

faqs.question: Do Managed Environments need extra licences?
faqs.answer: Users active in a managed environment need standalone premium licences. Microsoft 365 seeded rights are not enough.

faqs.question: Can I limit who a canvas app is shared with?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sharing limits can block sharing with security groups and cap the number of individuals.

title: Restrict who can enter an environment with a security group
shortDescription: Attach a Microsoft Entra security group to an environment so only its members are added as users, and understand what that does and does not control.
fullDescription: Without a security group, every licensed user in the tenant can be added to a Dataverse environment and appears in its user list. Associating a group limits environment membership to that group. It is the first gate. Security roles then decide what members can do.
problemStatement: A production environment lists thousands of enabled users who have nothing to do with the app, and any of them could be given a role by mistake or reach data through a shared app.
whenToUse: Production, test and sandbox environments with a defined audience
Separating departments or projects by environment
Keeping user lists short and reviewable
whenNotToUse: The default environment, which cannot be restricted by a security group
Using group membership as the only control, with broad security roles inside
formulaOrCode:
Create the group
  Microsoft Entra admin center > Groups > New group
    Type: Security        Name: PP-RequestHub-Prod-Users        Membership: Assigned (or Dynamic)
  Members of nested groups are not added ahead of time. They are added when they first open the
  environment and still need a security role, so direct membership is simpler to manage.
  Microsoft 365 groups also work. One group per environment.

Associate it
  Power Platform admin center > Environments > select > Edit (Details) > Security group > choose the group > Save
  New environment: choose the group in the creation dialog.
  Clearing the field later removes the restriction.

What changes
  Members with a licence: added to the environment as enabled users (on first access or by sync).
  Non-members already in the environment: disabled. Their records and ownership remain.
  Removing someone from the group disables them in the environment.
  Tenant-level admins (Power Platform admin, Dynamics 365 admin) can still enter regardless.
  Service principals (application users) are not governed by the group.

What it does not do
  Give any permission. Members still need a security role to see or do anything.
  Restrict canvas apps that use only non-Dataverse connectors from being shared, although only environment
  users can open apps in the environment.
  Apply to the default environment.

Speed up access for a new member
  Environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > Add user > search > Add        forces the sync
  Flow: Power Platform for Admins > Force Sync user (environment, user object id)
  PowerShell: Add-AdminPowerAppsSyncUser -EnvironmentName <id> -PrincipalObjectId <user object id>

Assign roles by team instead of per user
  Settings > Teams > Create team
    Team type: Microsoft Entra ID Security Group        Group: PP-RequestHub-Prod-Users
    Membership type: Members
  Manage security roles on the team: Basic User + Request Hub User.
  Members inherit the roles when they sign in. With "Member's privilege inheritance: Direct User" set on
  the role, they can own rows personally.

Suggested groups per environment
  PP-<App>-<Env>-Users        environment access + user role through the group team
  PP-<App>-<Env>-Admins       second group team with the admin app role
  Makers in Dev: PP-<App>-Dev-Makers with Environment Maker.
  The environment's security group must contain all of these people, so either nest by membership rules
  (dynamic group) or make the Users group the superset.

Review
  Entra access reviews on the group every quarter. Removing a member removes environment access at next sync.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a security group for the environment's intended users.
Associate the group with the environment in the admin center.
Create a group team linked to the same group and give it security roles.
Add members to the group and force a sync for anyone who needs access immediately.
Check the user list for people disabled by the change.
Review group membership on a schedule.
commonMistakes: Using nested groups and expecting members to appear in the environment before they first sign in.
Assuming group membership grants permissions.
Applying a group to an environment in use without warning existing users.
Assigning roles one user at a time.
troubleshooting: If a member cannot get in, check they are a direct member, licensed and synced.
If a user became disabled, they are not in the group. Add them or accept the removal.
If an app shows no data, the user has environment access but no security role.
If the option is missing, the environment is the default one or has no Dataverse database.
seoTitle: Restrict who can enter an environment with a security group
seoDescription: Attach a Microsoft Entra security group to an environment so only its members are added as users, and understand what that does and does not control.

faqs.question: How do I restrict access to a Power Platform environment?
faqs.answer: Associate a Microsoft Entra security group with the environment. Only its members are enabled as users.

faqs.question: Does adding someone to the group give them access to data?
faqs.answer: No. They also need a security role, assigned directly or through a team.

faqs.question: Can I put a security group on the default environment?
faqs.answer: No. The default environment always includes every licensed user in the tenant.

title: Bring the default environment under control
shortDescription: Rename the default environment, restrict its connectors, route new makers to personal developer environments and move important apps out of it.
fullDescription: Every tenant has a default environment that all licensed users can build in and that cannot be deleted or restricted by a security group. Left alone it fills with experiments, business-critical apps and abandoned flows side by side. A few settings turn it into a clearly labelled personal productivity space and send real projects elsewhere.
problemStatement: The default environment holds hundreds of apps from every department, some critical, most unowned, all sharing one Dataverse database and one set of connectors.
whenToUse: Any tenant where makers build in the default environment
Starting a governance programme
Before a licensing or capacity review
whenNotToUse: Blocking the default environment entirely, which pushes makers to unmanaged shadow tools
Moving apps without telling their owners and users
formulaOrCode:
1. Rename it
   Admin center > Environments > the default environment > Edit > Name: "Personal Productivity (default)"
   The label "(default)" stays. The name tells makers what it is for.

2. Apply a strict DLP policy scoped to it
   Policy: "Default environment"        Scope: Add multiple environments > only the default
   Business: SharePoint, Office 365 Outlook, Office 365 Users, Teams, OneDrive for Business, Approvals,
             Excel Online (Business), Planner, Notifications, Forms
   Blocked:  HTTP, HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID, custom connectors (pattern rule *), social and consumer
             connectors, SQL Server and other premium data sources
   Non-business: the remainder
   Exclude the default environment from the broader tenant policy so the two do not conflict in unexpected ways.

3. Route makers to their own environments
   Admin center > Manage > Tenant settings > Environment routing: On
     Applies to: all makers, or a security group for a phased start
     Environment group: assign new developer environments to a group with your rules
   Effect: a maker opening make.powerapps.com lands in a personal Developer environment that is created for
   them, instead of the default. Developer environments created by routing are Managed Environments
   and do not count against the tenant's Dataverse capacity.

4. Limit who is an admin and who can create
   Tenant settings > Developer environment assignments: Everyone
   Tenant settings > Production environment assignments: Only specific admins
   Tenant settings > Trial environment assignments: Only specific admins
   Default environment > Settings > Users + permissions: review holders of System Administrator.
   Everyone has Environment Maker in the default environment. This cannot be removed from the tenant as a
   whole, but sharing limits can be applied if it is a Managed Environment.

5. Limit sharing (if you enable Managed Environments on the default)
   Exclude sharing with security groups: On        Limit individuals: 10 to 20
   Check licensing first: users of apps in a managed environment need premium licences.

6. Find what matters
   Inventory: Get-AdminPowerApp -EnvironmentName <default id> | select DisplayName, Owner, LastModifiedTime
              Get-AdminFlow -EnvironmentName <default id>
   Flag apps shared with more than 20 users or with a group, apps using premium connectors, flows running
   daily under a named individual, and anything whose owner has left.

7. Move the important ones
   Add the app, its flows, connection references and environment variables to a solution in the default
   environment > export > import to a dedicated environment > re-share > tell users the new link >
   after two weeks remove the original.
   SharePoint-form customisations cannot move. They stay tied to their list.

8. Clean up the remainder
   Contact owners of items unused for 6 months (the CoE Starter Kit has an inactivity process). Delete after
   a notice period. Deleted canvas apps can be restored for a limited time with Get-AdminDeletedPowerAppsList
   and Get-AdminRecoverDeletedPowerApp.

9. Welcome message
   Managed Environments > maker welcome content, or a pinned Teams post: what the default environment is for,
   where to request a project environment, and the support route.
stepByStepInstructions: Rename the default environment to state its purpose.
Scope a restrictive DLP policy to it.
Turn on environment routing so new makers get developer environments.
Restrict creation of production and trial environments to admins.
Inventory apps and flows and identify the widely used ones.
Move important solutions to dedicated environments and retire abandoned items with notice.
commonMistakes: Leaving HTTP and custom connectors open in the default environment.
Moving an app without re-sharing or communicating the new link.
Deleting unowned items without a notice period.
Enabling Managed Environments on the default without a licence check.
troubleshooting: If a flow is suspended after the DLP change, move it to a project environment where its connectors are allowed.
If makers cannot find their apps, they were routed to a developer environment. Show them the environment picker.
If an app will not export, add it to a solution first and include its dependencies.
If routing is not happening, check the setting's target group and that developer environment creation is allowed.
seoTitle: Bring the default environment under control
seoDescription: Rename the default environment, restrict its connectors, route new makers to personal developer environments and move important apps out of it.

faqs.question: Can I delete or disable the default environment?
faqs.answer: No. It always exists and all licensed users can build in it. You can rename it, restrict connectors and route makers elsewhere.

faqs.question: What is environment routing?
faqs.answer: A tenant setting that sends makers to their own developer environment instead of the default when they open the maker portal.

faqs.question: Should production apps live in the default environment?
faqs.answer: No. Move them to dedicated environments with their own access, DLP policy and release process.

title: Block cross-tenant connections with tenant isolation
shortDescription: Stop apps and flows in your tenant connecting to other tenants with Entra-based connectors, and the reverse, with an allow-list for approved partners.
fullDescription: A maker can sign in to a connector with an account from another organisation and move data between tenants in a flow. DLP policies do not stop this, because the connector is the same. Tenant isolation blocks connections that authenticate against a different Microsoft Entra tenant, in both directions, with exceptions you list.
problemStatement: A flow copies files from the company SharePoint to a SharePoint site in a personal or partner tenant, using a second connection signed in with an outside account.
whenToUse: Tenants handling regulated or confidential data
Organisations with a small, known set of partner tenants
Closing the gap DLP policies leave open
whenNotToUse: Tenants whose apps legitimately connect to many external tenants, without building the allow-list first
Expecting it to cover connectors that do not use Microsoft Entra authentication
formulaOrCode:
Where
  Power Platform admin center > Security > Identity and access > Tenant isolation
  (older navigation: Policies > Tenant isolation)

Directions
  Inbound    connections created in ANOTHER tenant that sign in to YOUR tenant's data
  Outbound   connections created in YOUR tenant that sign in to another tenant

Turn on
  Tenant isolation: On       With no rules, both directions are blocked for Entra-based connectors.

Allow-list rules (New tenant rule)
  Direction: Inbound | Outbound | Inbound and Outbound
  Tenant: domain or tenant ID, for example fabrikam.com or 3f2a...     * means all tenants
  Examples:
    Partner you send data to:              Outbound    fabrikam.com
    Parent company reading your data:      Inbound     contoso-group.com
    Two-way with a subsidiary:             Inbound and Outbound    3f2a1c9e-....

What is covered
  Connectors that authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID: SharePoint, Dataverse, Office 365 Outlook, OneDrive
  for Business, Teams, Azure AD-secured custom connectors, SQL Server with Entra sign-in, and similar.
What is not covered
  Connectors using API keys, basic authentication or non-Entra OAuth (for example many third-party SaaS
  connectors). Control those with DLP policies.
  The HTTP connector to arbitrary endpoints. Block or restrict it with DLP and endpoint filtering.
  Guests accessing your apps: a B2B guest signs in to YOUR tenant, so that is not a cross-tenant connection.

Before turning it on: find existing cross-tenant connections
  Admin center > Tenant isolation page offers a report of impacted connections where available.
  PowerShell:
    Get-AdminPowerAppConnection | Select-Object DisplayName, ConnectorName, EnvironmentName,
        @{n='Account';e={$_.Statuses.target}}, @{n='CreatedBy';e={$_.CreatedBy.userPrincipalName}} |
      Where-Object { $_.CreatedBy -and $_.DisplayName -notlike "*@contoso.com" }
    The connection display name is usually the signed-in account. Names outside your domains indicate
    cross-tenant use.
  CoE Starter Kit inventory: connection identities table lists accounts used per connector.

Roll-out
  1. Report and contact the owners of cross-tenant connections.
  2. Add rules for approved partner tenants.
  3. Turn isolation on. Existing blocked connections fail at their next run with an authorisation error.
  4. Publish the request route for a new partner tenant (who approves, how long it takes).

What users see
  Makers who add a blocked cross-tenant connection see a data policy error and the connection is not added.
  Flows that break the policy are saved as suspended and do not run until the connection is removed.

Entra tenant restrictions
  Tenant isolation is specific to Power Platform connectors. Entra cross-tenant access settings and tenant
  restrictions cover sign-ins more broadly. Use both for defence in depth.
stepByStepInstructions: List existing connections that sign in to other tenants.
Agree which partner tenants are approved and in which direction.
Add allow-list rules for those tenants.
Tell affected makers the date and the request route.
Turn tenant isolation on.
Watch for failed flows in the first week and review new requests.
commonMistakes: Turning it on without an inventory and breaking partner integrations.
Using a wildcard rule that defeats the control.
Assuming it blocks API-key connectors or HTTP calls.
Confusing guest access with cross-tenant connections.
troubleshooting: If a legitimate flow fails, add an outbound rule for that tenant or redesign the integration.
If a partner's flow can no longer read your data, they need an inbound rule on your side.
If data still leaves through a non-Entra connector, block or classify it in DLP.
If the error persists after adding a rule, recreate the connection.
seoTitle: Block cross-tenant connections with tenant isolation
seoDescription: Stop apps and flows in your tenant connecting to other tenants with Entra-based connectors, and the reverse, with an allow-list for approved partners.

faqs.question: What does tenant isolation do in Power Platform?
faqs.answer: It blocks connections that authenticate to a different Microsoft Entra tenant, inbound or outbound, except for tenants on an allow-list.

faqs.question: Is tenant isolation the same as a DLP policy?
faqs.answer: No. DLP controls which connectors can be combined. Tenant isolation controls which tenants Entra-based connections can sign in to.

faqs.question: Does it affect guest users?
faqs.answer: No. Guests sign in to your tenant, so their access is not a cross-tenant connection.

title: Assign Power Platform admin roles with least privilege
shortDescription: Which role does what, from tenant-level Power Platform Administrator down to Environment Maker, and how to grant admin access just in time instead of permanently.
fullDescription: Power Platform has tenant-wide admin roles in Microsoft Entra and per-environment roles in Dataverse. Too many permanent administrators is the commonest finding in a security review. Mapping each duty to the smallest role, and activating the powerful ones only when needed, cuts that risk without slowing anyone down.
problemStatement: Twelve people hold Global Administrator because they once needed to create an environment, and makers are System Administrators in production because it was the quickest fix for a permissions error.
whenToUse: Setting up or reviewing platform administration
Preparing for an audit
Separating platform admins from app owners
whenNotToUse: Giving makers System Administrator in production to solve an access problem
Using Global Administrator for day-to-day platform work
formulaOrCode:
Tenant-level roles (Microsoft Entra ID)
  Global Administrator            everything in the tenant. Not needed for Power Platform work.
  Power Platform Administrator    all environments, DLP policies, tenant settings, capacity, licences view.
                                  Gets System Administrator in every environment without a security group check.
  Dynamics 365 Administrator      similar reach, but only environments whose security group they belong to
                                  (or that have none).
  Fabric Administrator            Power BI and Fabric settings. Separate from the above.
  Billing / Licence Administrator buy and assign licences. No environment access.

Environment-level roles (Dataverse security roles)
  System Administrator            full control of one environment, including users, roles and data.
  System Customizer               customise tables, forms and apps. Sees only own rows by default.
  Environment Maker               create apps, flows, connections and custom connectors. No data access.
  Basic User                      run apps and own-row access on standard tables.
  Delegated / custom roles        app-specific access for users.
  Environments without Dataverse have two roles only: Environment Admin and Environment Maker.

Who gets what
  Platform team (2-4 people)      Power Platform Administrator, eligible through PIM, activated when needed
  Environment owner of a project  System Administrator in THEIR Dev and Test. Not in Production.
  Makers                          Environment Maker + System Customizer in Dev
  Release pipeline                service principal as application user with System Administrator in targets
  Support                         a custom support role in Production with read access and specific fixes
  End users                       Basic User + the app's role, through a group team
  Break-glass                     two cloud-only Global Administrator accounts, monitored, not used daily

Just-in-time elevation
  Entra Privileged Identity Management:
    Roles > Power Platform Administrator > Add assignments > Eligible (not Active)
    Settings: activation up to 8 hours, require justification and MFA, optionally approval
    Activate: My roles > Activate > reason > the role applies within minutes
  Inside an environment: tenant admins can self-elevate to System Administrator when required
    Admin center > Environment > Membership > Add me
    This is logged. With it, admins do not need a standing System Administrator role everywhere.

Review commands
  Entra role holders:
    Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "RoleManagement.Read.Directory"
    Get-MgDirectoryRole | Where-Object DisplayName -in "Power Platform Administrator","Dynamics 365 Administrator","Global Administrator" |
      ForEach-Object { $r = $_; Get-MgDirectoryRoleMember -DirectoryRoleId $r.Id |
        Select-Object @{n='Role';e={$r.DisplayName}}, @{n='User';e={$_.AdditionalProperties.userPrincipalName}} }
  System Administrators in one environment (Web API):
    GET /api/data/v9.2/systemusers?$select=fullname,domainname&$filter=isdisabled eq false and
        systemuserroles_association/any(r:r/name eq 'System Administrator')

Rules of thumb
  No named person is a permanent System Administrator in Production.
  Admin accounts are separate from daily accounts where policy requires it.
  Every admin assignment has an owner and a review date.
stepByStepInstructions: List current holders of tenant and environment admin roles.
Map each person's actual duties to the smallest sufficient role.
Move tenant admin roles to eligible assignments with just-in-time activation.
Remove makers' System Administrator role from production.
Use a service principal for deployments.
Review role holders every quarter.
commonMistakes: Using Global Administrator for Power Platform tasks.
Leaving System Administrator on makers in production after go-live.
Assigning admin roles directly with no expiry or review.
No break-glass account plan.
troubleshooting: If an admin cannot see an environment, they hold Dynamics 365 Administrator and are outside its security group.
If an activated role does not seem to apply, sign out and in again, then wait a few minutes.
If support needs occasional production access, create a narrow custom role instead of System Administrator.
If nobody can administer an environment, a Power Platform Administrator can add themselves through Membership.
seoTitle: Assign Power Platform admin roles with least privilege
seoDescription: Which role does what, from tenant-level Power Platform Administrator down to Environment Maker, and how to grant admin access just in time instead of permanently.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Power Platform Administrator and System Administrator?
faqs.answer: Power Platform Administrator is a tenant-wide Entra role over all environments. System Administrator is a Dataverse role inside one environment.

faqs.question: Do I need Global Administrator to manage Power Platform?
faqs.answer: No. Power Platform Administrator covers environments, policies and tenant settings.

faqs.question: Can admin roles be temporary?
faqs.answer: Yes. With Privileged Identity Management, people are eligible for a role and activate it for a limited time when needed.

title: Find what is using Dataverse storage and reduce it
shortDescription: Read the capacity report, identify the tables that consume database, file and log storage, and clear them safely with bulk delete jobs and retention settings.
fullDescription: Dataverse capacity is split into database, file and log storage, pooled across the tenant. When it runs out, new environments cannot be created and admin operations such as copy and restore are blocked. Most overuse comes from a handful of system tables: audit logs, system jobs, email attachments and flow run history.
problemStatement: The admin center shows the tenant over its database capacity. Nobody knows which environment or table is responsible, and environment copies are now blocked.
whenToUse: Capacity warnings or overage in the admin center
Routine housekeeping of long-lived environments
Before buying more capacity
whenNotToUse: Deleting business data to save space without the owner's agreement
Bulk deleting audit data that a retention policy requires you to keep
formulaOrCode:
See the numbers
  Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Capacity add-ons / Dataverse > Summary
    Database, File, Log: used versus entitled, with the top environments
  Dataverse tab > select an environment > Details: usage by table, per storage type, with a trend chart
  Download all tables for a spreadsheet view.

Usual suspects and what to do
  Log storage
    AuditBase                 Admin center > Environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings >
                              retention period (for example 90 or 365 days), then
                              Audit log management > Delete logs (by table, by date, or all before a date)
    Plug-in trace log         Settings > Customization > set Plug-in trace log to Off when not debugging.
                              Bulk delete existing rows.
  Database storage
    AsyncOperationBase        completed system jobs. Bulk delete: System Jobs where Status Reason = Succeeded
                              and Completed On older than 30 days. Schedule it to recur daily.
    WorkflowLogBase           classic workflow history. Bulk delete Process Sessions older than 30 days.
    FlowRun (flow run history in Dataverse)   controlled by the flow run retention setting:
                              default 28 days. Lower it per environment through the Organization table's
                              FlowRunTimeToLiveInSeconds if you do not need 28 days.
    ActivityPointerBase, EmailBase   old emails and activities. Bulk delete by date and status after agreement.
    DuplicateRecordBase, ImportJob, BulkDeleteOperation   remove old jobs and their results.
    Your own tables           archive closed rows: export to a data lake or SharePoint, or use Dataverse
                              long term retention (retention policies move rows to cheaper storage).
  File storage
    Attachment / ActivityMimeAttachment   email attachments. Bulk delete emails with attachments over a size
                              and age, or move files to SharePoint or Azure Blob.
    Annotation (Notes)        notes with large files. Query: Notes where File Size (Bytes) > 1048576.
    WebResourceBase, RibbonClientMetadataBase   solution content. Remove unused solutions.
    Canvas app files, image and file columns   review large uploads.

Create a recurring bulk delete job
  Admin center > Environment > Settings > Data management > Bulk deletion > New
    Look for: System Jobs
    Status Reason equals Succeeded       Completed On older than X days: 30
    Name: Delete succeeded system jobs over 30 days
    Run this job after every: 1 day        Send an email when finished: optional
  One job per table. Review results under Bulk deletion > Completed.

Find large rows with a query (Web API)
  GET /api/data/v9.2/annotations?$select=subject,filename,filesize,createdon&$filter=filesize gt 5000000&$orderby=filesize desc&$top=50

Reduce environments
  Delete unused sandboxes and expired trials: each Dataverse environment uses at least 1 GB of database capacity.
  Developer and Teams environments are counted separately from the pooled entitlement.

After deleting
  Storage figures refresh within about 24 to 48 hours. Capacity is released after the platform's cleanup.

Monitor
  Monthly: export the capacity summary. Alert when any storage type passes 85 percent.
  Tenant settings can restrict environment creation to admins while capacity is tight.
stepByStepInstructions: Open the capacity summary and identify which storage type is over.
Open the heaviest environment and list its largest tables.
Set audit retention and delete old audit logs where policy allows.
Create recurring bulk delete jobs for system jobs and other housekeeping tables.
Agree archiving or deletion rules for large business tables with their owners.
Check the figures again after two days and schedule a monthly review.
commonMistakes: Buying capacity before removing system job and audit build-up.
Leaving plug-in trace logging on in production.
One-off clean-ups with no recurring job.
Deleting audit history required for compliance.
troubleshooting: If figures do not drop, wait for the report to refresh. It can lag by a day or two.
If a bulk delete job fails on some rows, check dependencies and the job's failure details.
If file storage stays high, look at attachments and notes, not database tables.
If log storage grows quickly, review which tables and columns are audited and whether read auditing is on.
seoTitle: Find what is using Dataverse storage and reduce it
seoDescription: Read the capacity report, identify the tables that consume database, file and log storage, and clear them safely with bulk delete jobs and retention settings.

faqs.question: How do I see what is using Dataverse storage?
faqs.answer: Open Capacity in the Power Platform admin center, select an environment and view usage by table for database, file and log storage.

faqs.question: How do I free up Dataverse database storage?
faqs.answer: Delete completed system jobs and old workflow history with recurring bulk delete jobs, then archive closed business rows.

faqs.question: How do I reduce log storage?
faqs.answer: Set an audit retention period, delete old audit logs and turn off plug-in trace logging.

title: Back up, restore and copy Power Platform environments
shortDescription: Use system and manual backups, restore to a point in time, and copy production to a sandbox for testing, with the clean-up steps that keep the copy from emailing real users.
fullDescription: Dataverse environments are backed up continuously by the platform. Admins can add labelled manual backups before risky changes, restore a sandbox to a moment in time, and copy one environment over another. A restored or copied environment starts in administration mode with flows off, and needs deliberate steps before it is used.
problemStatement: A bulk update goes wrong in production, or testers need realistic data, and nobody is sure what restore options exist or what a restored copy will do when its flows wake up.
whenToUse: Before a major release or data migration
Recovering from accidental data loss
Refreshing a test environment with production data
whenNotToUse: Using restore to undo a single record change, where audit history is quicker
Copying production data into environments with weaker access controls
formulaOrCode:
What is backed up automatically
  System backups: continuous. Production environments with Dataverse: restorable for 7 days by default.
    Managed Environments can extend retention up to 28 days:
    Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentBackupRetentionPeriod -EnvironmentName <id> -NewBackupRetentionPeriodInDays 28
  Sandbox and other types: 7 days.
  Not included: SharePoint data, flows' external systems, connections' credentials.

Manual backup (a named restore point)
  Admin center > Environments > select > Backups > Create
    Label: "Before 1.5.0.0 release 2026-11-20"        Notes: who and why
  Kept for the same retention period as system backups. It does not consume storage capacity.

Restore
  Environments > select > Backups > Restore or manage
    System: choose a date and time.   Manual: choose the labelled backup.
    Target: a SANDBOX environment. The target is overwritten.
  Production cannot be restored over directly. To recover production:
    Option A (preferred): restore to a sandbox, then extract and re-import the lost data.
    Option B: change Production to Sandbox type (Edit > Type), restore over it, switch the type back.
  Requires 1 GB of spare capacity and that the tenant is not over capacity.

Copy
  Environments > select the source > Copy
    Copy over: Everything (data, users, customisations) | Customizations and schemas only
    Select tables: with "Everything" you can pick a subset of tables where offered
    Target: a sandbox in the same region. It is overwritten.
    Edit details: name, URL, security group. Audit logs: copying them is optional.

State of a restored or copied environment
  Administration mode: On             only System Administrators and Customizers can sign in
  Background operations: Off          no flows, workflows, async plug-ins, server-side sync
  Cloud flows: turned off             they stay off until someone turns them on
  Connection references keep their links, but connections may need re-authentication.
  Environment variables' current values are those of the source: they still point at PRODUCTION systems.

Checklist before letting users in (copy of production to test)
  1. Environment variables: change values to test endpoints, test SharePoint sites and test mailboxes.
  2. Connection references: point at test connections.
  3. Flows: review each before turning it on. Leave outbound notification flows off, or route to a test address.
  4. Email: Settings > Email > Mailboxes: disable or re-point server-side synchronisation.
  5. Integrations: disable service endpoints, webhooks and plug-in steps that call live systems.
  6. Data: mask or delete personal data if testers should not see it (bulk update, or copy schema only and
     load sample data).
  7. Security group and roles: confirm only testers have access.
  8. Turn off administration mode: Environments > select > Edit > Administration mode.

Deleted environments
  Environments > Recover deleted environments: available for a limited period after deletion (7 days by default).

Environments without Dataverse
  No backup or restore. Export apps and flows as packages or use solutions with source control.

Good practice
  Manual backup before every production release. A restore drill once a year into a sandbox.
  Source control for solutions: a backup restores data and customisations together, but Git tells you what changed.
stepByStepInstructions: Take a labelled manual backup before any risky production change.
Decide whether you need a restore to a point in time or a copy of the current state.
Restore or copy into a sandbox target.
Re-point environment variables, connections and integrations away from production.
Review flows and mailboxes before enabling background operations.
Turn off administration mode and confirm access is limited to the right people.
commonMistakes: Turning flows on in a copy that still points at production systems.
Expecting to restore directly over production.
Assuming backups cover SharePoint or other connected data.
Copying personal data into a broadly accessible test environment.
troubleshooting: If restore is unavailable, the tenant is over capacity or the target is a production type.
If users cannot sign in after a copy, administration mode is still on.
If emails went out from the copy, disable mailboxes and notification flows before disabling admin mode next time.
If the backup you need has expired, check whether a longer retention on Managed Environments is appropriate.
seoTitle: Back up, restore and copy Power Platform environments
seoDescription: Use system and manual backups, restore to a point in time, and copy production to a sandbox for testing, with the clean-up steps that keep the copy from emailing real users.

faqs.question: How long are Power Platform backups kept?
faqs.answer: System backups are kept for 7 days. Managed production environments can extend this to as much as 28 days.

faqs.question: Can I restore a production environment?
faqs.answer: Restore targets must be sandboxes. Restore to a sandbox and recover the data, or temporarily change the environment type.

faqs.question: What happens to flows when I copy an environment?
faqs.answer: They are turned off in the copy, and the environment starts in administration mode with background operations disabled.

title: Welcome new makers automatically with an admin flow
shortDescription: A scheduled flow that finds people who created their first app or flow, sends them the rules and resources, and records them in a makers list.
fullDescription: Most makers never read a governance site before building. The moment after their first app is the best time to reach them. A daily flow using the admin connectors lists new apps and flows, works out who is new, and sends a short welcome with the things they need to know: where to build, what is blocked, and how to get help.
problemStatement: Makers discover the DLP policy only when a flow is suspended, and discover the support channel only after an app has become critical.
whenToUse: Tenants with a steady stream of new makers
Sharing governance rules at the right moment
Building a makers contact list without the full CoE Starter Kit
whenNotToUse: Tenants already running the CoE Starter Kit's welcome email, which does the same
Long emails that read as a policy document
formulaOrCode:
Lists
  Makers (SharePoint or Dataverse): Title (email), DisplayName, FirstSeen (date), FirstItemType, FirstItemName,
          Environment, WelcomeSent (yes/no)

Flow: Welcome new makers
  Trigger: Recurrence, daily 07:00
  Run as: a service account with the Power Platform Administrator role (admin connectors return all environments)

  1. Power Platform for Admins > List Environments as Admin
  2. Apply to each environment (concurrency 5)
       Power Apps for Admins > Get Apps as Admin        Environment: current
       Filter array: createdTime ge addDays(utcNow(), -1)
         @greaterOrEquals(item()?['properties/createdTime'], addDays(utcNow(), -1))
       Append to varNew (array) for each:
         { "email": properties/owner/email, "name": properties/owner/displayName, "type": "app",
           "item": properties/displayName, "env": environment display name }
       Power Automate Management > List Flows as Admin   Environment: current
       Filter array on properties/createdTime the same way. The creator is properties/creator/userId (object id):
         Office 365 Users > Get user profile (V2) with that id for email and name. Append with type "flow".
  3. Distinct makers
       Select: email from varNew > union(body('Select'), body('Select'))
  4. Apply to each distinct email
       Get items: Makers, Filter Query: Title eq '<email>', Top 1
       Condition: length(...) equals 0
         Yes: Create item in Makers (FirstSeen = utcNow(), details from the first matching entry)
              Send an email (V2) from a shared mailbox, then Update item WelcomeSent = Yes
         No:  skip

Email (short, with links)
  Subject: Welcome to Power Platform at Contoso
  Hi @{name},
  You created your first @{type}, "@{item}". A few things worth knowing:
    Where to build: personal ideas in your Developer environment. Team solutions: request a project environment.
    Connectors: the default environment allows Microsoft 365 connectors. Others need a project environment.
    Sharing: apps shared with more than 20 people need a named backup owner.
    Help: Teams channel "Power Platform Makers", office hours Thursdays 14:00.
    Training: three short modules to start with.
  Reply to this message if you need anything.

Alternative trigger without polling
  Office 365 Management Activity (audit log) events for CreatePowerApp and CreateFlow, through a custom
  connector or Microsoft Sentinel. More timely, more set-up.

Extras
  Add new makers to the Makers Teams team:  Office 365 Groups > Add member to group
  Monthly: count of new makers by department (Get user profile > department) for the governance report.
  Guest makers: flag accounts whose email contains #EXT# for review.

Licensing and limits
  Admin connectors are standard connectors. Each "as Admin" call pages results: turn on Pagination
  (threshold 5000) on Get Apps as Admin and List Flows as Admin in large environments.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a Makers list to record who has been welcomed.
Build a daily flow under an admin service account that lists apps and flows created in the last day.
Resolve each creator to an email address and remove duplicates.
Check each against the Makers list and add those who are new.
Send a short welcome email from a shared mailbox.
Review the Makers list monthly for trends and follow-up.
