stepByStepInstructions: Choose a small set of specific keywords and the channels to watch.
Add the keyword trigger and fetch the message details.
Filter out bot posts, replies you made and duplicates.
Create a tracked item with the text, author and message link.
Reply in the thread with the reference.
Alert the on-call person for high-priority matches.
commonMistakes: Common keywords that match half the channel's messages.
The flow's own reply containing a keyword and re-triggering it.
No duplicate check on message ID.
Watching chats without the participants knowing.
troubleshooting: If the flow triggers itself, exclude messages from the bot or remove keywords from the reply text.
If the message text is empty, call Get message details with the IDs from the trigger.
If nothing triggers, confirm the connection's user is a member of the team and channel.
If it fires late, the trigger polls on an interval. Use a reaction or message action for immediacy.
seoTitle: Start a flow when a keyword is mentioned in a Teams channel
seoDescription: Watch channels for words such as urgent or outage, fetch the full message and act on it by creating a ticket or alerting an on-call group.

faqs.question: Can Power Automate react to words in a Teams message?
faqs.answer: Yes. The When keywords are mentioned trigger starts a flow for channel or group chat messages containing your keywords.

faqs.question: Does the trigger include the message text?
faqs.answer: It returns IDs and a link. Use Get message details to read the content and author.

faqs.question: How do I stop the flow replying to itself?
faqs.answer: Exclude messages posted by the Flow bot and keep keywords out of the reply.

title: Turn a Teams message into a task with a message action flow
shortDescription: Add a flow to the message menu in Teams that asks for a few details with a card, then creates a Planner task or list item linked to the original message.
fullDescription: The trigger 'For a selected message' puts a flow in the More actions menu of any Teams message. The person running it can be shown an Adaptive Card to add details. The flow receives the message, its author and a link, which makes it a quick route from conversation to tracked work.
problemStatement: Action items agreed in a chat are lost in the scroll, because moving them into the task tool means copying text and switching apps.
whenToUse: Capturing tasks, decisions or issues from conversations
Any follow-up that starts from a specific message
Teams that plan work in Planner or a list
whenNotToUse: Processes that should start automatically without a person choosing a message
Flows that need to appear for users who have never been given run access
formulaOrCode: Trigger Microsoft Teams > For a selected message (V2) Adaptive Card (optional): Create adaptive card > designer opens. Example card: { "type": "AdaptiveCard", "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json", "version": "1.4", "body": [ { "type": "Input.Text", "id": "taskTitle", "label": "Task title", "isRequired": true, "errorMessage": "Enter a title" }, { "type": "Input.Date", "id": "dueDate", "label": "Due date" }, { "type": "Input.ChoiceSet", "id": "bucket", "label": "Bucket", "value": "backlog", "choices": [ { "title": "Backlog", "value": "backlog" }, { "title": "This week", "value": "week" } ] }, { "type": "Input.Toggle", "id": "assignToMe", "title": "Assign to me", "value": "true" } ], "actions": [ { "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Create task" } ] } Trigger outputs triggerBody()?['entity/cardOutputs/taskTitle'], ['entity/cardOutputs/dueDate'], ['entity/cardOutputs/bucket'] triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/messagePayload/body/plainText'] the selected message as text triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/messagePayload/body/content'] HTML triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/messagePayload/from/user/displayName'] original author triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/messagePayload/linkToMessage'] deep link triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/from/aadObjectId'] who ran the flow triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/channelData/team/aadGroupId'] team (empty in chats) The designer lists these as dynamic content: "Message plain text", "Link to message", "Originating user". Create the task Planner > Create a task Group Id / Plan Id: your plan Title: @{triggerBody()?['entity/cardOutputs/taskTitle']} Bucket Id: @{if(equals(triggerBody()?['entity/cardOutputs/bucket'],'week'),'','')} Due Date Time: @{triggerBody()?['entity/cardOutputs/dueDate']} Assigned User Ids: @{if(equals(triggerBody()?['entity/cardOutputs/assignToMe'],'true'), triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/from/aadObjectId'], '')} Planner > Update task details Description: From @{...from/user/displayName}: @{take(...plainText, 800)} References: Resource link = linkToMessage, Alias = "Teams message", Type = Other Confirm to the person Microsoft Teams > Post message in a chat or channel Post as: Flow bot Post in: Chat with Flow bot Recipient: the user who ran it (Get user profile by object ID) Message: Task created: @{title} Or reply under the original message when it is in a channel: Reply with a message in a channel, Message ID = triggerBody()?['entity/teamsFlowRunContext/messagePayload/id'] Where it appears Hover a message > ... More actions > the flow's name (first use may sit under "More actions > See more"). The flow shows for its owners and for users it is shared with as run-only users. It must be in the default environment for the standard Teams menu. Share it with the team Flow details > Run only users > add the team's Microsoft 365 group. Connections used: "Provided by run-only user" for Planner so tasks are created as the person, or use the owner's connection so everything is created by one account. Name it for the menu The flow name is the menu label: "Create task from message" reads better than "Flow 12".
stepByStepInstructions: Create a flow with the For a selected message trigger.
Design a short Adaptive Card for the extra details.
Create the task or list item using the card answers and the message text.
Attach the link to the original message.
Confirm to the person who ran it.
Share the flow with the team as run-only users and give it a clear name.
commonMistakes: Building it outside the default environment and not finding it in the menu.
Not sharing it as run-only, so only the owner can see it.
Copying the HTML content into a plain-text field.
A vague flow name in the message menu.
troubleshooting: If the flow is missing from the menu, check the environment and run-only sharing, then restart Teams.
If card values are empty, compare input IDs with the cardOutputs property names.
If assignment fails, pass the user's object ID, not an email address.
If the team ID is empty, the message was in a chat. Branch on that.
seoTitle: Turn a Teams message into a task with a message action flow
seoDescription: Add a flow to the message menu in Teams that asks for a few details with a card, then creates a Planner task or list item linked to the original message.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate for a selected message Teams

faqs.question: How do I run a flow on a specific Teams message?
faqs.answer: Use the For a selected message trigger. The flow then appears under More actions on messages.

faqs.question: Can the flow ask the user questions first?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add an Adaptive Card to the trigger and read the answers from cardOutputs.

faqs.question: Why can't my colleagues see the flow in Teams?
faqs.answer: Share it with them as run-only users and make sure it lives in the default environment.

title: Create a Teams group chat from a flow and post into it
shortDescription: Open a one-to-one or group chat for the people involved in a record, give it a title, post the context and keep the chat ID for later updates.
fullDescription: Some events need the right three people talking, not another channel post. The Teams connector can create a chat with chosen members, name it, and post messages or cards into it. Storing the chat ID on the record lets later flows post updates into the same conversation.
problemStatement: A high-priority incident needs the requester, the engineer and the service owner in one conversation, and someone has to create the chat and paste in the details by hand each time.
whenToUse: Incident or escalation swarms with a few named people
Handover conversations tied to a record
Follow-ups that should stay in one thread
whenNotToUse: Broad announcements, which belong in a channel
Adding people outside the organisation without checking external access policy
formulaOrCode:
1. Create the chat Microsoft Teams > Create a chat Title: INC-@{triggerOutputs()?['body/ID']} @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Title']} (titles apply to group chats) Members to add: semicolon-separated UPNs or object IDs @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Author/Email']};@{triggerOutputs()?['body/AssignedTo/Email']};@{outputs('Get_owner')?['body/mail']} The connection's user is added automatically. Two members total = one-to-one chat (no title). Output: body('Create_a_chat')?['id'] for example 19:abc123...@thread.v2 2. Save the chat ID on the record SharePoint > Update item: TeamsChatId = body('Create_a_chat')?['id'] Later runs check it first: if not empty, reuse instead of creating another chat. 3. Post the context Microsoft Teams > Post message in a chat or channel Post as: User (the connection account) or Flow bot Post in: Group chat Group chat: body('Create_a_chat')?['id'] (enter as custom value) Message:

@{triggerOutputs()?['body/Title']}

Priority: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Priority/Value']}
Reported: @{convertFromUtc(triggerOutputs()?['body/Created'],'Eastern Standard Time','dd MMM HH:mm')}

Open the incident

Or Post card in a chat or channel with an Adaptive Card and the same chat ID. 4. Later updates into the same chat (another flow, on status change) Condition: TeamsChatId is not empty Post message in a chat or channel > Group chat > TeamsChatId Message: Status changed to @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Status/Value']} by @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Editor/DisplayName']} 5. Add someone later Microsoft Teams > Add a member to a chat (where available), or Graph: Send a Microsoft Graph HTTP request POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/chats/@{chatId}/members { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.aadUserConversationMember", "roles": ["owner"], "user@odata.bind": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users('
stepByStepInstructions: Collect the participants' email addresses or object IDs from the record.
Create the chat with a meaningful title.
Store the returned chat ID on the record.
Post the summary and a link to the record in the chat.
Have later flows reuse the stored chat ID for updates.
Use a service account connection for creation and posting.
commonMistakes: Creating a new chat on every update.
Not storing the chat ID.
Using a personal connection so messages appear to come from an individual.
Including external users without checking policy.
troubleshooting: If the chat is created without a title, there were only two members. Titles need a group chat.
If posting fails, enter the chat ID as a custom value and confirm the poster is a member.
If a member is missing, their address was blank or malformed in the semicolon list.
If duplicates appear, check the stored chat ID before the create action.
seoTitle: Create a Teams group chat from a flow and post into it
seoDescription: Open a one-to-one or group chat for the people involved in a record, give it a title, post the context and keep the chat ID for later updates.

faqs.question: Can Power Automate create a Teams group chat?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Create a chat action takes a title and a list of members and returns the chat ID.

faqs.question: How do I post to the same chat later?
faqs.answer: Save the chat ID on the record when the chat is created and use it in later post actions.

faqs.question: Can the Flow bot post in a group chat?
faqs.answer: In many cases yes. Posting as the connection's user is the dependable option when that user is a member.

title: Mention a tag, a channel or a whole team from a flow
shortDescription: Notify the right group without listing people: post a message that @mentions a Teams tag, the channel or the team using the connector or Microsoft Graph.
fullDescription: Mentioning individuals from a flow is straightforward with the user mention token. Notifying a group such as the on-call tag or everyone in a channel needs a different approach: the tag mention token action, or a Graph request with a mentions array. Used sparingly, it gets attention without building recipient lists.
problemStatement: An alert must reach whoever is on call this week. The flow hard-codes three names, and nobody remembers to change them when the rota changes.
whenToUse: Alerts for a rota or role managed as a Teams tag
Announcements that should notify a channel
Avoiding hard-coded recipient lists
whenNotToUse: Routine posts, where team-wide mentions quickly get muted
Private channels with the Flow bot, which cannot post there
formulaOrCode: A. Mention a tag (connector) Microsoft Teams > List all tags for a team Team: IT Support Filter array: displayName equals 'OnCall' > first(body('Filter_array'))?['id'] Microsoft Teams > Get an @mention token for a tag Team: IT Support Tag: the tag id Microsoft Teams > Post message in a chat or channel Post as: User (tag mentions require posting as a user, not the Flow bot) Post in: Channel Team: IT Support Channel: Alerts Message: @{outputs('Get_an_@mention_token_for_a_tag')?['body/atMention']} Database CPU above 90% for 10 minutes. Open dashboard B. Mention a person (for reference) Get an @mention token for a user: User = email > body/atMention in the message. Works as Flow bot or User. C. Mention the channel or the team (Microsoft Graph) Microsoft Teams > Send a Microsoft Graph HTTP request URI: https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/teams/@{teamId}/channels/@{channelId}/messages Method: POST Body: { "body": { "contentType": "html", "content": "Alerts Planned maintenance tonight 22:00 to 23:00." }, "mentions": [ { "id": 0, "mentionText": "Alerts", "mentioned": { "conversation": { "id": "@{channelId}", "displayName": "Alerts", "conversationIdentityType": "channel" } } } ] } Whole team: "id": "@{teamId}", "conversationIdentityType": "team", and mentionText = the team name. Tag through Graph: "mentioned": { "tag": { "id": "", "displayName": "OnCall" } } Several mentions: number them 0, 1, 2 in both the elements and the mentions array. Graph posts as the connection's user. Find IDs Team ID (group ID) and channel ID: channel > ... > Get link to channel: .../channel/19%3Aabc...%40thread.tacv2/Alerts?groupId= (URL-decode the channel part) Or List teams / List channels actions. Manage the rota as a tag Teams > team > ... > Manage tags > OnCall: members updated weekly by the team owner. Automate with Graph: POST /teams/{id}/tags/{tagId}/members { "userId": "
stepByStepInstructions: Create and maintain a Teams tag for the role or rota.
Look up the tag's ID in the flow.
Get the mention token for the tag and include it in the message.
Post as a user account that belongs to the team.
Use a Graph request with a mentions array for channel or team mentions.
Limit broad mentions to events that justify them.
commonMistakes: Hard-coding people instead of a tag.
Trying to post a tag mention as the Flow bot.
Mismatched ids between the at element and the mentions array.
Overusing team mentions until members mute the channel.
troubleshooting: If the mention shows as plain text, the token was not used or the mentions array does not match the at id.
If the tag action finds nothing, check the tag exists in that team and the name matches.
If the Graph request is forbidden, the connection's user is not a member of the team.
If nobody is notified, mentions may be disabled in the team's settings.
seoTitle: Mention a tag, a channel or a whole team from a flow
seoDescription: Notify the right group without listing people: post a message that @mentions a Teams tag, the channel or the team using the connector or Microsoft Graph.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate mention team tag channel

faqs.question: Can Power Automate @mention a Teams tag?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use Get an @mention token for a tag and post the message as a user.

faqs.question: How do I mention a whole channel or team from a flow?
faqs.answer: Send a Microsoft Graph request to post the message with a mentions entry whose conversation type is channel or team.

faqs.question: Why does my mention appear as text?
faqs.answer: The message must contain the mention token or a matching at element and mentions array, not just the name.

title: Provision a Team with standard channels from a request
shortDescription: Create a team from an approved request with consistent naming, owners, channels and a pinned tab, using the Teams connector and Microsoft Graph.
fullDescription: Self-service team creation produces inconsistent names and ownerless teams. A provisioning flow takes a request, checks it, creates the team with two owners, adds the standard channels and records the result. Every project or client team then starts with the same structure.
problemStatement: Project teams are created by whoever gets there first, with names nobody can search for, one owner and a different set of channels each time.
whenToUse: Project, client or department teams with a standard layout
Organisations that restrict who can create Microsoft 365 groups
Tracking teams with owners and review dates
whenNotToUse: One-off teams where a template in the Teams client is enough
Creating a team for every small topic, where a channel would do
formulaOrCode:
Request list: Team Requests
  Title (project name), Purpose, Owner1 (person), Owner2 (person), Members (multi-person), Privacy (Private | Public),
  Template (Project | Client), Status, TeamId, TeamUrl

Flow
  Trigger: When an item is created > approval by the collaboration team (optional) > Status Approved

  1. Name
     Compose TeamName: PRJ - @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Title']}
     Compose MailNickname: prj-@{toLower(replace(replace(triggerOutputs()?['body/Title'],' ','-'),'&',''))}
     Check for an existing group: Office 365 Groups > List groups, filter mailNickname eq '<nickname>'. Stop if found.

  2. Create the team
     Microsoft Teams > Create a team
       Team Name: TeamName        Description: Purpose        Visibility: Privacy
     Output: body('Create_a_team')?['newTeamId']
     The connection's account becomes an owner. Use a service account.

  3. Wait for provisioning
     Delay 30 seconds, then Do until Get a team succeeds (limit 10, 15 seconds apart). Channel and member
     calls fail if made too early.

  4. Owners and members
     Microsoft Teams > Add a member to a team: Team = newTeamId, User = Owner1 email, Set as team owner: Yes
     Repeat for Owner2. Apply to each Members: Add a member to a team (owner: No).
     Optionally remove the service account as owner afterwards (Graph DELETE /groups/{id}/owners/{id}/$ref)
     once two owners exist.

  5. Standard channels (array per template)
     Project: ["Planning","Delivery","Risks and Issues","Status Reports"]
     Apply to each: Microsoft Teams > Create a channel
       Team: newTeamId        Display Name: current item        Description: optional
     Private or shared channel through Graph:
       POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/teams/@{teamId}/channels
       { "displayName": "Commercial", "membershipType": "private",
         "members": [ { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.aadUserConversationMember", "roles": ["owner"],
                        "user@odata.bind": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users('<owner object id>')" } ] }

  6. Pin a website tab in General
     Send a Microsoft Graph HTTP request
       POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/teams/@{teamId}/channels/@{generalChannelId}/tabs
       { "displayName": "Project site",
         "teamsApp@odata.bind": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/appCatalogs/teamsApps/com.microsoft.teamspace.tab.web",
         "configuration": { "contentUrl": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/pmo/project/@{ID}",
                            "websiteUrl": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/pmo/project/@{ID}" } }
     General channel ID: List channels, filter displayName eq 'General'.

  7. Welcome post
     Post message in a chat or channel > Channel > General:
       Welcome. Planning holds the schedule, Risks and Issues holds the log. Owners: Owner1 and Owner2.

  8. Record
     Update the request: Status Ready, TeamId, TeamUrl
       https://teams.microsoft.com/l/team/@{encodeUriComponent(generalChannelId)}/conversations?groupId=@{teamId}&tenantId=<tenant id>
     Email the owners with the link and their responsibilities.

Alternative: create from a template in one call
  POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/teams
  { "template@odata.bind": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/teamsTemplates('standard')",
    "displayName": "PRJ - Apollo", "description": "…", "visibility": "Private",
    "channels": [ { "displayName": "Planning", "isFavoriteByDefault": true }, { "displayName": "Delivery" } ],
    "members": [ { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.aadUserConversationMember", "roles": ["owner"],
                   "user@odata.bind": "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users('<owner id>')" } ] }
  Returns 202 with a Location header to poll. Needs application or delegated Team.Create permission.

Governance to pair with it
  Restrict Microsoft 365 group creation to a security group that includes the service account.
  Group naming policy and expiration policy in Entra. Sensitivity labels for privacy and guest settings.
  Quarterly: teams with one owner or no activity are reported to the owners.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a request list with name, purpose, two owners and a template choice.
Build the name to your standard and check it does not already exist.
Create the team with a service account and wait for provisioning to finish.
Add both owners and the members.
Create the standard channels and pin key tabs.
Post a welcome message, record the team ID and notify the owners.
commonMistakes: Adding channels or members before the team has finished provisioning.
One owner only.
Leaving the service account as the only owner.
No duplicate name check.
troubleshooting: If channel creation fails with not found, increase the wait after creating the team.
If members are not added, the team is still provisioning or the user address is wrong.
If the tab call fails, check the General channel ID and that the app ID is the website tab.
If creation is forbidden, the service account is not allowed to create Microsoft 365 groups.
seoTitle: Provision a Team with standard channels from a request
seoDescription: Create a team from an approved request with consistent naming, owners, channels and a pinned tab, using the Teams connector and Microsoft Graph.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate create Team channels provisioning

faqs.question: Can Power Automate create a Microsoft Teams team?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Teams connector has Create a team, Create a channel and Add a member to a team actions.

faqs.question: Why do actions fail right after creating a team?
faqs.answer: Provisioning takes time. Wait and retry before adding channels, members or tabs.

faqs.question: How do I create private channels from a flow?
faqs.answer: Use a Microsoft Graph request to the channels endpoint with membershipType private and at least one owner.

title: Keep updates in one Teams thread by replying to the original post
shortDescription: Post once when a record is created, store the message ID, and send every later update as a reply so the channel shows one thread per record.
fullDescription: A flow that posts a new channel message for every status change buries the channel. Posting one root message per record and replying to it for each update keeps the history together and lets people follow or mute a single thread. The only requirement is saving the root message ID on the record.
problemStatement: A request generates six separate channel posts over its life. Readers cannot tell which posts belong together, and the channel becomes noise.
whenToUse: Records with several status updates over time
Incident and request channels
Any notification flow that posts more than once per item
whenNotToUse: One-off announcements with no follow-ups
Chats, where replies are not threaded the same way as channels
formulaOrCode:
Columns on the record TeamsMessageId (single line of text) TeamsThreadLink (hyperlink or text, optional) Flow A: on create, post the root message Trigger: SharePoint > When an item is created Microsoft Teams > Post message in a chat or channel Post as: Flow bot Post in: Channel Team: Operations Channel: Requests Subject: REQ-@{triggerOutputs()?['body/ID']} @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Title']} Message:

New request from @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Author/DisplayName']}

Open request

SharePoint > Update item TeamsMessageId: @{outputs('Post_message_in_a_chat_or_channel')?['body/id']} TeamsThreadLink: @{outputs('Post_message_in_a_chat_or_channel')?['body/messageLink']} (Posting a card instead: Post card in a chat or channel returns the same id property.) Flow B: on change, reply in the thread Trigger: SharePoint > When an item is created or modified Trigger condition so it runs only for real status changes, for example with a LastNotifiedStatus column: @not(equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/Status/Value'], triggerOutputs()?['body/LastNotifiedStatus'])) Condition: TeamsMessageId is not empty Yes: Microsoft Teams > Reply with a message in a channel Post as: Flow bot Post in: Channel Team / Channel: same as Flow A Message ID: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/TeamsMessageId']} Reply: Status changed to @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Status/Value']} by @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Editor/DisplayName']} (Card reply: Reply with an adaptive card in a channel, same Message ID.) No: Post a new root message and store its ID, as in Flow A. Update item: LastNotifiedStatus = current status Mention someone in the reply Get an @mention token for a user (assignee email) > include body/atMention in the reply text. When the root message was deleted The reply action fails with NotFound. Configure run after "has failed" on a fallback that posts a new root message and overwrites TeamsMessageId. Avoid the update loop Flow A's Update item triggers Flow B. The trigger condition on LastNotifiedStatus stops that run early. Alternatively have Flow A set LastNotifiedStatus in the same update. Graph alternative POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/teams/{teamId}/channels/{channelId}/messages/{messageId}/replies { "body": { "contentType": "html", "content": "Status changed to Approved" } } Tips Use the Subject field on the root message: it becomes the bold thread title and is searchable. Keep the first line of each reply self-contained, because the collapsed thread shows only the latest replies. The same identity should post root and replies, so the thread reads consistently.
stepByStepInstructions: Add a column to store the Teams message ID on the record.
Post one root message when the record is created and save its ID.
Trigger later updates only on meaningful changes.
Reply to the stored message ID with each update.
Fall back to a new root message when the ID is missing or the original was deleted.
Use the subject line so each thread has a clear title.
commonMistakes: Posting a new root message for every change.
Not saving the message ID.
Triggering on every edit, including the flow's own update.
Replying in a different team or channel than the root message.
troubleshooting: If the reply fails, confirm team, channel and message ID match the original post.
If the stored ID is blank, read body/id from the post action's output.
If the flow loops, add a trigger condition or a last-notified column.
If replies appear as new posts, you used the post action instead of the reply action.
seoTitle: Keep updates in one Teams thread by replying to the original post
seoDescription: Post once when a record is created, store the message ID, and send every later update as a reply so the channel shows one thread per record.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate reply to Teams channel message

faqs.question: How do I reply to a Teams channel message from Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use Reply with a message in a channel and pass the message ID of the original post.

faqs.question: Where does the message ID come from?
faqs.answer: From the output of the action that posted the original message. Save it on the record.

faqs.question: Can the reply contain an Adaptive Card?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use Reply with an adaptive card in a channel with the same message ID.

title: Make a canvas app fit Teams with context and theme
shortDescription: Read the Teams theme, team and channel a canvas app is running in, match dark mode, and filter data to the current channel.
fullDescription: A canvas app added as a Teams tab can tell where it is running. Apps built in Teams use the Teams integration object. Apps built in the standard maker portal receive context through query parameters. Either way the app can match the user's theme and scope its data to the team or channel, which makes one app reusable across many teams.
problemStatement: An app pinned as a tab stays bright white when Teams is in dark mode, and shows every team's records instead of the ones for the channel it is pinned in.
whenToUse: Apps pinned as channel or personal tabs
One app reused across several teams
Matching Teams light, dark and high-contrast themes
whenNotToUse: Security decisions based on context values, which a user can alter
Apps that are mainly used in the browser outside Teams
formulaOrCode:
A. Apps created in Teams (Dataverse for Teams) or with the Teams integration object
  Teams.ThisTeam.DisplayName      Teams.ThisTeam.GroupId
  Teams.ThisChannel.DisplayName   Teams.ThisChannel.Id
  Teams.Theme.Name                "default" | "dark" | "contrast"
  Teams.Locale                    for example "en-us"
  Example:  Filter(Tasks, 'Channel Id' = Teams.ThisChannel.Id)

B. Standard canvas apps added to Teams (Add to Teams, or a Website/Power Apps tab)
  Context arrives as parameters. Read them with Param():
    Param("theme")          default | dark | contrast
    Param("groupId")        Microsoft 365 group ID of the team
    Param("channelId")      19:...@thread.tacv2
    Param("teamId")         thread ID of the team
    Param("channelType")    Regular | Private | Shared
    Param("hostClientType") desktop | web | android | ios
    Param("subEntityId")    value from a deep link
    Param("locale"), Param("entityId"), Param("chatId"), Param("userTeamRole")
  Outside Teams these return blank.

  App.Formulas (named formulas)
    nfInTeams   = !IsBlank(Param("hostClientType")) || !IsBlank(Param("theme"));
    nfTheme     = Coalesce(Param("theme"), "default");
    nfGroupId   = Param("groupId");
    nfChannelId = Param("channelId");
    nfIsMobile  = Param("hostClientType") in ["android", "ios"];

C. Theme colours
  App.Formulas
    nfColors = Switch(nfTheme,
        "dark",     { Bg: ColorValue("#1F1F1F"), Surface: ColorValue("#292929"), Text: ColorValue("#FFFFFF"),
                      Subtle: ColorValue("#ADADAD"), Accent: ColorValue("#7F85F5"), Border: ColorValue("#3D3D3D") },
        "contrast", { Bg: Color.Black, Surface: Color.Black, Text: Color.White,
                      Subtle: Color.White, Accent: ColorValue("#FFFF01"), Border: Color.White },
                    { Bg: ColorValue("#F5F5F5"), Surface: Color.White, Text: ColorValue("#242424"),
                      Subtle: ColorValue("#616161"), Accent: ColorValue("#5B5FC7"), Border: ColorValue("#E0E0E0") });
  Use them:
    Screen.Fill = nfColors.Bg          Label.Color = nfColors.Text        Card container Fill = nfColors.Surface
    Button.Fill = nfColors.Accent      Borders = nfColors.Border
  The theme parameter is read at launch. If the user switches theme, the tab reloads with the new value.

D. Scope data to the channel
  Gallery.Items:
    Filter(Requests, IsBlank(nfChannelId) || ChannelId = nfChannelId)
  On create:
    Patch(Requests, Defaults(Requests), { Title: txtTitle.Text, ChannelId: nfChannelId, GroupId: nfGroupId })
  Show where you are:
    If(nfInTeams, "Requests for this channel", "All requests")
  Treat this as a convenience filter. Enforce access with SharePoint or Dataverse permissions.

E. Deep link to a record inside the tab
  Link: https://teams.microsoft.com/l/entity/<appId>/<entityId>?context={"subEntityId":"REQ-1042"}
  App.StartScreen: If(!IsBlank(Param("subEntityId")), scrDetail, scrHome)
  scrDetail.OnVisible: Set(gblRecord, LookUp(Requests, RequestNumber = Param("subEntityId")))

F. Layout inside Teams
  App settings > Display > Scale to fit: Off, Lock aspect ratio: Off. Use containers so the tab fills the width.
  Teams adds its own header: keep your app header short (40 to 48 px) or hide it when nfInTeams.
  Mobile Teams: check nfIsMobile for a single-column layout, or rely on App.Width breakpoints.

G. Add the app to Teams
  make.powerapps.com > Apps > select > Add to Teams > Add to a team > choose channel > Save.
  Or download the app package and publish to the organisation's app catalogue with a setup policy to pin it.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide whether the app uses the Teams integration object or query parameters.
Define named formulas for theme, group and channel.
Create a colour record per theme and bind fills and text colours to it.
Filter and stamp data with the channel or group ID.
Handle deep links through the sub-entity parameter.
Test in light, dark and high-contrast themes on desktop and mobile.
commonMistakes: Hard-coded white backgrounds in dark mode.
Assuming context values exist when the app runs in a browser.
Using the channel filter as a security boundary.
A fixed-size layout that leaves bars around the app in the tab.
troubleshooting: If Param values are blank, the app was opened outside Teams or as a website tab that does not pass context.
If colours do not change, check the named formula falls back to default when the parameter is blank.
If a private channel shows no data, its channel ID differs from the parent team. Store and filter by channel ID.
If the app looks cramped, turn off Scale to fit and use responsive containers.
seoTitle: Make a canvas app fit Teams with context and theme
seoDescription: Read the Teams theme, team and channel a canvas app is running in, match dark mode, and filter data to the current channel.
primaryKeyword: Power Apps Teams context theme Param

faqs.question: How does a canvas app know it is running in Teams?
faqs.answer: It receives parameters such as theme, groupId and channelId that can be read with Param, or it can use the Teams integration object.

faqs.question: How do I support Teams dark mode in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Read the theme value and bind fills and text colours to a set of colours for default, dark and contrast.

faqs.question: Can one app show different data in each channel?
faqs.answer: Yes. Store the channel ID on each record and filter by the current channel.

title: Schedule a Teams meeting from a flow
shortDescription: Create a Teams meeting with attendees and an agenda when a record reaches a stage, store the join link, and update or cancel it when details change.
fullDescription: Review meetings, kick-offs and interviews follow a record's progress. The Teams connector's Create a Teams meeting action places an event on a calendar with an online meeting link and invites attendees. Saving the event ID and join link on the record lets the flow reschedule or cancel later.
problemStatement: Each approved project needs a kick-off meeting. A coordinator creates every invite by hand, copying attendees and details from the list.
whenToUse: Meetings that follow a status change, such as approved or shortlisted
Standard agendas and attendee sets
Keeping the join link with the record
whenNotToUse: Finding a time that suits everyone, which needs availability checks first
Sending invites from a personal calendar for an organisational process
formulaOrCode:
Create Microsoft Teams > Create a Teams meeting Calendar id: Calendar (of the connection's account, or a shared calendar it can edit) Subject: Kick-off: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Title']} Message (HTML):

Agenda

  1. Scope and outcomes
  2. Roles
  3. Timeline and risks
  4. Next steps

Project record

Time zone: (UTC-05:00) Eastern Time (US & Canada) Start time: @{formatDateTime(triggerOutputs()?['body/KickoffDate'],'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss')} End time: @{formatDateTime(addMinutes(triggerOutputs()?['body/KickoffDate'],45),'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss')} Required attendees: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/ProjectManager/Email']};@{triggerOutputs()?['body/Sponsor/Email']} Optional attendees: pmo@contoso.com Importance: Normal Reminder: 15 Show as: Busy Start and end are local to the chosen time zone, without a Z suffix. If the list stores UTC: convertFromUtc(triggerOutputs()?['body/KickoffDate'],'Eastern Standard Time','yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss') Outputs to store on the record body('Create_a_Teams_meeting')?['id'] event ID body('Create_a_Teams_meeting')?['onlineMeeting/joinUrl'] join link SharePoint > Update item: MeetingEventId, MeetingJoinUrl Suggest a time first (optional) Office 365 Outlook > Find meeting times (V2) Required attendees: emails Meeting duration: 45 Start time: tomorrow 09:00 End time: +5 days Activity domain: Work first(body('Find_meeting_times_(V2)')?['meetingTimeSuggestions'])?['meetingTimeSlot/start/dateTime'] Suggestion times are returned in UTC. Convert before use. Reschedule or change Office 365 Outlook > Update event (V4) Calendar id: same calendar Id: MeetingEventId Subject, Start time, End time, Time zone: new values Required attendees: resend the full list The online meeting link stays the same. Attendees receive an update. Cancel Office 365 Outlook > Delete event (V2): Id = MeetingEventId attendees receive a cancellation Graph for a cancellation message: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/events/{id}/cancel { "comment": "Project on hold. A new date will follow." } Clear MeetingEventId and MeetingJoinUrl on the record. Channel meeting Create a Teams meeting has no channel option. Use Graph with the channel's email address as an attendee, or post the join link to the channel: Post message in a chat or channel: Kick-off scheduled for . Join Who is the organiser The connection's account. Use a service account with a mailbox and Teams licence (for example "PMO Meetings"), so meetings do not vanish or lose their organiser when a person leaves. Add the real host as a co-organiser afterwards in meeting options if needed. Recurring series The action creates single meetings. For a series, create the event through Microsoft Graph with a recurrence pattern and "isOnlineMeeting": true, "onlineMeetingProvider": "teamsForBusiness". Guard against duplicates Condition before creating: MeetingEventId is empty. Without it, each edit of the record creates another meeting.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide the trigger stage and the meeting's standard subject, agenda and attendees.
Create the Teams meeting with local start and end times and the right time zone.
Store the event ID and join link on the record.
Guard so a meeting is created only once per record.
Update the event when the date or attendees change.
Delete or cancel the event when the record is withdrawn.
commonMistakes: Passing UTC times with a non-UTC time zone, shifting the meeting.
Creating a meeting on every edit.
Using a personal connection as organiser.
Not storing the event ID, so the meeting cannot be changed.
troubleshooting: If the meeting is at the wrong hour, convert UTC values to the selected time zone before passing them.
If attendees are missing, check the semicolon-separated list for blank addresses.
If the join link is empty, read onlineMeeting/joinUrl from the action body.
If updates fail, the event belongs to another calendar or account than the connection's.
seoTitle: Schedule a Teams meeting from a flow
seoDescription: Create a Teams meeting with attendees and an agenda when a record reaches a stage, store the join link, and update or cancel it when details change.

faqs.question: Can Power Automate create a Teams meeting?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Teams connector's Create a Teams meeting action creates a calendar event with a join link and attendees.

faqs.question: How do I get the meeting join link in the flow?
faqs.answer: Read onlineMeeting/joinUrl from the action's output and store it on the record.

faqs.question: How do I reschedule a meeting created by a flow?
faqs.answer: Save the event ID and use Outlook's Update event action with the new times.

title: Fill an Adaptive Card drop-down with options from a list
shortDescription: Build the choices of an Input.ChoiceSet from SharePoint or Dataverse rows with a Select action, set a default, allow multi-select and read the answer back.
fullDescription: Hard-coded choices in a card go stale as soon as the list of categories or assignees changes. Generating the choices array from live data keeps the card current. A Select action shapes each row into a title and value pair, and the output is placed directly into the card JSON.
problemStatement: A triage card offers five assignees typed into the JSON. Two have changed teams, and every change means editing the flow.
whenToUse: Cards that assign, categorise or route using reference data
Choices that change over time
Multi-select questions built from a list
whenNotToUse: Hundreds of options, which are unusable in a card
Dependent drop-downs, which cards cannot refresh without a bot
formulaOrCode:
1. Get the options
  SharePoint > Get items: Support Agents
    Filter Query: Active eq 1        Order By: Title        Top Count: 50

2. Shape them
  Select
    From: body('Get_items')?['value']
    Map (text mode):
    { "title": "@{item()?['Title']} (@{item()?['Team/Value']})", "value": "@{item()?['Agent/Email']}" }
  Values must be strings. For numeric IDs: "value": "@{string(item()?['ID'])}"

3. Card
{
  "type": "AdaptiveCard", "$schema": "http://adaptivecards.io/schemas/adaptive-card.json", "version": "1.4",
  "body": [
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "Assign ticket #@{triggerOutputs()?['body/ID']}", "weight": "Bolder", "wrap": true },
    { "type": "TextBlock", "text": "@{triggerOutputs()?['body/Title']}", "wrap": true },
    { "type": "Input.ChoiceSet", "id": "assignee", "label": "Assign to", "style": "compact",
      "isRequired": true, "errorMessage": "Choose an agent",
      "value": "@{first(body('Select'))?['value']}",
      "choices": @{body('Select')} },
    { "type": "Input.ChoiceSet", "id": "tags", "label": "Tags", "isMultiSelect": true, "style": "expanded",
      "choices": @{body('Select_tags')} }
  ],
  "actions": [ { "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Assign" } ]
}
  "choices": @{body('Select')} is written without quotes: the action output is already a JSON array.

4. Styles
  "style": "compact"    drop-down (single select)
  "style": "expanded"   radio buttons, or check boxes with isMultiSelect
  "style": "filtered"   type-ahead search within the provided choices (version 1.5). Good for 20+ options.

5. Read the answer
  Single:  body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['data']?['assignee']         one value
  Multi:   body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['data']?['tags']             "Hardware,Urgent"
           split(coalesce(body('Post_adaptive_card_and_wait_for_a_response')?['data']?['tags'], ''), ',')
  Avoid commas inside values used with multi-select.

6. Look the choice up again
  The response holds only the value. To get the display name:
    Filter array:
      From: body('Select')        Condition: item()?['value'] is equal to <assignee value>
      first(body('Filter_array'))?['title']
  Or use the row ID as the value and Get item afterwards.

7. Default selection
  Single: "value": "<one of the values>". Omit it to force a deliberate choice (the required check then applies).
  Multi:  "value": "Hardware,Urgent"

8. No options
  Condition: length(body('Select')) is greater than 0. If empty, post a plain message that no agents are active
  instead of a card with an empty required field that cannot be submitted.

9. Add a fixed option
  union(body('Select'), json('[{"title":"Leave unassigned","value":"none"}]'))
  Put it in a Compose and use the Compose output for choices.

Limits
  Keep titles under about 60 characters, since they truncate on mobile.
  Stay below the 28 KB card size: 50 choices with short titles is comfortable.
stepByStepInstructions: Fetch the reference rows with a filter and a sensible limit.
Map each row to a title and string value with Select.
Place the Select output in the ChoiceSet's choices without quotes.
Choose compact, expanded or filtered style to suit the number of options.
Read the selected value from the response and look up related details.
Handle the case where no options exist.
commonMistakes: Typing choices into the JSON by hand.
Non-string values, which make the card invalid.
Quoting the choices array.
Commas in values used with multi-select.
troubleshooting: If the card fails to post, check each value is a string and the choices output is an array.
If the default is not selected, the value does not exactly match one of the choice values.
If multi-select returns one string, split it on commas.
If the list is long, switch the style to filtered and raise the card version to 1.5.
seoTitle: Fill an Adaptive Card drop-down with options from a list
seoDescription: Build the choices of an Input.ChoiceSet from SharePoint or Dataverse rows with a Select action, set a default, allow multi-select and read the answer back.
primaryKeyword: Adaptive Card ChoiceSet dynamic choices Power Automate

faqs.question: How do I populate an Adaptive Card drop-down from SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Use Get items, map each row to a title and value with Select, and insert the output as the ChoiceSet's choices.

faqs.question: How is a multi-select answer returned?
faqs.answer: As one comma-separated string of the selected values. Split it into an array in the flow.

faqs.question: Can the options change based on another input?
faqs.answer: Not in a flow-posted card. Cards cannot refresh choices without a bot, so ask in two steps or use an app.

title: Choose how a flow posts in Teams: Flow bot, user or agent
shortDescription: What each Post as and Post in option does, which combinations work in private channels and chats, and which identity suits alerts, approvals and conversations.
fullDescription: The Teams post actions ask two questions: who posts, and where. The answers decide whether the message looks automated, whether recipients can reply to someone, whether it works in private channels and whether a waiting card is possible. Picking deliberately avoids the common surprises.
problemStatement: A flow's messages appear to come from the person who built it, colleagues reply to them asking questions, and the same flow fails outright in a private channel.
whenToUse: Designing any Teams notification or card flow
Fixing posts that appear under the wrong name
Working out why posting fails in a private channel or group chat
whenNotToUse: Posting as a named employee for automated alerts
Assuming one configuration works in every location
formulaOrCode:
Post as
  Flow bot                 Shown as "Workflows" (formerly Power Automate), with "<owner name> via Workflows".
                           Clearly automated. Recipients cannot reply to it meaningfully.
  User                     Shown as the connection's account, exactly as if they typed it.
                           Replies and mentions go to that account.
  Power Virtual Agents     Shown as a Copilot Studio agent you choose. Needs the agent published to Teams.
  (Copilot Studio bot)     Lets replies continue as a conversation with the agent.

Post in
  Chat with Flow bot       one-to-one chat between the bot and one recipient
  Channel                  a standard, private or shared channel
  Group chat               an existing chat, by ID

What works
                              Flow bot     User      Agent
  Chat with Flow bot          yes          n/a       yes (chat with agent)
  Channel: standard           yes          yes       yes
  Channel: private            no           yes       no
  Channel: shared             limited      yes       no
  Group chat                  yes*         yes       no        *the bot is added to the chat on first post
  Post adaptive card and WAIT yes          yes**     yes       **waiting as User works in channels and chats

Typical choices
  Alert to a channel                          Flow bot in Channel. Private channel: User, with a service account.
  Personal notification                       Flow bot, Chat with Flow bot, Recipient = the person.
  Approval-style card to one person           Flow bot, Chat with Flow bot, Post adaptive card and wait.
  Card several people can answer              Flow bot in Channel, then update the card after the first response.
  Message that should invite a human reply    User, using a shared service account named for the team
                                              ("IT Service Desk"), in a chat or channel.
  Conversation after the notification         Agent, so the person can ask follow-up questions.

Recipient formats
  Chat with Flow bot > Recipient: email (UPN). Several recipients separated by semicolons create separate
  one-to-one posts, not a group chat.
  Group chat > enter the chat ID as a custom value (19:...@thread.v2).
  Channel > pick Team and Channel, or pass the team (group) ID and channel ID as custom values for dynamic targets.

First-time delivery
  The Flow bot can message a user who has never used Workflows. If the Workflows app is blocked by a Teams
  app permission policy, posts as Flow bot fail for those users: allow the app in the Teams admin center.
  Guests and external users cannot receive Flow bot chats.

Message content
  Post message accepts a subset of HTML: p, br, strong, em, a, ul/ol/li, table, code, h1 to h3.
  Use Post card for layout, buttons and inputs.
  Mentions: Get an @mention token for a user, then insert the token.

Identity hygiene
  Connections belong to people. For production flows create the Teams connection with a service account, so
  "via Workflows" shows a neutral name and the flow survives staff changes.
  The service account must be a member of the teams and private channels it posts to.

Throttling
  Per connection roughly 100 calls per 60 seconds for the Teams connector. Posting to many people in a loop:
  keep concurrency low, add a short delay, or send one channel post with a tag mention.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide whether the message should look automated or come from an account people can reply to.
Pick the location: bot chat, channel or group chat.
Check the combination is supported, especially for private channels.
Create the Teams connection with a service account for production flows.
Use card actions when layout, buttons or inputs are needed.
Test delivery for a user who has never used Workflows.
commonMistakes: Posting automated alerts as the maker's own account.
Using Flow bot in a private channel.
Putting several emails in Recipient and expecting a group chat.
Blocking the Workflows app in Teams policy and wondering why posts fail.
troubleshooting: If posting to a private channel fails, switch Post as to User and add that account to the channel.
If a user gets nothing, check the Workflows app is allowed for them and the address is their UPN.
If the name shown is a former employee, recreate the Teams connection with a service account.
If posts are throttled, lower concurrency or consolidate messages.
seoTitle: Choose how a flow posts in Teams: Flow bot, user or agent
seoDescription: What each Post as and Post in option does, which combinations work in private channels and chats, and which identity suits alerts, approvals and conversations.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate post as Flow bot vs user

faqs.question: What is the difference between posting as Flow bot and as User?
faqs.answer: Flow bot posts as the Workflows app and looks automated. User posts as the connection's account, as if that person wrote it.

faqs.question: Why can't my flow post in a private channel?
faqs.answer: The Flow bot is not supported in private channels. Post as a user who is a member of the channel.

faqs.question: Can a flow send a direct message to someone?
faqs.answer: Yes. Post as Flow bot in Chat with Flow bot and set the recipient to the person's email.

title: Add custom validation to a Power Pages form with JavaScript
shortDescription: Register a custom page validator so a basic form shows your message in the standard validation summary and blocks submit until the rule passes.
fullDescription: Power Pages forms validate required fields and data types on their own. Rules such as 'end date after start date' or 'phone or email required' need script. The supported way is to add a validator to the page's validator collection, which plugs into the same summary box and field highlighting as built-in checks.
problemStatement: A date range can be submitted with the end before the start. A hand-written alert on the submit button does not stop the form posting.
whenToUse: Cross-field rules on basic and multistep forms
Format checks beyond the column's data type
Conditional required fields
whenNotToUse: Rules that must hold for security or data integrity, which also need server-side enforcement
Replacing simple required settings that form metadata can handle
stepByStepInstructions: Find the logical names of the fields involved.
Add script to the page or the form's Custom JavaScript.
Create a validator object with an evaluation function and an error message.
Push it into Page_Validators when the document is ready.
Toggle the required style and validator for conditional rules.
Enforce critical rules again in Dataverse.
commonMistakes: Using alert and return false on the button's click, which the form ignores.
Selecting fields by display name instead of logical name.
Validating only in the browser.
Returning false for blank values, which duplicates the required message.
troubleshooting: If the validator never runs, check Page_Validators exists on that page and the script loads without errors.
If the message is not clickable, wrap it in an anchor that targets the field label.
If a date comparison is wrong, compare the hidden ISO value, not the formatted text.
If the rule fires on a hidden field, remove its validator when you hide the field.
seoTitle: Add custom validation to a Power Pages form with JavaScript
seoDescription: Register a custom page validator so a basic form shows your message in the standard validation summary and blocks submit until the rule passes.

faqs.question: How do I add custom validation to a Power Pages form?
faqs.answer: Create a validator object in JavaScript with an evaluation function and push it into the Page_Validators array.

faqs.question: Where do I put JavaScript for a basic form?
faqs.answer: In the page's JavaScript file, or in the form's Custom JavaScript box under Additional Settings in the Portal Management app.

faqs.question: Is client-side validation enough?
faqs.answer: No. Repeat important rules in Dataverse with business rules, workflows or plug-ins.

title: Build a multistep form with conditional branching
shortDescription: Split a long application into steps, branch to different steps based on an answer, show progress and let people resume where they left off.
fullDescription: A multistep form walks a visitor through several Dataverse forms or tabs in order, saving as it goes. Condition steps test a column value and send the visitor down one path or another. Session tracking lets a signed-in user return later and continue from the last completed step.
problemStatement: A grant application has forty fields. Business applicants need a company section that individuals should never see, and people abandon the single long page.
whenToUse: Long applications and registrations
Paths that differ by an early answer
Forms people complete over more than one sitting
whenNotToUse: Short forms, where a basic form is simpler
Branching so complex that a canvas or custom page would be clearer
formulaOrCode:
Dataverse preparation
  Table: Application (cr1a2_application)
  One main form per step (or one form with a tab per step):
    "Web - Applicant", "Web - Company", "Web - Project", "Web - Declaration"
  Column used for branching: cr1a2_applicanttype (Choice: Individual 100000000, Business 100000001)

Create the multistep form
  Design studio > page > + Multistep form > New multistep form
    Name: Grant application        Table: Application
  Add step (repeat):
    Step name, Table, Form, Tab (optional), Mode
  Steps
    1  Applicant      Load Form  form "Web - Applicant"     Mode: Insert
    2  Business?      Condition  cr1a2_applicanttype == 100000001
                                   Next step if true:  3 Company
                                   Next step if false: 4 Project
    3  Company        Load Form  form "Web - Company"       Mode: Edit     Source: Result from previous step
    4  Project        Load Form  form "Web - Project"       Mode: Edit     Source: Result from previous step
    5  Declaration    Load Form  form "Web - Declaration"   Mode: Edit     Source: Result from previous step
    6  Thank you      Redirect   to the page /application-received  (or a final step with a success message)
  Portal Management app > Multistep Forms > Form Steps shows the same with every option
  (Type: Load Form | Load Tab | Condition | Redirect).

Condition syntax (Condition step > Condition)
  cr1a2_applicanttype == 100000001
  cr1a2_amount > 5000 && cr1a2_country == "US"
  cr1a2_haspartner == true
  Operators: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, &&, ||, =* (contains, for text). Use logical names. Choices compare by number.

Settings worth changing (multistep form record)
  Progress indicator: Enabled        Type: Title | Numeric | Progress bar        Position: Top
  Start New Session On Load: No      (keeps a returning user's progress)
  Multiple Records Per User Permitted: No     (one application per user. Yes for repeatable requests)
  Edit Expired State Code / Status Code: stop editing once the record is submitted (for example inactive)
  Authentication required: Yes, so sessions can be tied to a contact

Per step
  Move Previous Permitted: Yes
  Associate Current Portal User: Yes on step 1, Target column: cr1a2_applicant (lookup to Contact)
    so the record belongs to the signed-in contact and table permissions with Contact scope apply.
  Set Values on Save: on the Declaration step set cr1a2_submittedon to the current date, and status reason
    to Submitted (Portal Management > step > Form Options, or a flow on update).
  Attach File: Yes on a documents step (notes or SharePoint, see the file upload pattern).

Table permissions
  Table: Application    Access type: Contact    Relationship: the applicant lookup
  Privileges: Create, Read, Write, Append, Append To        Web role: Authenticated Users
  Without Create and Write the form shows a permission error.

Client script per step
  Each step has its own Custom JavaScript. Validators and show/hide rules are added the same way as on basic forms.

Branching to a different table
  A step can load a form for a related table using Source: Record associated to current portal user, or
  Query string. Keep this for genuine child records.

Save and resume
  With Start New Session On Load = No and a signed-in user, returning to the page opens the last step
  reached. Add a "Save and finish later" hint next to the Next button with a content snippet.

Test
  Walk both branches. Use Previous across the condition step. Reload mid-way and confirm resume. Check the
  record's values after each step.
stepByStepInstructions: Create one Dataverse form or tab per step.
Add a multistep form and its load steps in order.
Insert condition steps that test the branching column.
Set source, mode and previous-step options on each step.
Associate the record with the signed-in contact and add table permissions.
Enable the progress indicator and test every path, including resume.
commonMistakes: Setting later steps to Insert, which creates a new record at each step.
Comparing choice columns to labels instead of numeric values.
No table permissions for create and write.
Starting a new session on every load, which loses progress.
troubleshooting: If a second record is created mid-way, set later steps to Edit with source Result from previous step.
If the condition always goes one way, check the logical name and the numeric choice value.
If users see access denied, add table permissions with contact scope and the right web role.
If Previous shows stale data, clear the server cache or republish after changing step settings.
seoTitle: Build a multistep form with conditional branching
seoDescription: Split a long application into steps, branch to different steps based on an answer, show progress and let people resume where they left off.
primaryKeyword: Power Pages multistep form conditional step

faqs.question: What is a multistep form in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: A sequence of Dataverse forms or tabs presented as steps, with saving between steps and optional branching.

faqs.question: Can a multistep form skip steps based on an answer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add a condition step that tests a column and sets different next steps for true and false.

faqs.question: Can users resume a multistep form later?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are signed in and the form does not start a new session on load.

title: Configure a Power Pages list with search, filters and row actions
shortDescription: Show Dataverse rows on a page with paging, search, a filter panel, a details link and create, edit and delete actions, all limited by table permissions.
fullDescription: A list component renders a Dataverse view on a web page. Most of what a records page needs is configuration: which views, how many rows, search, metadata filters, and actions that open forms. Table permissions decide which rows each visitor sees, so the same list serves every customer with their own data.
problemStatement: Customers need to see and manage their own support cases on the site, and writing a custom page for a table with paging and filtering would take days.
whenToUse: My records pages such as cases, applications or orders
Public directories from a Dataverse view
Simple self-service create, edit and delete
whenNotToUse: Highly designed layouts, where Liquid with FetchXML gives full control
Lists over very large unfiltered views, which load slowly
formulaOrCode:
Dataverse view first
  Table: Case (or your table) > Views > "Web - My active cases"
  Columns in display order: Case Number, Title, Status Reason, Created On
  Filter: Status = Active        Sort: Created On descending
  The list shows the view's columns and sort. Row scope comes from table permissions, not from the view.

Add the list
  Design studio > page > + List > New list
    Name: My cases        Table: Case        Views: Web - My active cases, Web - My resolved cases
  Several views appear as a drop-down on the page.

List settings (design studio or Portal Management > Lists)
  General
    Page Size: 10
    Enable Table Permissions: On            (always, except truly public reference data)
    Empty List Text: You have no cases yet.
  Search
    Enabled: Yes        Tooltip / hint text: Search title or number
    Searches the view's text columns. A leading * allows contains matches, for example *printer.
  Actions (Grid Configuration)
    View Actions > Create:  Target: Page (/support/new-case) or Basic form "Web - New case"
    Item Actions > Details: Target: Page (/support/case) or form "Web - Case details", Record ID parameter: id
                 > Edit:    Basic form "Web - Edit case"
                 > Delete:  with confirmation text
                 > Workflow: run an on-demand classic workflow against the row
    Download: adds an Excel export of the current view (respects permissions).
  Each action can have a custom button label.

Filter panel (Metadata Filter, Portal Management > List > Metadata Filter)
  Enabled: Yes        Orientation: Vertical | Horizontal        Apply button label: Apply
  Add filter types:
    Text            Column: Title                     free-text contains
    Attribute set   Column: Status Reason, Priority   check boxes built from choice options
    Lookup set      Column: Product                   check boxes from related rows
    Range set       Column: Created On                named ranges such as Last 7 days
    FetchXML        custom condition for anything else

Filter by the signed-in user without table permissions (Options tab)
  Portal User Attribute: customerid (or a contact lookup)        rows where that column = the current contact
  Account Attribute: parent customer account                     rows for the user's account
  Table permissions are the stronger control. Use both only when the view must narrow further.

Table permissions
  Table: Case        Access type: Contact (customerid) or Account        Privileges: Read, Write, Create, Append, Append To
  Web role: Authenticated Users (or a customer role)
  Child permission for notes if the details form shows the timeline:
    Table: Note (annotation)   Access type: Parent   Parent: the Case permission   Relationship: Case_Annotation

Details page
  Add a page /support/case with a basic form in Edit or Read-only mode,
  Record source: Query string, parameter name: id. The list's Details action passes ?id=<guid>.

Map and calendar views
  A list can render as a calendar (Calendar View settings: start, end, summary columns) or a map when rows
  hold latitude and longitude.

Performance
  Keep the view to under ten columns, avoid sorting on lookups, and filter the view itself (active only).
  Lists are cached per user for a short time: new rows can take a moment to appear.

Styling
  The list renders a Bootstrap table. Target it in the page's CSS: .entitylist .view-grid table { ... }
  Add a script on the list's "loaded" event to adjust cells:
    $(".entitylist.entity-grid").on("loaded", function () {
      // format status cells
    });
stepByStepInstructions: Create Dataverse views with the columns and sort the page should show.
Add a list to the page and select the views.
Turn on table permissions and create permissions scoped to the contact or account.
Enable search and add metadata filters for the main columns.
Add create, details, edit and delete actions that target forms or pages.
Create the details page that reads the record ID from the query string.
commonMistakes: Turning table permissions off to make rows appear.
Using a view with twenty columns.
Forgetting permissions for related tables shown on the details form.
Expecting the view's owner filter to restrict rows for web users.
troubleshooting: If the list is empty, check table permissions, the web role and that the view returns rows for that contact.
If an action button is missing, the user lacks the matching privilege, such as Write for Edit.
If search finds nothing, the searched column is not a text column in the view.
If changes do not show, clear the site cache or wait for it to refresh.
seoTitle: Configure a Power Pages list with search, filters and row actions
seoDescription: Show Dataverse rows on a page with paging, search, a filter panel, a details link and create, edit and delete actions, all limited by table permissions.

faqs.question: How do I show Dataverse records on a Power Pages site?
faqs.answer: Add a list component, choose the table and views, and set table permissions so visitors see only the rows they should.

faqs.question: How do I show only the signed-in user's rows?
faqs.answer: Create a table permission with Contact or Account access type and enable table permissions on the list.

faqs.question: Can visitors filter a list?
faqs.answer: Yes. Enable search and add metadata filters for text, choice, lookup and range columns.

title: Read, update and delete Dataverse rows with the Power Pages Web API
shortDescription: Query rows with OData, patch a column and delete a record from page script using the portal Web API, with the site settings and wrapper each call needs.
fullDescription: The portal Web API exposes Dataverse tables to page script under /_api. Reads use OData query options, updates use PATCH and deletes use DELETE. Every table must be enabled through site settings, every call is checked against table permissions and column permissions, and write calls must carry an anti-forgery token.
problemStatement: A page needs to load a user's open orders, let them change a delivery note inline and cancel an order, without full page reloads or a form per action.
whenToUse: Interactive pages that read and change data without reloads
Inline edits, toggles and quick actions
Custom layouts fed by JSON
whenNotToUse: Tables holding data a visitor should never query, even filtered
Complex transactions better handled by a flow or server logic
stepByStepInstructions: Enable the table and list the allowed columns in site settings.
Create table permissions for the operations the page needs.
Add the safeAjax wrapper to the site.
Query rows with select, filter, orderby and top.
Patch changed columns and delete or cancel rows through the wrapper.
Handle 403 and 404 responses with clear messages and test as different users.
commonMistakes: Using the table's singular logical name instead of the entity set name.
Setting fields to * on sensitive tables.
Calling $.ajax directly without the verification token for writes.
Assuming the filter in the query is the security boundary.
troubleshooting: If you get 404, check the Webapi/<table>/enabled setting and the plural entity set name.
If a column is rejected, add it to the fields setting and wait for the cache to refresh.
If writes return 403, add Write or Delete to the table permission for that web role.
If a lookup bind fails, use the navigation property's schema name with exact casing.
seoTitle: Read, update and delete Dataverse rows with the Power Pages Web API
seoDescription: Query rows with OData, patch a column and delete a record from page script using the portal Web API, with the site settings and wrapper each call needs.
primaryKeyword: Power Pages Web API GET PATCH DELETE

faqs.question: How do I query Dataverse from Power Pages JavaScript?
faqs.answer: Enable the table for the Web API in site settings, then send a GET to /_api/<entity set> with OData options through the safeAjax wrapper.

faqs.question: Does the Power Pages Web API respect security?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every call is checked against table permissions and column permissions for the signed-in user's web roles.

faqs.question: Why do I get 404 from /_api?
faqs.answer: The table is not enabled in site settings or the URL uses the wrong entity set name.

title: Let visitors upload files on a Power Pages form
shortDescription: Add attachments to basic and multistep forms, choose between Dataverse notes, Azure Blob Storage and SharePoint, and set file type and size limits.
fullDescription: Power Pages forms can accept files in three ways: as notes on the record, as notes whose content is stored in Azure Blob Storage, or as documents in a SharePoint library linked to the record. Each needs the right table permissions. Limits on type, size and count belong in the form configuration, not just in guidance text.
problemStatement: Applicants must attach proof documents. Emailing them separately breaks the link to the application and loses files.
whenToUse: Supporting documents on applications and cases
Photos or evidence attached to requests
Document exchange with customers through SharePoint
whenNotToUse: Very large files such as video without Azure storage
Accepting any file type on a public anonymous form
formulaOrCode:
Option A: attach on submit, stored as notes (simplest)
  Portal Management > Basic Forms > your form > Additional Settings > Add Attach File
    Attach File: Yes
    Attach File Storage Location: Note Attachment
    Allow Multiple Files: Yes
    Attach File Required: Yes (with a required error message)
    Restrict File Types: Yes     Accept (MIME): application/pdf,image/png,image/jpeg
                                 Accept (extensions): .pdf,.png,.jpg
    Maximum File Size (KB): 5120
    Label: Supporting documents
  Works on Insert-mode forms: files are saved as notes on the new record.
  Table permissions:
    Parent: your table (Create, Read, Write, Append To)
    Child:  Note (annotation), Access type Parent, relationship <table>_Annotations, privileges Create, Read, Write, Append
  Dataverse limit: environment's maximum attachment size (System Settings > Email > file size, default 5 MB,
  up to about 128 MB). Blocked extensions list also applies.

Option B: timeline (notes) control on an edit form
  Add the Timeline to the Dataverse form used by the basic form (Edit mode).
  Basic form metadata: Type Notes > Create Dialog Options, Edit, Delete enabled as needed.
  Notes are shown on the site only when their text starts with *WEB* by default. Notes added through the
  site get the prefix automatically. Staff adding a note for the customer type *WEB* first.

Option C: notes stored in Azure Blob Storage (large files, cheaper storage)
  Create a storage account and a container. Set CORS on the storage account for the site's URL.
  Site settings:
    FileStorage/CloudStorageAccount            <storage connection string>
    FileStorage/CloudStorageContainerName      <container>
  Form: Attach File Storage Location: Azure Blob Storage
  The note row stays in Dataverse with a pointer. Staff view files in model-driven apps through the
  Azure storage web resource from the Power Pages configuration.

Option D: SharePoint document library
  Admin: Power Pages admin > Set up > External apps / SharePoint integration: Enable.
  Dataverse: Document management enabled for the table, with a SharePoint site.
  Dataverse form: add a sub-grid for Document Locations (table: Document Locations, view: Active Document Locations).
  The basic form in Edit mode shows the library with Add files and New folder.
  Table permissions:
    Parent on your table, plus Child on Document Location (sharepointdocumentlocation), Access type Parent,
    privileges Create, Read, Write, Append, Append To.
  Good for exchanging documents both ways. Files live in SharePoint with its storage and versioning.

Option E: file columns
  A Dataverse File column on a form renders an upload control on the page. One file per column, size limit
  set on the column (up to several GB). Suits a fixed set of named documents, such as "Proof of identity".

Validation and safety
  Restrict types to what you need. Extension checks are not content checks: enable malware scanning where
  your platform plan includes it and treat uploads as untrusted.
  State limits beside the control with a content snippet: "PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 5 MB each".
  Anonymous uploads: add a CAPTCHA to the form (Additional Settings > Add Captcha) and keep size limits low.

After upload
  Cloud flow on note or document creation: virus scan service, move to a case folder, notify staff.
  Show the user what they uploaded on the confirmation page with a notes list or a Liquid query.
stepByStepInstructions: Choose the storage approach that suits file size and how staff will use the files.
Enable attach file on the form with type, size and count limits.
Add child table permissions for notes or document locations.
Configure Azure storage or SharePoint integration if selected.
Add a CAPTCHA and clear limit text for public forms.
Test upload, viewing by staff and viewing by the visitor.
commonMistakes: No child permission on notes, so uploads fail silently or files are invisible.
Unlimited file types on a public form.
Expecting notes added by staff to show on the site without the web prefix.
Using notes for very large files.
troubleshooting: If the upload control does not appear, check Attach File is enabled and the form mode supports it.
If the file is rejected, compare its size with both the form limit and the environment's attachment limit.
If uploaded files are not visible to the user, add Read on the note or document location child permission.
If SharePoint shows access denied, re-enable the integration and check the document location permission.
seoTitle: Let visitors upload files on a Power Pages form
seoDescription: Add attachments to basic and multistep forms, choose between Dataverse notes, Azure Blob Storage and SharePoint, and set file type and size limits.

faqs.question: How do I add file upload to a Power Pages form?
faqs.answer: Enable Attach File in the form's additional settings, choose a storage location and add table permissions for notes.

faqs.question: Where are uploaded files stored?
faqs.answer: As Dataverse notes by default, or in Azure Blob Storage, a SharePoint library or a file column depending on configuration.

faqs.question: How do I limit file type and size?
faqs.answer: Set Restrict File Types, the accepted types and the maximum file size on the form's attach file settings.

title: Set up sign-in for a Power Pages site
shortDescription: Choose between workforce Entra ID, Entra External ID and local accounts, configure the provider, map claims to the contact and control registration.
fullDescription: Every signed-in visitor on a Power Pages site is a Dataverse contact linked to an external identity. The identity provider decides who can sign in: employees through Microsoft Entra ID, customers through Entra External ID or another OpenID Connect provider. Getting claims mapping and registration settings right avoids duplicate contacts and open sign-up.
problemStatement: A partner site launched with local username and password accounts and open registration. There are duplicate contacts, forgotten passwords and sign-ups from people who are not partners.
whenToUse: Any site with signed-in content
Employee-facing sites using the corporate directory
Customer or partner sites needing self-service sign-up or invitation only
whenNotToUse: Local authentication for new sites, where an external identity provider is the recommended route
Open registration on sites exposing customer data without an approval or invitation step
formulaOrCode:
Where
  Power Pages design studio > Security > Identity providers

Option 1: employees (Microsoft Entra ID, workforce tenant)
  Enabled by default as "Microsoft Entra ID". Any user in your tenant can sign in.
  Restrict to some employees: Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > the site's app >
    Properties > Assignment required: Yes > Users and groups: add the allowed group.
  Set as default provider so visitors skip the provider choice page.

Option 2: customers and partners (Microsoft Entra External ID, or Azure AD B2C on existing sites)
  In the external tenant:
    App registrations > New: redirect URI  https://<site>.powerappsportals.com/signin-<provider-name>
      (the exact Reply URL is shown in the Power Pages provider wizard)
    Authentication: ID tokens enabled. Front-channel logout URL: https://<site>/Account/Login/LogOff
    User flows > Sign up and sign in: attributes Email, Given name, Surname. Identity providers: email one-time
      passcode or password, plus Google or Facebook if wanted. Add the app to the user flow.
  In Power Pages > Identity providers > New provider > OpenID Connect (or the Entra External ID tile)
