    Authority:      https://<tenant-subdomain>.ciamlogin.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0
    Client ID:      the app registration's application ID
    Redirect URL:   as shown
    Metadata address: <authority>/.well-known/openid-configuration
    Scope: openid email profile        Response type: id_token (or code with a client secret)
    External logout: On
  Additional settings
    Registration claims mapping:  firstname=given_name,lastname=family_name,emailaddress1=email
    Login claims mapping:         same list, to refresh the contact at each sign-in
    Contact mapping with email:   On       links the sign-in to an existing contact with that email
                                           instead of creating a duplicate. Use only when the provider
                                           verifies email addresses.
    Registration enabled:         On for self-service, Off for invitation only

Option 3: other providers
  OpenID Connect, SAML 2.0 or WS-Federation for a customer's own identity system. Same claims mapping idea.
  Social providers (Microsoft, LinkedIn, Facebook, Google, X) are available as direct tiles.

Local authentication (username and password stored with the contact)
  Supported but not recommended for new sites. Turn it off when using an external provider:
    Site setting  Authentication/Registration/LocalLoginEnabled = false
  Also consider
    Authentication/Registration/Enabled                     master switch for any registration
    Authentication/Registration/OpenRegistrationEnabled     false = no self sign-up
    Authentication/Registration/InvitationEnabled           true = redeem invitation codes
    Authentication/Registration/RequiresConfirmation        email confirmation
    Authentication/Registration/LoginButtonAuthenticationType = <provider authority>   go straight to one provider
    Authentication/Registration/ProfileRedirectEnabled      false to skip the profile page after first sign-in

What happens at first sign-in
  A contact is created (or matched by email) and an External Identity row links it to the provider's subject ID.
  The contact receives the Authenticated Users web role. Other roles are assigned by staff, a flow, or
  through an invitation that carries web roles.

Assign a web role automatically for a known domain (cloud flow)
  Trigger: Dataverse > When a row is added: External Identities (adx_externalidentity)
  Get the contact > Condition: endsWith(emailaddress1, '@partner.com')
  Dataverse > Relate rows: Contact <> Web Role (adx_webrole_contact) with the Partner role

Session and sign-out
  Authentication/ApplicationCookie/ExpireTimeSpan   default 24:00:00. Shorten for sensitive sites (for example 01:00:00)
  Authentication/ApplicationCookie/SlidingExpiration  true keeps active users signed in

Test matrix
  New user self-registers. Existing contact with the same email signs in for the first time (no duplicate).
  A user outside the allowed group or without an invitation is refused. Sign-out clears the provider session.
stepByStepInstructions: Decide who the audience is and pick the matching identity provider.
Register the site as an application with the provider and set the reply URL.
Add the provider in the design studio with authority, client ID and scope.
Map claims to contact columns and enable contact mapping by email where emails are verified.
Set registration to open, invitation only or closed, and turn off local sign-in.
Test first sign-in, existing-contact matching, refusal and sign-out.
commonMistakes: Leaving local sign-in and open registration on by default.
No claims mapping, creating contacts with blank names.
Contact mapping by email with a provider that does not verify addresses.
Granting data access to the Authenticated Users role when anyone can register.
troubleshooting: If sign-in fails with a redirect error, the reply URL in the app registration does not match the site's exactly.
If duplicate contacts appear, enable contact mapping with email and merge existing duplicates.
If names are blank, check the token contains the claims and the mapping uses the right claim names.
If users land on the profile page every time, set ProfileRedirectEnabled to false.
seoTitle: Set up sign-in for a Power Pages site
seoDescription: Choose between workforce Entra ID, Entra External ID and local accounts, configure the provider, map claims to the contact and control registration.

faqs.question: How do users sign in to a Power Pages site?
faqs.answer: Through an identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID for employees or Entra External ID for customers. Each user is linked to a Dataverse contact.

faqs.question: How do I stop anyone registering on my site?
faqs.answer: Turn off open registration and use invitations, or require assignment on the Entra application for employee sites.

faqs.question: How do I avoid duplicate contacts at sign-in?
faqs.answer: Enable contact mapping with email so a new sign-in links to the existing contact with that address.

title: Personalise Power Pages content with the Liquid user object
shortDescription: Greet the signed-in contact, show their account details, branch on sign-in state and roles, and pass user values safely into page script.
fullDescription: Liquid runs on the server before a page is sent. The user object is the signed-in visitor's contact row, so any contact column, the parent account and the visitor's web roles are available to templates. It covers most personalisation without script, and it is the right way to hand the user's ID to JavaScript.
problemStatement: Every visitor sees the same generic page. The site knows who is signed in but shows no name, no account context and the same calls to action to everyone.
whenToUse: Greeting and account context on dashboards and headers
Different content for anonymous and signed-in visitors
Passing the contact ID or roles to page script
whenNotToUse: Hiding sensitive data with Liquid alone, without table permissions
Heavy queries in headers that run on every page
stepByStepInstructions: Check sign-in state with the user object.
Output contact columns with the escape filter.
Read the parent account through the lookup and entities object.
Branch on web roles for role-specific links and content.
Pass the user's ID and roles to script with the json filter.
Wrap user-specific markup in substitution tags inside cached templates.
commonMistakes: Using Liquid visibility as the only protection for data.
Outputting user values without escape or json filters.
Personalised content inside a cached header without substitution.
Comparing role names with different casing or spelling.
troubleshooting: If user is empty for a signed-in visitor, the template is output cached. Add substitution tags.
If a custom column prints nothing, check the logical name and that the column has a value.
If the account row is blank, the visitor lacks a table permission to read their account.
If script breaks on names with apostrophes, switch to the json filter.
seoTitle: Personalise Power Pages content with the Liquid user object
seoDescription: Greet the signed-in contact, show their account details, branch on sign-in state and roles, and pass user values safely into page script.

faqs.question: What is the Liquid user object in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: It is the signed-in visitor's contact row, giving templates access to contact columns, the parent account and web roles.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a visitor is signed in?
faqs.answer: Use {% if user %}. The object is empty for anonymous visitors.

faqs.question: How do I get the current user's ID in JavaScript?
faqs.answer: Output it with Liquid into a script block, for example {{ user.id }}, using the json filter for text values.

title: Build reusable layouts with Power Pages web templates
shortDescription: Compose pages from a base layout and small partial templates using extends, block and include, and pass parameters to partials for cards, banners and lists.
fullDescription: Web templates are the source code of a Power Pages site. Template inheritance lets every page share one base layout with named blocks to override. Includes pull in partials such as a card or breadcrumb, with parameters. Structured this way, a design change is made once and appears everywhere.
problemStatement: The same hero banner and card markup is pasted into fifteen pages. A design tweak means editing each one, and they have already drifted apart.
whenToUse: Sites with more than a handful of custom pages
Repeated components such as cards, banners and alerts
Custom page layouts beyond the built-in templates
whenNotToUse: Simple sites built entirely in the design studio's visual editor
Deep inheritance chains that are hard to follow
stepByStepInstructions: Create a base layout web template with named blocks.
Create page layouts that extend the base and override blocks.
Move repeated markup into partial templates with parameters.
Create page templates that point at the layouts and assign them to pages.
Use JSON-returning templates for script-driven parts.
Keep templates in source control with the PAC CLI.
commonMistakes: Copying markup between pages instead of including a partial.
Putting content outside block tags in an extending template, where it is ignored.
Queries inside partials that run once per loop iteration.
Unescaped user input in partial output.
troubleshooting: If the extended layout renders nothing, check extends is the first statement and content sits inside blocks.
If an include prints nothing, the template name is misspelled or its parameters are empty.
If a JSON template returns HTML, set the MIME type and remove the header and footer on its page template.
If changes do not appear, clear the cache from the design studio's preview or the site's admin actions.
seoTitle: Build reusable layouts with Power Pages web templates
seoDescription: Compose pages from a base layout and small partial templates using extends, block and include, and pass parameters to partials for cards, banners and lists.
primaryKeyword: Power Pages web template include extends

faqs.question: What is a web template in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: A stored block of HTML and Liquid that page templates render, used for layouts, partials and custom endpoints.

faqs.question: How do I reuse markup across Power Pages pages?
faqs.answer: Put it in a web template and include it, passing parameters, or build a base layout and extend it.

faqs.question: Can a web template return JSON?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set its MIME type to application/json and use a page template without the site header and footer.

title: Manage editable text and configuration with content snippets and site settings
shortDescription: Keep labels, notices and footer text in content snippets and keep switches, URLs and limits in site settings, so content editors never touch templates.
fullDescription: Text typed into templates needs a developer for every wording change. Content snippets are named pieces of text or HTML that editors change in the studio or the Portal Management app, per language. Site settings hold configuration values that templates and platform features read. Using both keeps templates stable across environments.
problemStatement: The support phone number appears in eight templates. Changing it took a developer, a deployment and still missed two pages.
whenToUse: Text that changes without a release: notices, labels, legal lines
Values that differ between environments, such as URLs and feature switches
Multilingual sites
whenNotToUse: Secrets such as API keys, which site settings do not protect from templates or exports
Large page bodies, which belong in page copy
formulaOrCode:
Content snippets (Portal Management > Content Snippets) Name: Support/Phone Type: Text Language: English Value: +1 555 0100 Name: Home/Notice Type: HTML Value: Offices closed 25 December. Name: Footer/Legal Type: HTML Name: Requests/EmptyState Type: Text Value: You have no requests yet. Naming: Area/Purpose. One row per language for multilingual sites. In templates {{ snippets['Support/Phone'] }} {{ snippets['Home/Notice'] | default: '' }} {% assign notice = snippets['Home/Notice'] %} {% if notice and notice != '' %}
{{ notice }}
{% endif %} Editable in place by content authors (shows an edit affordance to users with content permissions): {% editable snippets 'Home/Notice' type: 'html' %} {% editable snippets 'Support/Phone' type: 'text', default: 'Contact us' %} Built-in snippets worth knowing Footer, Head/Bottom (extra tags before , for analytics or meta tags), Site name, Account/SignIn/PageTitle, Search/Title, Profile/..., and many labels used by forms and sign-in pages. Search the list before writing your own label. Site settings (Portal Management > Site Settings) Name: Support/Email Value: help@contoso.com Name: Feature/ShowChat Value: true Name: Requests/MaxOpen Value: 5 Name: Integration/StatusPageUrl Value: https://status.contoso.com In templates {{ settings['Support/Email'] }} {% assign showChat = settings['Feature/ShowChat'] | boolean %} {% if showChat %}{% include 'Partial - Chat Widget' %}{% endif %} {% assign maxOpen = settings['Requests/MaxOpen'] | integer | default: 5 %} {% if openCount >= maxOpen %}

{{ snippets['Requests/LimitReached'] }}

{% endif %} In script (publish only non-sensitive values) Platform settings you will meet Authentication/Registration/OpenRegistrationEnabled Search/Enabled Webapi//enabled, Webapi/
/fields HTTP/X-Frame-Options, HTTP/Content-Security-Policy Header/OutputCache/Enabled, Footer/OutputCache/Enabled Site/EnableDefaultHtmlEditor Profile/ForceSignUp Authentication/ApplicationCookie/ExpireTimeSpan Environment-specific values Site settings can take their value from a Dataverse environment variable: on the setting choose Source: Environment variable and select it. The same solution then carries different values per environment. Without that, keep a short post-deployment list of settings to check. Secrets: reference an environment variable of type Secret (Azure Key Vault) only for server-side features that support it. Anything rendered by Liquid can be seen by visitors. Who can edit Snippets: content authors with a web role that has website access permission "Manage Content Snippets". Site settings: administrators in the Portal Management app. Caching Changes made in the Portal Management app can take a few minutes to appear. Use the design studio's Sync button or the site's "Clear cache" action (/_services/about as an administrator) to refresh at once. Convention Text a business person may reword: snippet. A value that changes behaviour: site setting. A value that differs per environment: site setting backed by an environment variable.
stepByStepInstructions: List the hard-coded text and values in your templates.
Create content snippets for wording and site settings for configuration.
Replace literals in templates with snippets and settings lookups.
Add default values so a missing row does not break the page.
Back environment-specific settings with environment variables.
Give content authors permission to edit snippets and show them where.
commonMistakes: Hard-coding contact details and notices in templates.
Storing secrets in site settings.
No defaults, leaving blank gaps when a snippet is missing.
One snippet reused for unrelated purposes.
troubleshooting: If a snippet shows nothing, check the name, the language and that the row belongs to this website.
If a setting change has no effect, clear the site cache.
If a boolean setting behaves oddly, convert it with the boolean filter before testing it.
If values are wrong after deployment, check environment variable values in the target.
seoTitle: Manage editable text and configuration with content snippets and site settings
seoDescription: Keep labels, notices and footer text in content snippets and keep switches, URLs and limits in site settings, so content editors never touch templates.
primaryKeyword: Power Pages content snippets site settings

faqs.question: What is a content snippet in Power Pages?
faqs.answer: A named piece of text or HTML that templates output and editors can change without touching code.

faqs.question: What are site settings used for?
faqs.answer: Configuration values read by templates and platform features, such as feature switches, limits and URLs.

faqs.question: Should I store API keys in site settings?
faqs.answer: No. Anything a template can read can end up in the page. Keep secrets in server-side components.

title: Create dependent drop-downs on a Power Pages form
shortDescription: Filter a second drop-down by the first on a basic form, using the Web API to fetch matching rows, with a fallback that needs no code.
fullDescription: Country then city, category then subcategory: dependent choices are a common form need. On Power Pages, lookups can render as drop-downs, and a short script can reload the child's options when the parent changes, using the portal Web API. For lookups, Dataverse's related-records filtering on the form also works with no script at all.
problemStatement: A request form lists 300 subcategories in one drop-down, most of which do not belong to the chosen category, and people pick invalid combinations.
whenToUse: Two-level choices stored as lookups
Forms where an invalid parent and child pair must be prevented
Long child lists that need narrowing
whenNotToUse: Three or more dependent levels on one form, where a guided multistep form is clearer
Relying on client filtering alone to guarantee valid combinations
stepByStepInstructions: Model the child table with a lookup to the parent.
Try related-records filtering with both lookups rendered as drop-downs.
If needed, enable the Web API for the child table and grant read permission.
Add script that reloads the child's options when the parent changes.
Preserve the saved child value on edit forms.
Add a server-side rule that rejects mismatched pairs.
commonMistakes: Loading every child row into one long drop-down.
Forgetting to restore the saved value in edit mode.
No table permission on the child table, so the list is empty.
Trusting the client filter to guarantee valid data.
troubleshooting: If the child list is empty, test the /_api URL in the browser while signed in and read the error.
If the saved value disappears on edit, pass the initial value into the first load.
If the form saves a blank lookup, update the hidden name and entity name fields on change.
If options do not refresh, check the parent's change event fires for a drop-down, not the modal lookup.
seoTitle: Create dependent drop-downs on a Power Pages form
seoDescription: Filter a second drop-down by the first on a basic form, using the Web API to fetch matching rows, with a fallback that needs no code.

faqs.question: Can Power Pages forms have cascading drop-downs?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use lookups rendered as drop-downs with related-records filtering, or reload the child options with script and the Web API.

faqs.question: Do I need the Web API for dependent drop-downs?
faqs.answer: Not always. Form-level lookup filtering or Liquid-rendered JSON can work without it.

faqs.question: How do I keep the selected value on an edit form?
faqs.answer: Read the child's value before reloading options and select it again after the options are rebuilt.

title: Prefill Power Pages form fields from the user, the URL or a parent record
shortDescription: Set default values on a basic form from the signed-in contact, a query string parameter or a parent record, using form metadata first and script only where needed.
fullDescription: Asking visitors to retype what the site already knows makes forms longer and data worse. Basic form metadata can prepopulate a field from the current contact or a fixed value, set values on save, and link a new record to a parent passed in the URL. A few lines of script cover what metadata cannot.
problemStatement: A signed-in customer opening 'New case' has to type their name, email and account again, and the case is not linked to the product page they came from.
whenToUse: Create forms for signed-in users
Forms opened from a parent record or a specific product or event
Hidden values such as source or campaign
whenNotToUse: Trusting prefilled hidden values for security decisions
Overwriting values on edit forms
stepByStepInstructions: List which fields the site already knows for a signed-in user or from the entry link.
Add basic form metadata to prepopulate those fields from the current portal user.
Use Set Value On Save for hidden values such as source and submitted date.
Configure the entity reference from the query string to link to a parent record.
Add script for remaining query string values, only filling empty fields.
Enforce important values on the server.
commonMistakes: Reaching for script before form metadata.
Disabling a prefilled input so its value is not saved.
Prefilling on edit forms and overwriting saved data.
Trusting URL parameters for sensitive columns.
troubleshooting: If the field stays empty, check the metadata's attribute logical name and that the user is signed in.
If the parent link is not set, confirm the relationship name and the query string parameter name.
If a lookup shows blank after script prefill, set the name and entity name inputs as well as the ID.
If a value reverts after a validation error, set it only when the field is empty on load.
seoTitle: Prefill Power Pages form fields from the user, the URL or a parent record
seoDescription: Set default values on a basic form from the signed-in contact, a query string parameter or a parent record, using form metadata first and script only where needed.

faqs.question: How do I prefill a Power Pages form with the user's details?
faqs.answer: Add basic form metadata for each field with Prepopulate Field set to Current Portal User and the contact column to copy.

faqs.question: Can I pass values to a form in the URL?
faqs.answer: Yes. Read query string parameters with script, or use the form's entity reference setting to link a parent record by ID.

faqs.question: How do I set a hidden value when the form is saved?
faqs.answer: Use Set Value On Save in basic form metadata, which applies the value on the server at save time.

title: Call a Power Automate flow from a Power Pages page
shortDescription: Register a cloud flow with a site, restrict it to web roles, call it from page script with inputs and use the values it returns.
fullDescription: Some page actions need more than a Dataverse write: checking stock in another system, creating a payment link, sending a document. Power Pages can call a cloud flow directly. The flow is registered against the site, limited to chosen web roles, and invoked from script through a site endpoint that carries the visitor's identity.
problemStatement: A page needs live delivery slots from an external API. Calling the API from the browser would expose the key, and writing a row then waiting for a triggered flow is slow and awkward.
whenToUse: Calling external systems without exposing credentials
Server-side logic started by a button on a page
Returning a computed result to the visitor
whenNotToUse: Simple Dataverse creates and updates, where the Web API is faster
Operations longer than about two minutes, which should be asynchronous
stepByStepInstructions: Create a flow with the Power Pages trigger and typed inputs.
End it with Return value(s) to Power Pages.
Register the flow with the site and select the web roles allowed to call it.
Call the flow URL from script with the inputs wrapped in eventData.
Verify identifiers inside the flow before returning or changing data.
Handle errors and disable the button while the call runs.
commonMistakes: Putting an API key in page script instead of calling a flow.
Trusting a contact ID sent by the browser.
Long-running flows called synchronously.
Allowing the Anonymous Users role to trigger a flow that sends email or costs money.
troubleshooting: If the call returns 403, the visitor's web role is not assigned to the flow on the site.
If inputs arrive empty, check the eventData wrapper and that names match the trigger inputs.
If the response cannot be parsed, return text outputs and parse nested JSON strings twice.
If it works in development only, turn the flow on in the target and re-add it under Cloud flows.
seoTitle: Call a Power Automate flow from a Power Pages page
seoDescription: Register a cloud flow with a site, restrict it to web roles, call it from page script with inputs and use the values it returns.

faqs.question: Can a Power Pages site call a Power Automate flow?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the When Power Pages calls a flow trigger, register the flow with the site and call its URL from page script.

faqs.question: Who can trigger the flow?
faqs.answer: Only visitors in the web roles you assign to the flow when adding it to the site.

faqs.question: Can the flow return data to the page?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Return value(s) to Power Pages action sends text, number or boolean outputs back in the response.

title: Take a Power Pages site live: visibility, domain and security checks
shortDescription: The steps from private trial site to public production: convert to production, set visibility, add a custom domain and certificate, run the security scan and tune caching.
fullDescription: A Power Pages site starts private and on a trial. Going live is more than flipping a switch: it needs a production licence state, public visibility, a custom domain with TLS, a review of table permissions and anonymous access, and performance settings such as the content delivery network. Working through a fixed list avoids the classic launch-day surprises.
problemStatement: A site is announced to customers while still private, on a trial about to expire, with the default domain and a table permission that exposes every contact to signed-in users.
whenToUse: First launch of any Power Pages site
Major releases that change permissions or authentication
Periodic health reviews
whenNotToUse: Making the site public before permissions have been reviewed
Skipping the checklist for internal-only sites, which still hold real data
formulaOrCode:
Where: Power Pages home > site > ... > Admin center (Power Platform admin center > Resources > Power Pages sites > site)

1. Licence and state
   Site Details > Convert to production (trial sites stop after 30 days)
   Confirm capacity: authenticated users per site per month and anonymous users per site per month licences
   or pay-as-you-go linked to the environment.
   Application type shown as Production.

2. Site visibility
   Design studio > Security > Site visibility (or admin center > Site visibility)
     Private: only makers and people you list (Entra accounts) can view.  Public: anyone.
   Keep Private through testing. Switch to Public at launch. Only admins or allowed makers can change it
   (tenant setting can restrict who may make sites public).

3. Custom domain and certificate
   Admin center > Custom domains > + Add new
     Upload a TLS certificate (.pfx with password) or select an existing one. Enter www.contoso.com.
     Create the DNS record: CNAME  www  ->  <site>.powerappsportals.com
   After adding: update the identity provider's redirect URLs to the new host, plus any hard-coded links,
   CORS settings on storage, and the Web API allowed origins if used from other sites.
   One custom domain per site. For an apex domain, use Azure Front Door in front of the site.

4. Security review
   Design studio > Security > Run scan (security scan): fix reported issues (headers, exposed tables, libraries).
   Table permissions:
     No Global Read on tables with personal data for Authenticated or Anonymous roles.
     Every list and form has Enable Table Permissions on.
     Anonymous Users role: read only, public reference tables only.
   Web API: Webapi/<table>/fields lists columns explicitly. innererror setting removed or false.
   Authentication: open registration off unless intended. Local sign-in disabled when using an external provider.
   Page permissions: restricted pages have Restrict Read rules for the right web roles.
   HTTP headers (site settings):
     HTTP/X-Frame-Options                 SAMEORIGIN
     HTTP/Content-Security-Policy         script-src 'self' 'nonce' https://trusted.cdn.com; frame-ancestors 'self'
     HTTP/X-Content-Type-Options          nosniff
     HTTP/Strict-Transport-Security       max-age=31536000
   Web application firewall: admin center > Security > Web Application Firewall: Enable (requires CDN).
   IP restrictions: only for sites meant for known networks.
   Minimum TLS and "Maker identity provider" settings as per your policy.

5. Performance
   Admin center > Content Delivery Network: Enable       static files served from edge locations
   Server-side caching is on by default. Header and footer output caching site settings enabled.
   Large images compressed. Lists limited to 10 to 25 rows. Avoid heavy fetchxml in the header.
   Region: the site runs in the environment's region. Check latency from your main audience.

6. Content and SEO
   Page titles and descriptions set. Remove sample pages and lorem text. 404 and access denied pages customised.
   robots.txt: a web file named robots.txt at the site root (Home), partial URL robots.txt.
   Sitemap: add a page that outputs XML with Liquid, or submit key URLs in the search console.
   Head/Bottom content snippet: analytics tags and consent banner script.
   Search: Search/Enabled true, and confirm results respect permissions.

7. Operations
   Diagnostics: admin center > Site actions > Enable diagnostic logging to Azure Blob Storage for errors.
   Site health: Run Site Checker and fix warnings.
   Maintenance: admin center > Enable maintenance mode shows a holding page during big deployments.
   Restart site and Clear cache actions known to the support team.
   Backups: environment backups cover site metadata, since it lives in Dataverse.
   Authentication key: note the expiry date shown in the admin center and renew before it lapses.

8. Launch
   Smoke test as anonymous, as a new registrant and as each web role, on desktop and phone.
   Switch visibility to Public. Test again on the custom domain. Monitor diagnostics for the first days.
stepByStepInstructions: Convert the site to production and confirm licensing.
Review table permissions, anonymous access, Web API settings and registration.
Run the security scan and add security headers.
Add the custom domain and certificate and update identity provider redirect URLs.
Enable the content delivery network and check caching.
Smoke test every role, then set the site to public and monitor.
commonMistakes: Launching on a trial site.
Adding the custom domain without updating sign-in redirect URLs.
Global read permissions left over from development.
Developer error settings left on in production.
troubleshooting: If visitors are asked to sign in with a work account, the site is still private.
If sign-in fails after the domain change, add the new redirect URL at the identity provider.
If pages are slow, enable the CDN and reduce queries in shared templates.
If the site shows an authentication key warning, renew the key in the admin center.
seoTitle: Take a Power Pages site live: visibility, domain and security checks
seoDescription: The steps from private trial site to public production: convert to production, set visibility, add a custom domain and certificate, run the security scan and tune caching.

faqs.question: How do I make a Power Pages site public?
faqs.answer: Change Site visibility from Private to Public in the design studio's Security area or the admin center.

faqs.question: Can a Power Pages site use my own domain?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add a custom domain with a TLS certificate in the admin center and point a CNAME record at the site.

faqs.question: What should I check before launch?
faqs.answer: Production state and licences, table permissions and anonymous access, the security scan, custom domain and sign-in redirects, and CDN and caching.

title: Onboard external users with Power Pages invitations
shortDescription: Send invitation codes that link a known contact to their sign-in, assign web roles and an account automatically on redemption, and automate the whole cycle.
fullDescription: For partner and customer sites, people should not be able to register and see data just by signing up. Invitations tie a contact you created to whichever identity they sign in with. On redemption the invitation can grant web roles and associate an account, so access is decided by you, not by the registration form.
problemStatement: Open registration creates new, empty contacts unconnected to the customer's account, so new users see nothing and staff fix every one by hand.
whenToUse: Partner and customer sites where access is granted, not self-claimed
Bulk onboarding of contacts from a customer list
Giving roles and account association at first sign-in
whenNotToUse: Public community sites where anyone may join
Sending codes to shared mailboxes
formulaOrCode:
Site settings
  Authentication/Registration/Enabled                  true
  Authentication/Registration/OpenRegistrationEnabled  false      no self sign-up
  Authentication/Registration/InvitationEnabled        true
  Authentication/Registration/RequiresInvitation       true       (where present) sign-up only with a code

Create an invitation (Portal Management > Contacts > select contact > Create Invitation, or Invitations > New)
  Name: Onboard Priya Shah
  Type: Single (one contact, one redemption) | Group (one code, many redemptions up to Maximum Redemptions)
  Invited Contact(s): the contact row
  Owner / Inviter: staff user (used in the email)
  Expiry Date: 14 days ahead
  Assign to Account: the customer account      sets the contact's parent customer on redemption
  Assign to Web Roles: Customer User (and Customer Admin where relevant)
  Execute Workflow on Redeeming Contact: optional classic workflow
  Invitation Code: generated automatically

Send it
  Invitation > Flow / Process > Run workflow "Send Invitation" (classic workflow installed with the site).
  Edit that workflow's email: sender, wording and the link
    https://www.contoso.com/register?invitation=<Invitation Code>
  Or send from a cloud flow (below) for better templates.

What the user does
  Opens the link > Redeem invitation page with the code filled in > signs in or signs up with the identity
  provider > the sign-in is linked to the invited contact > roles and account applied > invitation status
  becomes Redeemed.

Automate with a cloud flow
  Trigger: Dataverse > When a row is added: Contacts, filter: cr1a2_portalaccess eq true
           (or a button flow / approval from an access request list)
  Add a new row: Invitations (adx_invitation)
    Name: Onboard @{fullname}        Type: Single (756150000)
    Invite Contact (adx_invitecontact): contacts(<contact id>)
    Expiry Date: addDays(utcNow(), 14)
    Assign To Account (adx_assigntoaccount): accounts(<parent account id>)
  Relate rows: Invitation <> Web Roles (adx_invitation_webrole or the relationship shown in your environment)
    with the Customer User role
  Get the row again to read adx_invitationcode
  Send an email (V2) from a shared mailbox:
    Subject: Your access to the Contoso customer site
    Body: link with the code, expiry date, a named contact for help.
  Update the contact: cr1a2_invitedon = utcNow()

Reminders and expiry
  Scheduled flow daily: Invitations where statuscode is Sent and expiry within 3 days and not redeemed >
  one reminder. Expired and unredeemed: notify the account manager.

Bulk onboarding
  Import contacts (Excel or dataflow) with cr1a2_portalaccess = true. The flow above issues invitations.
  Throttle email sending with low concurrency.

Offboarding
  Remove web roles from the contact (Relate/Unrelate rows) and, for a full block, delete the contact's
  External Identity row or deactivate the contact. Flow trigger: contact deactivated or account relationship ended.

Without invitations (Entra External ID with contact mapping)
  Create contacts in advance with the right email, account and web roles. Enable "Contact mapping with email".
  When the person signs up with that verified email, they are linked to the existing contact and already
  have access. Simpler for users. Requires verified emails at the provider.

Audit
  Invitations view: Redeemed, Sent, Expired counts. Contact > Web Roles subgrid shows current access.
  Review external access per account twice a year with the account's admin.
stepByStepInstructions: Turn off open registration and enable invitations in site settings.
Create contacts with the right account before inviting.
Create invitations that assign web roles and the account.
Send the invitation link by email with an expiry date.
Automate creation, reminders and expiry with flows.
Remove roles and identities when access should end.
commonMistakes: Open registration left on beside invitations.
Invitations with no web roles, leaving users with no access after redemption.
No expiry date on codes.
Never removing access for people who leave the customer.
troubleshooting: If redemption creates a new contact, the user registered without the code. Merge and re-link, and require invitations.
If the user has no access after redeeming, check the invitation's web roles and the account assignment.
If the code is rejected, it has expired or reached its maximum redemptions.
If emails are not sent, the classic workflow is off or its sender has no mailbox. Use the cloud flow.
seoTitle: Onboard external users with Power Pages invitations
seoDescription: Send invitation codes that link a known contact to their sign-in, assign web roles and an account automatically on redemption, and automate the whole cycle.

faqs.question: What is a Power Pages invitation?
faqs.answer: A record with a code that links an existing contact to the identity they sign in with, optionally granting web roles and an account.

faqs.question: How do I stop self-registration on my site?
faqs.answer: Set OpenRegistrationEnabled to false and enable invitations, so only people with a valid code can register.

faqs.question: Can invitations assign web roles automatically?
faqs.answer: Yes. Roles listed on the invitation are given to the contact when the code is redeemed.

title: Put a Power Pages site in source control with the PAC CLI
shortDescription: Download a site's pages, templates and settings as files, edit and review them in Git, upload changes, and move the site between environments with deployment profiles.
fullDescription: A Power Pages site is stored as rows in Dataverse. The PAC CLI turns those rows into a folder of HTML, CSS, JavaScript and YAML files, which makes changes reviewable and repeatable. Deployment profiles swap environment-specific values such as site settings during upload. Sites using the enhanced data model can also travel inside solutions.
problemStatement: Site changes are made directly in production because nobody can say what differs between the development and live sites, and there is no history of who changed a template.
whenToUse: Teams with more than one person editing a site
Promoting a site through development, test and production
Editing templates in a code editor with search and diff
whenNotToUse: Uploading over a target someone is editing in the studio at the same time
Expecting table data such as products or cases to move with the site
formulaOrCode:
Set up
  pac auth create --name PagesDev --environment https://contoso-dev.crm.dynamics.com
  pac pages list
      Index  Website Id                             Friendly Name      Model Version
      [1]    8a7b6c5d-....                          Customer Portal    Enhanced (2)

Download
  pac pages download --path ./site --webSiteId 8a7b6c5d-... --modelVersion 2 --overwrite
  (modelVersion 1 = standard data model, 2 = enhanced data model)

Folder layout (./site/customer-portal)
  web-pages/<page>/<Page>.webpage.yml                  page properties
  web-pages/<page>/content-pages/<Page>.en-US.webpage.copy.html      page content (HTML and Liquid)
                                 <Page>.en-US.webpage.custom_css.css
                                 <Page>.en-US.webpage.custom_javascript.js
  web-templates/<name>/<Name>.webtemplate.source.html
  content-snippets/<name>/<Name>.en-US.contentsnippet.value.html
  basic-forms/, advanced-forms/ (multistep), lists/, web-files/ (css, js, images)
  sitesetting.yml, webrole.yml, table-permissions/*.yml, page-templates/, sitemarker.yml, website.yml
  .portalconfig/                                       manifest used to detect changes. Commit it.

Edit and upload
  Open the folder in Visual Studio Code (the Power Platform Tools extension adds Liquid support and icons).
  pac pages upload --path ./site/customer-portal --modelVersion 2
  Only changed files are sent, based on the manifest. Then clear the site cache:
  design studio > Preview > or Sync, or admin center > Site actions > Restart for stubborn cases.

Git
  git init && git add -A && git commit -m "Baseline of customer portal"
  .gitignore: nothing special is required. Do not commit certificates or exported secrets.
  Branch per change, pull request, review the diff of templates and YAML.
  Refresh from the environment before starting, since colleagues may have used the studio:
    pac pages download --path ./site --webSiteId <id> --modelVersion 2 --overwrite && git status

Deployment profiles (environment-specific values)
  ./site/customer-portal/deployment-profiles/test.deployment.yml
    adx_sitesetting:
      - adx_sitesettingid: 3f0c....            # id from sitesetting.yml
        adx_value: https://test-api.contoso.com
        adx_name: Integration/ApiUrl
      - adx_sitesettingid: 9b1d....
        adx_value: "false"
        adx_name: Authentication/Registration/OpenRegistrationEnabled
  Upload with the profile:
    pac auth select --name PagesTest
    pac pages upload --path ./site/customer-portal --deploymentProfile test --modelVersion 2

First move to a new environment
  1. Deploy the Dataverse solution first: tables, forms, views, flows, environment variables.
  2. Target environment: create a site (same template family) or, for the enhanced model, import a solution
     containing the site components.
  3. pac pages upload with the profile for that environment.
  4. Bind or check: identity provider settings, custom domain, cloud flow registrations, table permissions'
     web role links, and site visibility.

Solutions route (enhanced data model)
  Add the site and its components to a solution (Solutions > Add existing > Site) and deploy managed with
  pipelines. Use the CLI for developer editing and diffing, solutions for promotion.

Pipeline (Azure DevOps or GitHub)
  Steps: install PAC CLI > pac auth create with a service principal > pac pages upload --deploymentProfile prod
  The application user needs a role with access to the site's tables (System Administrator is typical).

Bootstrap version
  pac pages bootstrap-migrate --path ./site/customer-portal      converts Bootstrap 3 markup to 5 for older sites.

What does not travel
  Business data rows, contacts and their web role assignments, authentication secrets entered in the
  target, and custom domain configuration.
stepByStepInstructions: Authenticate the PAC CLI and list sites to get the website ID and data model version.
Download the site to a folder and commit it as a baseline.
Edit files in a code editor and upload changes.
Create deployment profiles for values that differ per environment.
Deploy the Dataverse solution first, then upload the site with the target's profile.
Automate uploads in a pipeline with a service principal.
commonMistakes: Uploading stale local files over newer studio changes.
Not committing the .portalconfig manifest.
Moving the site before the tables and forms it depends on.
Keeping environment-specific URLs in the main site settings instead of a profile.
troubleshooting: If upload reports nothing to change, the manifest is out of step. Download again or delete the target entry in .portalconfig.
If changes do not appear on the site, clear the cache or restart the site.
If download fails on model version, pass the version shown by pac pages list.
If forms break in the target, the Dataverse form or view names differ. Deploy the solution first.
seoTitle: Put a Power Pages site in source control with the PAC CLI
seoDescription: Download a site's pages, templates and settings as files, edit and review them in Git, upload changes, and move the site between environments with deployment profiles.

faqs.question: How do I export a Power Pages site?
faqs.answer: Use pac pages download with the website ID to save the site's pages, templates and settings as files.

faqs.question: How do I move a Power Pages site to another environment?
faqs.answer: Deploy the Dataverse solution, then upload the site files with pac pages upload and a deployment profile, or use solutions for enhanced data model sites.

faqs.question: What are deployment profiles?
faqs.answer: YAML files that override values such as site settings for a specific environment during upload.

title: Poll for a result with Do until, with a safe timeout
shortDescription: Wait for a job, file or status to be ready by checking on an interval, with the loop limits set deliberately and a clear path when time runs out.
fullDescription: Some systems answer later: an export job, a document conversion, a record waiting for another process. Do until repeats actions until a condition is true, but its default limits of 60 iterations and one hour end the loop silently and let the flow carry on as if it had succeeded. A polling loop needs explicit limits and a check after it finishes.
problemStatement: A flow starts an export, loops until the status is Complete, then downloads the file. When the export takes longer than usual the loop gives up quietly and the download step fails with a confusing error.
whenToUse: Waiting for long-running API jobs
Waiting for a file or record to appear
Any check-then-wait logic
whenNotToUse: Events that have a trigger or webhook, which need no polling
Waits of many days, where a scheduled flow that checks a queue is more robust
formulaOrCode:
Structure
  Initialize variable  varStatus (String) = ""
  Initialize variable  varAttempts (Integer) = 0

  Do until:   @or(equals(variables('varStatus'), 'Complete'), equals(variables('varStatus'), 'Failed'))
    Change limits:   Count 40        Timeout PT20M
      HTTP (or Get item, Get file metadata ...): read the job status
      Set variable varStatus = body('HTTP')?['status']
      Increment variable varAttempts
      Condition: varStatus is not Complete and not Failed
        Yes: Delay 30 seconds

  Condition (after the loop): varStatus equals Complete
    Yes: continue with the download
    No:  Terminate, Failed, message: Export did not finish. Last status '@{variables('varStatus')}' after @{variables('varAttempts')} checks.

How Do until behaves
  The condition is evaluated AFTER each pass, so the actions always run at least once.
  It stops when the condition is true, OR Count is reached, OR Timeout elapses. In the last two cases the
  loop is marked Succeeded and the flow continues. Always test the outcome after the loop.
  Defaults: Count 60, Timeout PT1H. Maximum Count 5,000. Timeout up to the flow's own run limit (30 days).
  Timeout uses ISO 8601: PT30S, PT15M, PT2H, P1D.
  The timeout is checked between iterations. One slow action can overrun it.

Choosing limits
  Expected duration 5 minutes, worst case 15: Delay 30 seconds, Count 40, Timeout PT20M.
  Count x Delay should be a little more than Timeout, so Timeout is the effective limit.

Back off instead of a fixed delay
  Delay (seconds): @{min(300, mul(15, variables('varAttempts')))}
  Checks at 15s, 30s, 45s ... capped at 5 minutes. Fewer calls for slow jobs, quick answers for fast ones.

Honour Retry-After
  If the status call returns a Retry-After header:
  Delay: @{int(coalesce(outputs('HTTP')?['headers']?['Retry-After'], '30'))}

Errors inside the loop
  A failed action fails the loop. To keep polling through transient errors:
    Put the status call in a Scope. Add an action after it with run after "has failed, has timed out"
    that does nothing but set varLastError. The Delay follows with run after on both paths.
  Stop early on a real failure by including Failed in the loop's condition.

Wait for a SharePoint file to exist
  Do until: @equals(variables('varFound'), true)       Count 20, Timeout PT10M
    Get files (properties only): Filter Query FileLeafRef eq 'export-@{variables('jobId')}.csv', Top Count 1
    Set variable varFound = @{greater(length(body('Get_files')?['value']), 0)}
    Condition varFound is false > Delay 30 seconds

Wait for a record to change
  Prefer a trigger with a trigger condition on the status column, which uses no polling.
  When the wait must sit inside one run: the same loop with Get item and the status value.

Asynchronous APIs (202 Accepted with a Location header)
  The HTTP action follows the 202 pattern by itself when "Asynchronous Pattern" is On in its settings:
  it polls the Location URL until the final response. No Do until needed.

Cost
  Each pass counts its actions against the daily request allowance: 4 actions x 40 passes = 160.
  Longer delays reduce this.
stepByStepInstructions: Initialise a status variable and an attempts counter.
Add a Do until whose condition covers both success and failure states.
Set Count and Timeout to match the worst acceptable wait.
Read the status, update the variable and delay only when not finished.
After the loop, test whether the success state was reached.
Fail the run with a clear message when it was not.
commonMistakes: Leaving default limits and assuming the loop always finishes.
No check after the loop, so later actions run against missing data.
A fixed one-second delay that burns thousands of actions.
Looping on a condition that can never become true after a failure.
troubleshooting: If the loop exits early, raise Timeout and Count and check which limit was hit in the run history.
If the flow continues after an unfinished job, add the condition after the loop.
If the loop never ends, include failure states in the condition.
If transient errors stop polling, wrap the status call in a scope and handle its failure.
seoTitle: Poll for a result with Do until, with a safe timeout
seoDescription: Wait for a job, file or status to be ready by checking on an interval, with the loop limits set deliberately and a clear path when time runs out.

faqs.question: Why does my Do until loop stop before the condition is true?
faqs.answer: It reached its Count or Timeout limit. The defaults are 60 iterations and one hour, and the flow continues afterwards.

faqs.question: How do I wait in a flow until something is ready?
faqs.answer: Use Do until with a status check and a Delay inside, explicit limits, and a condition after the loop.

faqs.question: Does Do until check the condition first?
faqs.answer: No. It runs the actions once, then evaluates the condition after each pass.

title: Generate a PDF from a Word template in a flow
shortDescription: Fill a Word template's content controls with record data, including a repeating table, convert the result to PDF and save it beside the record.
fullDescription: Letters, certificates and summaries are easier to maintain as a Word document than as HTML in a flow. The Word Online connector fills plain text and repeating content controls in a template, and the OneDrive Convert file action turns the result into a PDF. Template changes are then made in Word by the business, not in the flow.
problemStatement: An approval letter is built from concatenated HTML in a flow. Every wording change needs a developer, and the output never quite matches the brand template.
whenToUse: Letters, certificates, quotes and summaries from record data
Documents with a table of line items
PDF copies filed with a request
whenNotToUse: Standard-licence-only environments, since Word Online (Business) is a premium connector
Pixel-perfect designs with complex layouts, where a dedicated document service fits better
formulaOrCode:
1. Prepare the template (Word desktop)
  File > Options > Customize Ribbon > tick Developer.
  Developer tab > Design Mode. For each value: place the cursor > Plain Text Content Control > Properties >
    Title: RequestNumber (also set Tag). Titles become the field names in the flow. No spaces is safest.
  Repeating rows: build a table with a header row and ONE data row. Put a plain text control in each cell
    (Item, Qty, Price). Select the whole data row > Repeating Section Content Control > Title: Lines.
  Images: Picture Content Control with a title (filled with base64 image content).
  Save as .docx in a SharePoint library or OneDrive folder the flow account can read: /Templates/ApprovalLetter.docx

2. Fill it
  Word Online (Business) > Populate a Microsoft Word template
    Location: SharePoint site (or OneDrive)      Document Library: Documents      File: /Templates/ApprovalLetter.docx
    After selecting the file, the controls appear as fields:
      RequestNumber: REQ-@{triggerOutputs()?['body/ID']}
      Requester:     @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Author/DisplayName']}
      ApprovedOn:    @{convertFromUtc(utcNow(),'Eastern Standard Time','d MMMM yyyy')}
      Amount:        @{formatNumber(triggerOutputs()?['body/Amount'],'C2','en-US')}
      Lines:         switch to "input entire array" and pass an array whose keys match the inner control titles

  Build the Lines array with Select
    From: body('Get_items_lines')?['value']
    Map:  Item  = item()?['Title']
          Qty   = string(item()?['Quantity'])
          Price = formatNumber(item()?['UnitPrice'],'C2','en-US')
  All values are text. Format numbers and dates before passing them.

  Dynamic template path: when File is an expression, the fields are not shown. Pass a JSON object in the
  "dynamicFileSchema" input instead, keyed by the controls' internal IDs. Simpler: one flow branch per template,
  or keep titles identical across templates and select the file with a Switch.

3. Save the Word file
  OneDrive for Business > Create file
    Folder Path: /Generated        File Name: REQ-@{triggerOutputs()?['body/ID']}.docx
    File Content: body('Populate_a_Microsoft_Word_template')

4. Convert to PDF
  OneDrive for Business > Convert file
    File: outputs('Create_file')?['body/Id']        Target type: PDF
  (Word Online also has "Convert Word Document to PDF" for files already in SharePoint or OneDrive.)

5. File the PDF and clean up
  SharePoint > Create file
    Folder Path: /Shared Documents/Requests/REQ-@{ID}        File Name: Approval letter REQ-@{ID}.pdf
    File Content: body('Convert_file')
  OneDrive > Delete file: the temporary .docx
  SharePoint > Update file properties (optional): RequestId, DocumentType = Approval letter

6. Send it
  Office 365 Outlook > Send an email (V2) > Attachments
    Name: Approval letter REQ-@{ID}.pdf        Content: body('Convert_file')

Limits and behaviour
  Supported controls: plain text, repeating section, picture, check box (in newer versions). Rich text
  controls, drop-downs and date pickers are not filled.
  Controls inside headers, footers and text boxes may not be detected. Keep them in the body.
  A control left empty shows nothing in the output. Supply a dash for optional values where blank looks wrong.
  Line breaks in a plain text control: allow carriage returns in the control's properties.
  File size up to about 10 MB for populate, and conversion has its own size limits.

Without premium
  Build HTML with Compose and save as .html, then OneDrive Convert file to PDF. Layout control is limited,
  but all connectors are standard.
stepByStepInstructions: Add titled plain text content controls to a Word template and a repeating section around the table row.
Store the template in a library the flow account can read.
Populate the template with formatted text values and an array for the repeating section.
Create the Word file in OneDrive and convert it to PDF.
Save the PDF with the record and delete the temporary file.
Attach or link the PDF in the notification.
commonMistakes: Using rich text or legacy form fields, which are not filled.
Passing numbers and dates unformatted.
Wrapping the whole table instead of only the data row in the repeating section.
Leaving temporary Word files to pile up.
troubleshooting: If fields do not appear in the action, the controls lack titles or the file path is dynamic.
If the table shows one row, the repeating section does not wrap the row or the array keys do not match the control titles.
If the PDF conversion fails, create the file in OneDrive first and pass its ID.
If the template seems out of date, the flow caches the schema. Re-select the file in the action.
seoTitle: Generate a PDF from a Word template in a flow
seoDescription: Fill a Word template's content controls with record data, including a repeating table, convert the result to PDF and save it beside the record.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate populate Word template PDF

faqs.question: How do I fill a Word template from Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Add titled content controls to the document and use the Word Online (Business) action Populate a Microsoft Word template.

faqs.question: How do I convert the document to PDF?
faqs.answer: Save the populated file to OneDrive and use the Convert file action with target type PDF.

faqs.question: Can the template include a table with a variable number of rows?
faqs.answer: Yes. Wrap the data row in a repeating section content control and pass an array.

title: Read large Excel tables reliably in a flow
shortDescription: Get past the 256-row default, filter and select columns at the source, handle dates and blanks, and find one row by key without reading the whole table.
fullDescription: List rows present in a table returns only the first 256 rows unless pagination is enabled, hands back dates as serial numbers and supports just a limited filter syntax. Knowing these limits, and the settings that address them, makes Excel a workable source for a few thousand rows.
problemStatement: A flow imports a 3,000-row spreadsheet but only 256 rows arrive, dates look like 45978, and the run takes twenty minutes because it loops over every row to find one.
whenToUse: Importing or reconciling spreadsheets kept in SharePoint or OneDrive
Looking up a value in a reference workbook
Scheduled processing of a maintained Excel table
whenNotToUse: Workbooks edited by many people while the flow writes to them
Data sets beyond tens of thousands of rows, which belong in a list or database
formulaOrCode:
Prerequisites
  The data is formatted as a TABLE (Insert > Table) with a name such as tblOrders.
  The file is .xlsx in OneDrive for Business or a SharePoint library. No merged cells in the table.
  File size up to 25 MB for the connector.

Action
  Excel Online (Business) > List rows present in a table
    Location / Document Library / File / Table: pick from the lists
    Filter Query:   Status eq 'Open'
    Order By:       OrderDate desc
    Top Count:      (empty)
    Skip Count:     (empty)
    Select Query:   OrderId,Customer,OrderDate,Amount,Status
    DateTime Format: ISO 8601            (advanced parameter: dates arrive as 2026-11-20T00:00:00.000Z)
  Settings > Pagination: On        Threshold: 5000 (up to 100,000 with premium-level limits)

Filter Query rules (narrower than SharePoint)
  One condition only, or simple and/or in newer versions. Operators: eq, ne, contains, startswith, endswith.
    Customer eq 'Contoso'
    contains(Customer, 'Cont')
  No gt/lt on dates or numbers in many tenants. Filter those afterwards with Filter array:
    @greater(float(item()?['Amount']), 1000)
    @greaterOrEquals(item()?['OrderDate'], addDays(utcNow(), -30))
  Column names with spaces: use the header exactly in Select Query. In Filter Query spaces may fail:
  rename headers to single words where you can.

Find one row by key
  Excel Online (Business) > Get a row
    Key Column: OrderId        Key Value: @{triggerBody()?['orderId']}
  Returns the first match or fails with 404 when there is none. Configure run after "has failed" for not found.
  Key values are compared as text.

Values arrive as strings
  Number:  float(item()?['Amount'])               blank cells are "" so guard them:
           float(if(empty(item()?['Amount']), '0', item()?['Amount']))
  Date without ISO format (serial number 45978):
           addDays('1899-12-30', int(item()?['OrderDate']), 'yyyy-MM-dd')
  Boolean: equals(toLower(item()?['Active']), 'true')

Shape without loops
  Select: From body('List_rows_present_in_a_table')?['value']
          Map: id = item()?['OrderId'], amount = float(...), date = item()?['OrderDate']
  Filter array for conditions the connector cannot do. Then a single loop only over rows that need action.

Dynamic file (path chosen at run time)
  The File field needs the file's ID, not its path:
    SharePoint > Get file metadata using path > Id            or the trigger's file identifier
  Table: type the table name as a custom value.
  With a dynamic file the designer cannot show columns: reference them as item()?['ColumnName'].
  For files that arrive without a table: Excel > Create table (Range A1:F5000, columns from headers), or run
  an Office Script that creates the table and returns its name.

Avoid locking and stale reads
  The connector reads the saved copy. Recent edits in the desktop app may not be saved yet.
  Writes (Add a row, Update a row) can fail with a lock when someone has the file open in desktop Excel.
  Ask users to work in Excel for the web, or process a copy:
    SharePoint > Copy file to a "processing" folder, then read the copy.

Throughput
  Excel Online connector: about 100 calls per 60 seconds per connection. Updating rows one at a time
  is slow. For hundreds of updates use an Office Script that takes an array and writes it in one call.
stepByStepInstructions: Format the data as a named table in a workbook stored in SharePoint or OneDrive.
Turn on pagination with a threshold above the row count.
Filter and select columns at the source where the connector allows.
Request ISO 8601 dates and convert numbers from text.
Use Get a row for single lookups by key.
Shape results with Select and Filter array before any loop.
commonMistakes: Leaving pagination off and processing only 256 rows.
Looping over all rows to find one.
Treating numeric and date cells as typed values.
Writing to a workbook that people have open in desktop Excel.
troubleshooting: If only 256 rows come back, enable Pagination in the action's settings.
If the filter is rejected, simplify to one condition and move the remainder to Filter array.
If dates are numbers, set DateTime Format to ISO 8601 or convert the serial number.
If the table list is empty, the range is not a table or the file is .xls or .csv.
seoTitle: Read large Excel tables reliably in a flow
seoDescription: Get past the 256-row default, filter and select columns at the source, handle dates and blanks, and find one row by key without reading the whole table.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate Excel list rows present in a table

faqs.question: Why does Power Automate return only 256 rows from Excel?
faqs.answer: That is the default page size. Turn on Pagination in the action settings and set a higher threshold.

faqs.question: Can I filter Excel rows in the List rows action?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a limited OData filter such as a single eq or contains condition. Do other filtering with Filter array.

faqs.question: How do I get one Excel row by ID?
faqs.answer: Use Get a row with the key column and key value.

title: Run an Office Script from a flow to process Excel in one call
shortDescription: Pass data into a workbook script and get results back: write hundreds of rows at once, read a formatted range, refresh formulas or tidy a sheet.
fullDescription: The Excel connector works a row at a time. An Office Script runs inside the workbook and can read or write thousands of cells in a single action. A flow passes parameters such as an array of rows, the script does the work, and returns a value the flow can use. It is the practical way to do bulk or formatting work in Excel from a flow.
problemStatement: Writing 800 rows to a report workbook with Add a row into a table takes over ten minutes and regularly hits throttling.
whenToUse: Bulk writes and updates to a workbook
Reading data that is not in a table, or needs clean-up first
Formatting, sorting or clearing a report sheet
whenNotToUse: Workbooks outside OneDrive or SharePoint
Tenants where Office Scripts are disabled by the administrator
stepByStepInstructions: Write an Office Script whose main function takes parameters and returns a value.
Read and write ranges in bulk inside the script.
Shape the flow's data into an array with Select and pass it as a JSON string.
Call Run script with the workbook and parameters.
Use the returned result in later actions.
Store production scripts in SharePoint and run them with a service account.
commonMistakes: Looping in the flow and calling the script once per row.
Cell-by-cell reads and writes inside the script.
Scripts kept in a personal OneDrive for a team process.
Passing arrays whose value order does not match the table's columns.
troubleshooting: If the script is not listed, the connection's user cannot see it. Share it or move it to SharePoint.
If the run times out, send fewer rows per call or replace per-cell operations with range operations.
If parameters do not appear, they are not declared on main with supported types.
If the action is unavailable, ask the administrator to enable Office Scripts and their use in Power Automate.
seoTitle: Run an Office Script from a flow to process Excel in one call
seoDescription: Pass data into a workbook script and get results back: write hundreds of rows at once, read a formatted range, refresh formulas or tidy a sheet.

faqs.question: Can Power Automate run an Excel script?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Excel Online (Business) connector has a Run script action that executes an Office Script with parameters.

faqs.question: How do I write many rows to Excel quickly from a flow?
faqs.answer: Pass the rows as an array to an Office Script that calls addRows or setValues once.

faqs.question: Can an Office Script return data to the flow?
faqs.answer: Yes. Whatever main returns is available in the action's result output.

title: Call Microsoft Graph and other APIs with app credentials from a flow
shortDescription: Register an app, grant application permissions and call an API from the HTTP action using its built-in Entra authentication, with the secret held outside the flow.
fullDescription: When no connector action exists, the HTTP action can call any REST API. For Microsoft APIs it can obtain a token itself using an app registration's client ID and secret or certificate. The call then runs as the application, independent of any user, which suits background automation as long as the permissions are kept narrow.
problemStatement: A flow must read sign-in activity and update group settings that no connector exposes. Using a person's delegated connection breaks when they leave or their password changes.
whenToUse: Graph or Azure endpoints with no connector action
Background jobs that should not depend on a user account
Calling your own APIs protected by Entra ID
whenNotToUse: Broad application permissions such as Sites.FullControl.All when a scoped permission exists
Environments where the premium HTTP connector is blocked by DLP
formulaOrCode:
1. App registration (Microsoft Entra admin center) App registrations > New registration: "Flow - Group maintenance", single tenant, no redirect URI. API permissions > Add > Microsoft Graph > Application permissions Group.Read.All, User.Read.All only what the flow needs Grant admin consent. Certificates & secrets > New client secret (12 months) > copy the VALUE once. Note: Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID. 2. Keep the secret out of the flow Environment variables in the solution: cnt_GraphTenantId (text), cnt_GraphClientId (text), cnt_GraphClientSecret (Secret, Azure Key Vault) Read the secret with Dataverse > Perform an unbound action > RetrieveEnvironmentVariableSecretValue, Secure Outputs on. 3. HTTP action with built-in authentication HTTP Method: GET URI: https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups?$filter=groupTypes/any(c:c eq 'Unified')&$select=id,displayName,createdDateTime&$top=100 Headers: ConsistencyLevel: eventual (needed for some advanced queries with $count) Authentication: Active Directory OAuth Authority: https://login.microsoftonline.com Tenant: the Graph Tenant Id environment variable, picked from dynamic content Audience: https://graph.microsoft.com Client ID: the Graph Client Id environment variable, picked from dynamic content Credential Type: Secret Secret: @{outputs('Get_secret')?['body/EnvironmentVariableSecretValue']} Settings: Secure Inputs: On The action requests and caches the token. No separate token call is needed. Result: body('HTTP')?['value'] next page: body('HTTP')?['@odata.nextLink'] Audience per API Microsoft Graph https://graph.microsoft.com SharePoint REST https://contoso.sharepoint.com Dataverse Web API https://contoso.crm.dynamics.com Azure Resource Manager https://management.azure.com Your own API api:// (expose an app role and assign it to the client app) 4. POST example Method: POST URI: https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/@{variables('userId')}/sendMail Headers: Content-Type: application/json Body: { "message": { "subject": "Access review due", "body": { "contentType": "HTML", "content": "

Review your group by Friday.

" }, "toRecipients": [ { "emailAddress": { "address": "owner@contoso.com" } } ] }, "saveToSentItems": false } (needs Mail.Send application permission, ideally restricted to specific mailboxes with an application access policy) 5. Certificate instead of a secret Credential Type: Certificate > Pfx: base64 of the .pfx from Key Vault > Password. Longer lived and preferred by many security teams. 6. Manual token request (non-Microsoft OAuth 2.0 APIs) HTTP POST https://auth.vendor.com/oauth/token Headers: Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded Body: grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=@{...}&client_secret=@{encodeUriComponent(...)}&scope=api.read Token: body('Get_token')?['access_token'] Next call header: Authorization: Bearer @{body('Get_token')?['access_token']} Secure Inputs and Outputs on both actions. 7. Alternatives that avoid your own app registration "Send a Microsoft Graph HTTP request" actions on the Teams, Outlook and Groups connectors: delegated, limited to certain Graph segments, no secret to manage. HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID (preauthorized) connector: delegated calls as the connection user. Custom connector with OAuth: reusable actions and DLP classification by host. 8. Errors 401 invalid audience or expired secret. 403 permission not granted or consent missing. 429 throttled: keep the default retry policy, honour Retry-After. Track the secret's expiry date and renew before it lapses: a calendar reminder or a scheduled flow that reads application passwordCredentials through Graph.
stepByStepInstructions: Register an application and grant only the application permissions required.
Store tenant ID, client ID and secret as environment variables, with the secret in Key Vault.
Add an HTTP action with Active Directory OAuth authentication and the correct audience.
Turn on secure inputs and outputs for actions that handle the secret or token.
Handle paging, throttling and permission errors.
Record the secret's expiry and renew it ahead of time.
commonMistakes: Typing the secret into the action.
Granting far wider permissions than needed.
Using the wrong audience, so the token is rejected.
Forgetting that secrets expire.
troubleshooting: If you get 401, check the audience matches the API's resource and the secret is current.
If you get 403, grant admin consent and confirm you added application, not delegated, permissions.
If the HTTP action is unavailable, a DLP policy blocks it. Request an exception with endpoint filtering.
If results are incomplete, follow the nextLink until it is absent.
seoTitle: Call Microsoft Graph and other APIs with app credentials from a flow
seoDescription: Register an app, grant application permissions and call an API from the HTTP action using its built-in Entra authentication, with the secret held outside the flow.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate HTTP OAuth client credentials Graph

faqs.question: How do I call Microsoft Graph from Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use the HTTP action with Active Directory OAuth authentication and an app registration, or a connector's Send a Microsoft Graph HTTP request action.

faqs.question: Where should I store the client secret?
faqs.answer: In Azure Key Vault, referenced by a secret environment variable, and read it at run time with secure outputs.

faqs.question: What is the audience value?
faqs.answer: The resource the token is for, such as https://graph.microsoft.com for Graph or your Dataverse URL for the Web API.

title: Page through an API with a next link in a flow
shortDescription: Collect every page from a REST API that returns results in pages, using a Do until loop on the next link, offset counters or cursor tokens.
fullDescription: Connector actions page for you when pagination is enabled. The plain HTTP action does not: it returns one page and a pointer to the next. A loop that follows the pointer and merges each page into an array collects the full result, as long as it has a stop condition and a limit.
problemStatement: A Graph query should return 1,400 users, but the flow processes only the first 100 because the response is paged and nothing follows the next link.
whenToUse: Microsoft Graph, Dataverse Web API and other OData APIs called with HTTP
Vendor APIs using page numbers, offsets or cursors
Exports that must be complete
whenNotToUse: Connector actions that already support the Pagination setting
Pulling very large data sets into flow memory, where a dataflow or export API is better
formulaOrCode:
A. OData next link (Graph, Dataverse, SharePoint REST)
  Initialize variable  varUrl (String) = https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users?$select=id,displayName,mail&$top=999
  Initialize variable  varAll (Array) = []

  Do until:  @empty(variables('varUrl'))          Limits: Count 100, Timeout PT30M
    HTTP  GET  @{variables('varUrl')}             (authentication as usual)
    Compose Merge:  @union(variables('varAll'), body('HTTP')?['value'])
    Set variable varAll = @{outputs('Merge')}
    Set variable varUrl = @{coalesce(body('HTTP')?['@odata.nextLink'], '')}

  After the loop: length(variables('varAll'))

  Notes
    A variable cannot reference itself in Set variable, hence the Compose in between.
    union() removes exact duplicate objects. That is harmless for rows with IDs. To keep true duplicates,
    use an Append to array variable inside an Apply to each instead (slower).
    Dataverse: add header  Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=5000  and follow @odata.nextLink the same way.
    SharePoint REST (verbose): next link is d.__next. With odata=nometadata it is odata.nextLink.
    The HTTP action has a built-in Pagination setting too (Settings > Pagination > Threshold). It follows
    @odata.nextLink automatically for OData-style responses. Try it first for Graph: one action, no loop.

B. Page number
  Initialize varPage (Integer) = 1,  varMore (Boolean) = true
  Do until: @equals(variables('varMore'), false)        Count 200
    HTTP GET https://api.vendor.com/orders?page=@{variables('varPage')}&per_page=100
    Merge + Set varAll as above (body('HTTP')?['data'])
    Set varMore = @{greater(length(body('HTTP')?['data']), 99)}        a short page means the end
       or  @{less(variables('varPage'), body('HTTP')?['meta']?['total_pages'])}
    Increment varPage

C. Offset and limit
  HTTP GET .../items?offset=@{variables('varOffset')}&limit=200
  Set varMore = @{equals(length(body('HTTP')?['items']), 200)}
  Increment varOffset by 200

D. Cursor token
  HTTP GET .../events?limit=500@{if(empty(variables('varCursor')), '', concat('&cursor=', encodeUriComponent(variables('varCursor'))))}
  Set varCursor = @{coalesce(body('HTTP')?['next_cursor'], '')}
  Do until: @empty(variables('varCursor'))   (the first pass always runs)

E. Link header (GitHub-style)
  Header: Link: <https://api.github.com/...&page=2>; rel="next", <...>; rel="last"
  Next URL:
    @{if(contains(coalesce(outputs('HTTP')?['headers']?['Link'], ''), 'rel="next"'),
         first(split(last(split(first(split(outputs('HTTP')?['headers']?['Link'], '>; rel="next"')), '<')), '>')),
         '')}

Safety
  Always set Count and Timeout on the loop and check after it whether the stop condition was truly met:
    Condition: varUrl is empty (or varMore is false). Otherwise Terminate as Failed: "Paging stopped early".
  429 responses: keep the default retry policy. Add a short Delay between pages for strict APIs.

Memory and size
  A flow action's output is limited to roughly 100 MB, and variables holding tens of thousands of objects
  slow the run. Reduce early: request only needed fields ($select), and where possible process each page
  inside the loop (for example send it to a child flow or batch write) instead of accumulating everything.

Process per page instead of accumulating
  Do until ...
    HTTP GET page
    Select the fields needed
    Run a Child Flow (or batch request) with the page's rows
    Set varUrl to the next link
stepByStepInstructions: Find how the API signals the next page: link, page number, offset or cursor.
Initialise variables for the pointer and the combined results.
Loop until the pointer is empty or the last page is short.
Merge each page into the results with a Compose and Set variable.
Set loop limits and verify completion after the loop.
Process per page when the full set would be very large.
commonMistakes: Assuming the first response is the whole result.
No loop limits, risking an endless run when the pointer never clears.
Self-referencing a variable in Set variable.
Accumulating huge arrays in memory.
troubleshooting: If the loop never ends, log the pointer each pass. Some APIs repeat the last link.
If counts are short, check whether union removed duplicates or the loop hit its Count limit.
If the next link fails authentication, send the same headers and authentication on every page request.
If the run is slow, raise the page size to the API's maximum and select fewer fields.
seoTitle: Page through an API with a next link in a flow
seoDescription: Collect every page from a REST API that returns results in pages, using a Do until loop on the next link, offset counters or cursor tokens.

faqs.question: How do I handle pagination with the HTTP action in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Follow the next link in a Do until loop and merge each page into an array, or turn on the action's Pagination setting for OData responses.

faqs.question: Why can't I append an array to itself in Set variable?
faqs.answer: A variable cannot reference itself. Compute the merged array in a Compose, then set the variable to that output.

faqs.question: How do I know the loop collected everything?
faqs.answer: After the loop, check the next pointer is empty and compare the count with the API's total if it provides one.

title: Read values from XML in a flow with xpath
