shortDescription: Extract single values, repeating nodes and attributes from XML responses and files with the xml and xpath functions, including documents that use namespaces.
fullDescription: SOAP services, RSS feeds, bank files and many older systems return XML. Power Automate has no Parse XML action, but the xml() and xpath() expressions select nodes directly, and converting XML to JSON gives ordinary property access. Namespaces are the usual stumbling block, and have a standard workaround.
problemStatement: A supplier's order feed arrives as XML. The flow needs the order number and each line item, but there is no parser action, and the first xpath attempt returns nothing because of a namespace.
whenToUse: SOAP and legacy web service responses
XML files from SharePoint or email
RSS and Atom feeds beyond what the RSS connector exposes
whenNotToUse: JSON APIs, where Parse JSON is simpler
Very large XML files near the 100 MB message limit
formulaOrCode:
Sample
<Order id="SO-1042" xmlns:c="http://contoso.com/common">
  <Customer><c:Name>Fabrikam</c:Name><Email>buyer@fabrikam.com</Email></Customer>
  <Lines>
    <Line sku="A100"><Qty>2</Qty><Price>19.50</Price></Line>
    <Line sku="B200"><Qty>1</Qty><Price>5.00</Price></Line>
  </Lines>
</Order>

Get the XML as an XML object
  From a string or HTTP body:      xml(body('HTTP'))
  From a SharePoint file:          xml(base64ToString(body('Get_file_content')?['$content']))
  Compose "Doc": @{xml(...)}       reuse outputs('Doc') below

Single values (wrap with string() inside the XPath to get text directly)
  Order id (attribute):   xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'string(/Order/@id)')                         SO-1042
  Email:                  xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'string(/Order/Customer/Email)')
  Line count:             xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'count(/Order/Lines/Line)')                   2
  Total:                  xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'sum(/Order/Lines/Line/Price)')               24.5
  First SKU:              xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'string(/Order/Lines/Line[1]/@sku)')
  By condition:           xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'string(/Order/Lines/Line[@sku="B200"]/Qty)')
  Without string(), xpath returns an array of nodes (base64-encoded XML fragments in run history).

Repeating nodes
  Select
    From: xpath(outputs('Doc'), '/Order/Lines/Line')
    Map:  sku   = xpath(xml(item()), 'string(/Line/@sku)')
          qty   = int(xpath(xml(item()), 'string(/Line/Qty)'))
          price = float(xpath(xml(item()), 'string(/Line/Price)'))
  Result: [ { "sku": "A100", "qty": 2, "price": 19.5 }, ... ]
  Each item is a node. Wrap it with xml(item()) and query relative to its own root.

Namespaces
  /Order/Customer/Name returns nothing because Name is in the c namespace. Options:
  1. local-name():
     xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'string(/Order/Customer/*[local-name()="Name"])')
     Default namespace on the root (xmlns="http://...") means EVERY element needs it:
     xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'string(/*[local-name()="Order"]/*[local-name()="Customer"]/*[local-name()="Email"])')
  2. Strip namespaces first (simple, fine when names do not clash):
     Compose Clean: replace(replace(string(body('HTTP')), ' xmlns="http://contoso.com/orders"', ''), 'c:', '')
     then xml(outputs('Clean'))
  3. Match anywhere:  xpath(outputs('Doc'), 'string(//*[local-name()="Name"])')

Convert to JSON instead
  json(xml(body('HTTP')))
  { "Order": { "@id": "SO-1042", "Customer": { "c:Name": "Fabrikam", "Email": "..." },
               "Lines": { "Line": [ { "@sku": "A100", "Qty": "2", "Price": "19.50" }, ... ] } } }
  Attributes get an @ prefix, text beside attributes appears as #text, and all values are strings.
  Catch: a single Line becomes an object, two or more become an array, so a loop written for an array
  fails on single-line orders. Use xpath for repeating nodes, which always returns an array.

SOAP call and response
  HTTP POST https://legacy.contoso.com/Service.asmx
    Headers: Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8        SOAPAction: "http://tempuri.org/GetOrder"
    Body:
    <soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
      <soap:Body><GetOrder xmlns="http://tempuri.org/"><orderId>@{variables('orderId')}</orderId></GetOrder></soap:Body>
    </soap:Envelope>
  Read: xpath(xml(body('HTTP')), 'string(//*[local-name()="GetOrderResult"]/*[local-name()="Status"])')

Build XML
  xml(json('{ "Order": { "@id": "SO-1", "Customer": "Fabrikam" } }'))  >  <Order id="SO-1"><Customer>Fabrikam</Customer></Order>
  Escape text placed inside hand-written XML:
    replace(replace(replace(value, '&', '&'), '<', '<'), '>', '>')

Encoding
  A byte order mark or wrong encoding makes xml() fail. Strip it:
    replace(base64ToString(...), decodeUriComponent('%EF%BB%BF'), '')
stepByStepInstructions: Convert the response or file content to an XML object with xml().
Select single values with xpath and the string() function.
Select repeating nodes into an array and map them with Select.
Handle namespaces with local-name() or by stripping them.
Convert numbers and dates from text.
Use json(xml()) only when single-versus-array differences are not a risk.
commonMistakes: Ignoring namespaces and getting empty results.
Forgetting string() and receiving node arrays.
Relying on json(xml()) for repeating elements that may occur once.
Building XML by concatenation without escaping.
troubleshooting: If xpath returns nothing, check for a default namespace and switch to local-name().
If xml() fails, the content is not well-formed or has a byte order mark. Inspect the raw string.
If values look base64-encoded in history, wrap the expression in string() inside the XPath.
If a loop fails on a single item, select nodes with xpath so the result is always an array.
seoTitle: Read values from XML in a flow with xpath
seoDescription: Extract single values, repeating nodes and attributes from XML responses and files with the xml and xpath functions, including documents that use namespaces.

faqs.question: How do I parse XML in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use xml() to load it and xpath() to select values, or convert it with json(xml()) and read properties.

faqs.question: Why does my xpath return an empty result?
faqs.answer: Usually a namespace. Match elements with local-name() or remove the namespace declarations first.

faqs.question: How do I loop over repeating XML elements?
faqs.answer: Select them with xpath, which returns an array of nodes, and read each with xpath(xml(item()), ...).

title: Calculate due dates in working days, skipping weekends and holidays
shortDescription: Add a number of working days to a date and count working days between two dates, using a holiday list and expressions without looping day by day.
fullDescription: Service levels are written in working days, but addDays counts every day. A dependable calculation generates the candidate dates as an array, removes weekends and holidays with Filter array, and picks the nth remaining date. It needs no loop, runs in a few actions and reads holidays from a list the business maintains.
problemStatement: A five-working-day deadline set on a Thursday before a public holiday comes out as the following Tuesday, when it should be the Friday after.
whenToUse: Due dates and service level targets
Reminder schedules that ignore weekends
Reporting elapsed working days
whenNotToUse: Hour-level service levels with business hours, which need a fuller calendar
Regions with different working weeks unless you parameterise the weekend days
formulaOrCode:
Inputs
  startDate (for example the Created date), daysToAdd (for example 5)
  Holidays list (SharePoint): Title, HolidayDate (date only), Region (optional)

1. Holidays as an array of yyyy-MM-dd strings
  Get items: Holidays, Filter Query: HolidayDate ge '@{formatDateTime(variables('startDate'),'yyyy-MM-dd')}', Top Count 100
  Select "Holidays": From value   Map (text mode):  @formatDateTime(item()?['HolidayDate'],'yyyy-MM-dd')

2. Candidate dates: enough calendar days to contain the working days
  Select "Candidates"
    From: @range(1, add(mul(variables('daysToAdd'), 2), 15))
    Map (text mode): @formatDateTime(addDays(variables('startDate'), item()), 'yyyy-MM-dd')
  (range starts at 1 so counting begins the day after the start date)

3. Keep working days only
  Filter array "WorkingDays"
    From: body('Candidates')
    Advanced mode:
    @and(
      not(equals(dayOfWeek(item()), 0)),
      not(equals(dayOfWeek(item()), 6)),
      not(contains(body('Holidays'), item()))
    )
  dayOfWeek: 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday.

4. The due date is the nth working day
  Compose "DueDate":  @body('WorkingDays')[sub(variables('daysToAdd'), 1)]
  As a date-time for SharePoint: @{outputs('DueDate')}T17:00:00Z   or just the date for date-only columns.

Working days between two dates (elapsed)
  Select "Span"
    From: @range(0, add(div(sub(ticks(variables('endDate')), ticks(variables('startDate'))), 864000000000), 1))
    Map:  @formatDateTime(addDays(variables('startDate'), item()), 'yyyy-MM-dd')
  Filter array with the same condition > length(body('Filter_array'))
  This counts both the start and end dates when they are working days. Subtract 1 for "days elapsed".
  range() accepts up to 100,000 items, so multi-year spans are fine.

Is today a working day? (guard for scheduled reminders)
  @and(not(contains(createArray(0,6), dayOfWeek(convertFromUtc(utcNow(),'Eastern Standard Time')))),
       not(contains(body('Holidays'), convertFromUtc(utcNow(),'Eastern Standard Time','yyyy-MM-dd'))))
  Use local time: late evening UTC can already be tomorrow, or still yesterday, locally.

Next working day on or after a date
  Candidates from range(0, 10), same filter, first(body('WorkingDays')).

Different weekend (for example Friday and Saturday)
  Replace the two dayOfWeek tests with:
    not(contains(createArray(5,6), dayOfWeek(item())))
  Or hold weekend day numbers in an environment variable and parse them with json().

Reusable child flow
  Trigger: Manually trigger a flow, inputs StartDate (date), Days (number), Region (text)
  Steps 1 to 4 above, holidays filtered by region.
  Respond to a PowerApp or flow: DueDate (text)
  Call it from any flow or from a canvas app.

Same logic in Power Fx (canvas apps)
  With({ c: AddColumns(Sequence(varDays * 2 + 15), d, DateAdd(varStart, Value, TimeUnit.Days)) },
       Last(FirstN(Filter(c, Weekday(d, StartOfWeek.Monday) <= 5 && !(d in colHolidays.HolidayDate)), varDays)).d)

Check
  Start Thu 24 Dec 2026, 5 working days, holiday Fri 25 Dec: Mon 28, Tue 29, Wed 30, Thu 31, then with 1 Jan
  as a holiday the fifth day is Mon 4 Jan 2027.
stepByStepInstructions: Keep public holidays in a list with a date column.
Load holidays as an array of date strings.
Generate candidate dates after the start date with range and Select.
Filter out weekends and holidays.
Take the nth remaining date as the due date.
Wrap the logic in a child flow so every process uses the same calendar.
commonMistakes: Using addDays and adjusting weekends by hand.
Looping one day at a time with a counter.
Comparing date-times with dates, so holidays never match.
Working in UTC when the business day is local.
troubleshooting: If holidays are not skipped, format both sides as yyyy-MM-dd strings before comparing.
If the index is out of range, generate more candidate dates.
If the result is a day off, check the time zone conversion of the start date.
If regions differ, filter the holiday list by region.
seoTitle: Calculate due dates in working days, skipping weekends and holidays
seoDescription: Add a number of working days to a date and count working days between two dates, using a holiday list and expressions without looping day by day.

faqs.question: How do I add business days to a date in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Generate a range of following dates, filter out weekends and holidays, and take the nth date that remains.

faqs.question: How do I exclude public holidays?
faqs.answer: Keep them in a list, load them as an array of date strings and exclude candidates contained in that array.

faqs.question: Is there a built-in working days function?
faqs.answer: No. Flows have addDays and dayOfWeek, which you combine as shown.

title: Move and copy SharePoint files in a flow without name clashes
shortDescription: Archive or route documents between libraries, choose what happens when the name already exists, rename as part of the move and keep metadata and versions.
fullDescription: Moving a file sounds trivial until the destination already has one with that name, the target folder does not exist, or the metadata disappears. The SharePoint Move file and Copy file actions keep versions and matching columns, and have an explicit setting for name conflicts. Renaming is a separate small step.
problemStatement: A flow archives approved documents by reading the content and creating a new file in another library. Version history and metadata are lost, and the run fails whenever a file of the same name exists.
whenToUse: Archiving completed documents
Routing uploads from a drop-off library
Publishing approved files to a read-only library
whenNotToUse: Bulk migrations of thousands of files, where migration tooling is better
Moves between tenants, which these actions do not support
formulaOrCode:
Move one file
  SharePoint > Move file
    Current Site Address: https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Intake
    File to Move:        @{triggerOutputs()?['body/{Identifier}']}          (file identifier from the trigger or Get files)
    Destination Site Address: https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Archive
    Destination Folder:  /Shared Documents/2026/Contracts
    If another file is already there:  Move with a new name | Replace | Fail this action
  Output: body('Move_file')?['Id'], ['ItemId'], ['Name'], ['Path']

  "Move with a new name" appends a number (Contract1.pdf). Replace overwrites, adding a version where
  versioning allows. Fail lets you handle the clash yourself.

Copy instead
  SharePoint > Copy file: same fields. Use for publishing while the original stays in place.

What comes across
  Version history (Move, within the same tenant), Created/Modified and authors, and column values where the
  destination library has columns with the same internal name and type. Managed metadata and lookups need
  matching term sets and lists. Columns missing at the destination are dropped silently.
  Approval status, retention labels and unique permissions do not reliably follow.

Make sure the folder exists
  SharePoint > Create new folder
    List or Library: Documents        Folder Path: 2026/Contracts/@{variables('customer')}
  Creates nested folders in one call and does not fail if they already exist.

Rename as part of the move (two approaches)
  A. Rename after moving
     Send an HTTP request to SharePoint
       Site: destination        Method: POST
       Uri: _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Documents')/items(@{body('Move_file')?['ItemId']})/validateUpdateListItem
       Body: { "formValues": [ { "FieldName": "FileLeafRef", "FieldValue": "CON-@{variables('number')}.pdf" } ] }
     validateUpdateListItem changes the name without creating a new version or altering Modified, when
     bNewDocumentUpdate is true:  add  , "bNewDocumentUpdate": true  to the body.
  B. Rename before moving, with the same call against the source library.

A unique, readable name
  @{formatDateTime(utcNow(),'yyyyMMdd')}-@{replace(replace(triggerOutputs()?['body/{FilenameWithExtension}'],'#',''),'%','')}
  Strip characters SharePoint rejects:  " * : < > ? / \ |    and avoid leading or trailing spaces and periods.
  Keep the whole path under 400 characters.

Handle the conflict yourself
  Move file with "Fail this action", then a parallel branch with run after "has failed":
    Condition: contains(string(outputs('Move_file')?['body']), 'already exists')
      Yes: Move again to a "Duplicates" folder, or rename with a timestamp and retry
      No:  Terminate with the error

After the move
  Update file properties using the new ItemId: Status = Archived, ArchivedOn = utcNow()
  Update the source record's link column: body('Move_file')?['Path'] (server-relative) with the site URL in front.
  Links shared as "People with existing access" keep working after a move within the tenant, because SharePoint
  redirects by document ID where that feature is on. Path-based links break.

Many files
  Get files (properties only) with a filter (for example Status eq 'Approved'), Top Count 200.
  Apply to each with concurrency 1 to 5: Move file. Moves are asynchronous copy jobs under the hood, so high
  concurrency causes throttling and lock errors.
  Large files (hundreds of MB) can exceed the action timeout: the move may still complete. Check before retrying.

Move a whole folder
  SharePoint > Move folder / Copy folder with the folder's identifier. Same conflict option.

Locked or checked-out files
  Fail with "The file is locked for shared use" or "checked out". Add a retry after a delay, or a Do until
  with a few attempts, and report files still locked.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the destination folder path if it may not exist.
Use Move file or Copy file with the file identifier, not file content.
Choose the conflict behaviour deliberately.
Rename with validateUpdateListItem when the destination name must follow a standard.
Update metadata and links using the new item ID.
Limit concurrency and handle locked files when moving many.
commonMistakes: Recreating the file from content, which loses versions and metadata.
Leaving the conflict option on its default without deciding.
Destination library missing the columns you expect to keep.
High concurrency on bulk moves.
troubleshooting: If metadata is lost, add columns with the same internal names to the destination library.
If the move fails with a path error, create the folder first and check for invalid characters.
If the file is locked, retry after a delay and ask users to close it.
If the action times out on a large file, check the destination before retrying to avoid duplicates.
seoTitle: Move and copy SharePoint files in a flow without name clashes
seoDescription: Archive or route documents between libraries, choose what happens when the name already exists, rename as part of the move and keep metadata and versions.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate move file SharePoint rename

faqs.question: How do I move a SharePoint file with Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use the SharePoint Move file action with the file identifier, destination site and folder.

faqs.question: What happens if a file with the same name exists?
faqs.answer: You choose: move with a new name, replace the existing file, or fail the action so you can handle it.

faqs.question: Does Move file keep version history and metadata?
faqs.answer: Versions are kept within a tenant, and column values are kept where the destination has matching columns.

title: Save email attachments from a shared mailbox to SharePoint
shortDescription: Watch a shared mailbox, skip signature images, save each real attachment to a library with useful metadata and file the email afterwards.
fullDescription: Invoices, forms and reports still arrive by email. A flow on a shared mailbox can save each attachment to a SharePoint library with the sender, subject and received date as metadata. The details that matter are filtering out inline images, making file names unique and marking the email as processed.
problemStatement: Supplier invoices arrive in a shared mailbox. Someone saves each PDF by hand, half the saved files are logo images from signatures, and there is no record of which emails were handled.
whenToUse: Invoice, order and form intake by email
Archiving reports sent by other systems
Feeding an approval or extraction process
whenNotToUse: Mailboxes receiving sensitive personal data without a retention and access plan
Very large attachments beyond connector limits, which need a different transfer route
formulaOrCode:
Trigger
  Office 365 Outlook > When a new email arrives in a shared mailbox (V2)
    Original Mailbox Address: invoices@contoso.com
    Folder: Inbox
    Include Attachments: Yes
    Only with Attachments: Yes
    Subject Filter / From: optional
  The connection's user needs Full Access to the shared mailbox.
  Trigger condition to ignore automatic replies:
    @not(contains(toLower(triggerOutputs()?['body/subject']), 'automatic reply'))

Loop the attachments
  Apply to each: triggerOutputs()?['body/attachments']         (concurrency off, or low)

    Condition "real attachment" (advanced, all true)
      @equals(items('Apply_to_each')?['isInline'], false)
      @greater(items('Apply_to_each')?['size'], 10000)                         skips tiny icons
      @or(endsWith(toLower(items('Apply_to_each')?['name']), '.pdf'),
          endsWith(toLower(items('Apply_to_each')?['name']), '.xlsx'),
          endsWith(toLower(items('Apply_to_each')?['name']), '.docx'))

    Yes >
      Compose FileName
        @{formatDateTime(triggerOutputs()?['body/receivedDateTime'],'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss')}_@{replace(replace(replace(items('Apply_to_each')?['name'],'#',''),'%',''),'&','and')}

      SharePoint > Create file
        Site: https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Finance
        Folder Path: /Invoices/Inbox/@{formatDateTime(utcNow(),'yyyy-MM')}
        File Name: @{outputs('FileName')}
        File Content: @{base64ToBinary(items('Apply_to_each')?['contentBytes'])}
      (Create file makes the folder path if it does not exist.)

      SharePoint > Update file properties
        Id: outputs('Create_file')?['body/ItemId']
        Sender:        triggerOutputs()?['body/from']
        EmailSubject:  triggerOutputs()?['body/subject']
        ReceivedOn:    triggerOutputs()?['body/receivedDateTime']
        MessageId:     triggerOutputs()?['body/internetMessageId']
        Status:        New

Attachments missing content
  Large attachments can arrive without contentBytes. Fetch them:
    Office 365 Outlook > Get Attachment (V2)
      Message Id: triggerOutputs()?['body/id']      Attachment Id: items('Apply_to_each')?['id']
      Original Mailbox Address: invoices@contoso.com
    File Content: body('Get_Attachment_(V2)')?['contentBytes']   (through base64ToBinary)

Mark the email as handled
  Office 365 Outlook > Move email (V2)
    Message Id: triggerOutputs()?['body/id']      Folder: Processed      Original Mailbox Address: invoices@contoso.com
  Or Mark as read or unread (V3) and assign a category "Filed" (Assigns an Outlook category).
  Emails where nothing qualified: move to "Needs review" and notify the team.

Avoid duplicates
  The same email can be picked up again after a mailbox move or flow restart. Before creating files:
    Get files (properties only): Filter Query MessageId eq '@{triggerOutputs()?['body/internetMessageId']}', Top Count 1
    Stop if found.

Acknowledge the sender (optional)
  Send an email from a shared mailbox (V2): "We received 2 documents: ..." with the saved names.
  Do not reply to no-reply addresses or to your own domain's automated senders, to avoid mail loops.

Zip files and embedded messages
  .zip: save as is, or expand with OneDrive > Extract archive to folder, then copy the contents.
  .msg/.eml attachments: saved as files. Their inner attachments are not unpacked by this flow.

Limits
  Trigger delivers messages up to about 50 MB in total. Exchange's own attachment size limits apply.
  Shared mailbox triggers poll every few minutes. Several emails at once produce parallel runs.

Next steps in the chain
  A second flow on file creation: AI Builder invoice processing, an approval, or routing by supplier.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a library with columns for sender, subject, received date and message ID.
Trigger on new email in the shared mailbox with attachments included.
Loop the attachments and keep only non-inline files of expected types.
Create each file with a timestamped name and set its metadata.
Move the email to a processed folder or categorise it.
Check for an existing message ID to avoid saving twice.
commonMistakes: Saving inline signature images as documents.
File names that collide when two emails carry 'invoice.pdf'.
Leaving processed emails in the inbox with no marker.
Auto-replying to automated senders and starting a loop.
troubleshooting: If files are empty or corrupt, wrap contentBytes in base64ToBinary or fetch with Get Attachment.
If the trigger never fires, the connection user lacks access to the shared mailbox or the folder is wrong.
If logos are saved, tighten the inline, size and extension conditions.
If Create file fails on the name, strip characters SharePoint does not allow.
seoTitle: Save email attachments from a shared mailbox to SharePoint
seoDescription: Watch a shared mailbox, skip signature images, save each real attachment to a library with useful metadata and file the email afterwards.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate save email attachments to SharePoint

faqs.question: How do I save email attachments to SharePoint automatically?
faqs.answer: Use the Outlook trigger for new email with attachments, loop the attachments and call SharePoint Create file for each.

faqs.question: How do I skip signature images?
faqs.answer: Filter on isInline equals false, a minimum size and the file extensions you expect.

faqs.question: Does this work with a shared mailbox?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the shared mailbox trigger and give the connection's user Full Access to the mailbox.

title: Move Microsoft Forms file uploads into a SharePoint library
shortDescription: Read the upload question's JSON, fetch each file from where Forms stored it and file it in a library alongside a list item for the response.
fullDescription: A file upload question in Microsoft Forms stores files in the form owner's OneDrive, or in the group's SharePoint site for group forms. The response contains only a JSON string describing them. A flow has to parse that string, fetch each file's content and create it where the process needs it.
problemStatement: Applicants attach documents to a form. The files sit in a personal OneDrive folder that the processing team cannot see, disconnected from the response data.
whenToUse: Intake forms with supporting documents
Moving uploads out of a personal OneDrive
Linking files to a list item per response
whenNotToUse: External respondents, since file upload questions work only for signed-in users in your organisation
Forms needing more than 10 files or files above the question's size limit
formulaOrCode:
Trigger and response
  Microsoft Forms > When a new response is submitted: Form Id
  Microsoft Forms > Get response details: Form Id, Response Id
  The upload question's value is a STRING containing JSON, or empty when nothing was uploaded:
  [ { "name": "passport_Priya Shah.pdf", "link": "https://contoso-my.sharepoint.com/...", "id": "01ABC...",
      "type": null, "size": 182340, "referenceId": "01DEF...", "driveId": "b!xyz...", "status": 1,
      "uploadSessionUrl": null } ]

Create the record first
  SharePoint > Create item: Applications
    Title: @{outputs('Get_response_details')?['body/r1a2b3...']}        Applicant email: responder
  Folder for the files: SharePoint > Create new folder: Applications Documents / APP-@{outputs('Create_item')?['body/ID']}

Parse the upload answer
  Condition: not(empty(outputs('Get_response_details')?['body/<upload question id>']))
  Parse JSON
    Content: @{outputs('Get_response_details')?['body/<upload question id>']}
    Schema:
    { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object", "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" }, "link": { "type": "string" }, "id": { "type": "string" },
        "size": { "type": "integer" }, "driveId": { "type": "string" } } } }
  Or without the action:  json(outputs('Get_response_details')?['body/<upload question id>'])

Copy each file
  Apply to each: body('Parse_JSON')

  A. Personal form (files in the owner's OneDrive: Apps/Microsoft Forms/<form name>/<question>)
     OneDrive for Business > Get file content
       File: @{items('Apply_to_each')?['id']}
     SharePoint > Create file
       Folder Path: /Applications Documents/APP-@{outputs('Create_item')?['body/ID']}
       File Name:   @{items('Apply_to_each')?['name']}
       File Content: @{body('Get_file_content')}
     The flow's OneDrive connection must be the form owner's account.

  B. Group form (files in the group's SharePoint site: Documents/Apps/Microsoft Forms/<form name>/<question>)
     SharePoint > Get file content using path
       Site Address: the group site
       File Path: /Shared Documents/Apps/Microsoft Forms/<Form name>/<Question>/@{items('Apply_to_each')?['name']}
     SharePoint > Create file (as above)
     Or use Move file / Copy file with the path to keep it within SharePoint.

  C. Works for both, by drive and item ID (Graph)
     Send an HTTP request (Office 365 Groups or HTTP with Entra ID):
       GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/@{items('Apply_to_each')?['driveId']}/items/@{items('Apply_to_each')?['id']}/content

Clean file names
  Forms appends the responder's name: "passport_Priya Shah.pdf". To standardise:
    @{concat('APP-', outputs('Create_item')?['body/ID'], '_', replace(items('Apply_to_each')?['name'], concat('_', outputs('Get_response_details')?['body/responder']), ''))}
  Remove characters SharePoint rejects if you build names from answers.

Link the files to the record
  Update item: DocumentsFolder = link to the folder
    https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/HR/Applications%20Documents/APP-@{ID}
  Or attach instead of filing: SharePoint > Add attachment (Id = item ID, File Name, File Content).

Tidy up the source
  OneDrive > Delete file (id) after a successful copy, if the Forms copy should not linger.
  The response in Forms still shows the link, which will then be broken. Decide which copy is the record.

Several upload questions
  Repeat Parse and loop per question, or build one array:
    union(json(coalesce(answerA,'[]')), json(coalesce(answerB,'[]')))

Limits of the question type
  Up to 10 files per question, 10 MB, 100 MB or 1 GB each as configured. Signed-in users in your organisation only.
  File types can be restricted on the question (Word, Excel, PPT, PDF, Image, Video, Audio).

Ownership
  Personal forms tie the process to one person's OneDrive. Create the form as a GROUP form
  (Forms > My groups) so files land in the team's SharePoint site and survive staff changes.
stepByStepInstructions: Create the form as a group form so uploads land in a team site.
Trigger on a new response and get the response details.
Check the upload answer is not empty and parse its JSON string.
Create the list item and a folder for the response.
Loop the files, get each file's content and create it in the folder.
Store the folder link on the item and decide whether to remove the Forms copy.
commonMistakes: Treating the answer as an array without parsing the string.
No empty check when the question is optional.
Using a personal form for a team process.
Looking in OneDrive for files from a group form.
troubleshooting: If Parse JSON fails on null, add the empty condition or wrap with coalesce(..., '[]').
If Get file content fails, check whether the form is personal or group and use the matching connector.
If the file is not found by path, read the name and folder from the link property.
If names include the responder's name, strip that suffix when building the new name.
seoTitle: Move Microsoft Forms file uploads into a SharePoint library
seoDescription: Read the upload question's JSON, fetch each file from where Forms stored it and file it in a library alongside a list item for the response.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate Forms file upload SharePoint

faqs.question: Where do Microsoft Forms file uploads go?
faqs.answer: To the form owner's OneDrive for personal forms, or the group's SharePoint site for group forms, under Apps/Microsoft Forms.

faqs.question: How do I get Forms uploads in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Parse the upload answer's JSON string, then fetch each file by ID or path and create it in your library.

faqs.question: Can external users upload files in Forms?
faqs.answer: No. File upload questions require respondents to be signed in to your organisation.

title: Create or update hundreds of SharePoint items fast with $batch
shortDescription: Send up to 1,000 create, update or delete operations to SharePoint in one request using the REST $batch endpoint, with chunking and result checking.
fullDescription: Create item inside Apply to each handles a few items per second and spends an action on each. The SharePoint REST $batch endpoint accepts many operations in a single request. A flow builds the batch body as text, posts it with Send an HTTP request to SharePoint, and checks the response for failures. Imports of thousands of rows drop from an hour to a minute or two.
problemStatement: Importing 3,000 rows into a list takes 50 minutes with Apply to each, consumes thousands of actions and is regularly throttled part-way through.
whenToUse: Bulk imports and syncs into SharePoint lists
Mass status updates or deletes
Flows near their daily action allowance
whenNotToUse: A few dozen items, where the standard actions are simpler to maintain
Operations that depend on each other's results within the same batch
formulaOrCode:
Inputs
  varRows: array of objects to create, for example from Excel, each { Title, Amount, DueDate }
  List: Projects      Site: https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/PMO
  Entity type name (needed for verbose metadata only): SP.Data.ProjectsListItem
    GET _api/web/lists/getbytitle('Projects')?$select=ListItemEntityTypeFullName

1. Chunk the rows (1,000 per batch at most. 200 to 500 is a safe size)
  Compose BatchSize: 300
  Apply to each chunk index:  range(0, add(div(sub(length(variables('varRows')), 1), 300), 1))        concurrency 1
    Compose Chunk: take(skip(variables('varRows'), mul(item(), 300)), 300)

2. Build one changeset entry per row with Select
  Select "Ops"
    From: outputs('Chunk')
    Map (text mode, a single string per row):
@{concat('--changeset_', variables('guid'), decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'),
'Content-Type: application/http', decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'),
'Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary', decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'), decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'),
'POST https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/PMO/_api/web/lists/getbytitle(''Projects'')/items HTTP/1.1', decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'),
'Content-Type: application/json;odata=nometadata', decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'), decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'),
string(setProperty(setProperty(json('{}'), 'Title', item()?['Title']), 'Amount', item()?['Amount'])),
decodeUriComponent('%0D%0A'))}
  setProperty builds the item's JSON body and escapes quotes and special characters for you. Add one
  setProperty per column, using internal column names.
  variables('guid') = guid() created once per chunk (Compose).

3. Assemble the batch body (Compose "Body")
--batch_@{variables('guid')}
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="changeset_@{variables('guid')}"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary

@{join(body('Ops'), '')}
--changeset_@{variables('guid')}--
--batch_@{variables('guid')}--
  Blank lines matter: one blank line after each header block. Line endings must be CRLF.

4. Send
  SharePoint > Send an HTTP request to SharePoint
    Site Address: https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/PMO
    Method: POST
    Uri: _api/$batch
    Headers: Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=batch_@{variables('guid')}
             Accept: application/json;odata=nometadata
    Body: @{outputs('Body')}

5. Check the result
  The response is multipart text with one HTTP status per operation. The request itself returns 200 even
  when individual operations fail.
    Compose Result: @{string(body('Send_an_HTTP_request_to_SharePoint'))}
    Failures: sub(length(split(outputs('Result'), 'HTTP/1.1 4')), 1) + the same for 'HTTP/1.1 5'
    Created:  sub(length(split(outputs('Result'), 'HTTP/1.1 201')), 1)
  Condition: failures greater than 0 > log the chunk index and the response to a list or file, then continue or stop.

Update and delete entries
  Update:  'PATCH https://.../items(', item()?['ID'], ') HTTP/1.1'  plus headers
           'IF-MATCH: *'   and the JSON body of changed columns. Success status: 204.
  Delete:  'DELETE https://.../items(', item()?['ID'], ') HTTP/1.1'  with 'IF-MATCH: *' and no body. Status 200.
           Recycle instead: POST .../items(<id>)/recycle

Column formats in the JSON body
  Choice: "Status": "Open"        Number: 1250.5        Yes/No: true        Date: "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"
  Person: "OwnerId": 12 (site user ID)        Lookup: "ProjectId": 7
  Multi-choice (nometadata): "Tags": ["A","B"]

Behaviour
  Operations in one changeset are NOT transactional in SharePoint Online: some can succeed while others fail.
  Order within a changeset is preserved. Triggers on the list still fire for every item created: a flow on
  "When an item is created" will run once per item, so pause or guard it during imports.
  Throttling still applies, but one batch counts far less than 300 separate calls. Keep chunk concurrency at 1
  and add a 1 to 2 second delay between chunks for large loads.

Actions used
  3,000 rows in chunks of 300: about 10 x 5 actions = 50, instead of 3,000.
stepByStepInstructions: Shape the rows into objects that match the list's internal column names.
Split the rows into chunks of a few hundred.
Build a changeset entry per row with Select and join them.
Wrap the entries in the batch body with a unique boundary and CRLF line endings.
Post to _api/$batch with Send an HTTP request to SharePoint.
Count success and failure statuses in the response and log failures.
commonMistakes: Treating a 200 response as proof every operation succeeded.
LF line endings or missing blank lines in the batch body.
Unescaped quotes in values breaking the JSON.
Running chunks in parallel and being throttled.
troubleshooting: If the whole batch is rejected with 400, check the boundary names match between header and body.
If items fail with a field error, use internal column names and the right value format for each type.
If only some rows are created, read the per-operation statuses and fix those rows.
If a downstream flow floods, add a trigger condition or switch it off during the import.
seoTitle: Create or update hundreds of SharePoint items fast with $batch
seoDescription: Send up to 1,000 create, update or delete operations to SharePoint in one request using the REST $batch endpoint, with chunking and result checking.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate SharePoint batch create items

faqs.question: How do I create many SharePoint items quickly in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Build a REST $batch request containing all the create operations and send it with Send an HTTP request to SharePoint.

faqs.question: How many operations can one SharePoint batch hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 1,000, though a few hundred per request is a safer size.

faqs.question: Is a SharePoint batch transactional?
faqs.answer: No. Individual operations can fail while others succeed, so check each status in the response.

title: Hide sensitive data in flow run history with secure inputs and outputs
shortDescription: Stop passwords, tokens and personal data appearing in run history by securing the right actions, and understand how the protection flows to later actions.
fullDescription: Run history shows the inputs and outputs of every action to anyone who can open the flow. Secure Inputs and Secure Outputs replace that content with a notice. Applied to the actions that fetch or use sensitive values, they keep secrets and personal data out of history, though they do not make a flow safe from its own editors.
problemStatement: A support engineer opening a failed run can read an API key in the HTTP action's headers and full salary details in a Get item output.
whenToUse: Actions that read or send secrets and tokens
Flows processing personal, health or financial data
Any flow whose run history is visible to more than its author
whenNotToUse: Treating it as access control, since co-owners can turn the setting off
Securing every action, which makes troubleshooting impossible
formulaOrCode:
Turn it on
  Action > ... (or Settings in the new designer) > Secure Inputs: On / Secure Outputs: On > Done
  A padlock icon appears on the action. Run history then shows:
    "Content not shown due to security configuration."

Which setting where
  Fetch a secret (Key Vault Get secret, RetrieveEnvironmentVariableSecretValue, token request)
      Secure Outputs: On
  Use a secret (HTTP with an Authorization header or key in the body or URL)
      Secure Inputs: On           and Secure Outputs if the response echoes it
  Read personal data (Get item, List rows, Get user profile)
      Secure Outputs: On
  Send personal data (Send an email, Post message, Create item)
      Secure Inputs: On
  Trigger receiving sensitive payloads (HTTP request, Forms, Dataverse row)
      Trigger settings > Secure Inputs and Secure Outputs: On

How protection propagates
  When an action's outputs are secured, any LATER action that uses those outputs has its INPUTS hidden
  automatically. Its outputs are not hidden unless you secure them too.
    Get secret (Secure Outputs)  >  HTTP uses the secret: inputs hidden automatically
                                  >  HTTP response visible unless Secure Outputs is set on HTTP
  Compose, Set variable, Select and Parse JSON that touch a secured value: their inputs are hidden, their
  outputs are NOT. A Compose that just passes the secret through exposes it in its output.
    Fix: turn on Secure Outputs on those actions as well, or avoid intermediate copies.
  Variables: Initialize/Set variable shows the value in its inputs. Secure Inputs on each one that holds a secret.
  Apply to each: secure the actions inside. The loop's own item list comes from the source action's outputs.

Example: API call with a key
  1. Dataverse > Perform an unbound action: RetrieveEnvironmentVariableSecretValue       Secure Outputs: On
  2. HTTP GET https://api.vendor.com/v1/customers/@{id}
       Headers: x-api-key: @{outputs('Get_secret')?['body/EnvironmentVariableSecretValue']}
       Secure Inputs: On (explicit, do not rely on propagation alone)        Secure Outputs: On if the body has personal data
  3. Parse JSON of the response                                                       Secure Inputs: On, Secure Outputs: On
  4. Create item with only the non-sensitive fields                                   left visible for support

What it does not do
  Co-owners can edit the flow, switch the settings off and run it again. Limit owners, and use a service
  account plus solutions so production flows are managed and not edited in place.
  Error messages from a failed secured action can still reveal fragments (for example a URL in an
  exception). Keep secrets out of URLs where the API allows headers.
  Data sent to another system (email, Teams, a list) is as visible as that system makes it.
  Flow checker and exported definitions still contain anything typed directly into an action: never
  hard-code secrets, read them at run time.
  Child flows: secure the trigger of the child and the Run a Child Flow action in the parent. Settings do not
  cross the boundary by themselves.
  Dataverse-stored run history (FlowRun table) holds the same redacted view.

Keep troubleshooting possible
  Leave non-sensitive steps visible. Log a correlation ID, record IDs and status codes to a logging list
  (never the payload). On failure, write the error code and action name, not the content.

Review checklist for a flow
  Any Authorization, key, password or token text in action inputs? Secured.
  Any action returning personal data beyond names and IDs? Secured outputs.
  Any Compose or variable holding those values? Secured.
  Owners list limited? Yes.
stepByStepInstructions: List the actions that fetch, hold or send secrets and sensitive data.
Turn on Secure Outputs where such data is read and Secure Inputs where it is used.
Secure intermediate Compose, variable and Parse JSON actions that copy the values.
Secure the trigger when the incoming payload is sensitive.
Run the flow and inspect history to confirm nothing sensitive is shown.
Limit flow owners and log only non-sensitive diagnostics.
commonMistakes: Securing the fetch but not the Compose that copies the value.
Putting a key in the URL, where errors may reveal it.
Assuming secured actions protect against co-owners.
Securing everything and losing the ability to diagnose failures.
troubleshooting: If a secret still shows, find the action whose output displays it and turn on Secure Outputs there.
If support cannot diagnose runs, add a logging step with IDs and status codes.
If a child flow shows the data, secure its trigger and the calling action.
If the setting is missing, look under the action's Settings tab in the new designer.
seoTitle: Hide sensitive data in flow run history with secure inputs and outputs
seoDescription: Stop passwords, tokens and personal data appearing in run history by securing the right actions, and understand how the protection flows to later actions.

faqs.question: What do Secure Inputs and Secure Outputs do in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: They hide an action's inputs or outputs in run history, replacing them with a notice.

faqs.question: Do later actions also hide the value?
faqs.answer: Their inputs are hidden when they use a secured output, but their own outputs are visible unless secured too.

faqs.question: Does this stop flow owners seeing the data?
faqs.answer: No. An owner can turn the setting off. Restrict who can edit the flow.

title: Split an array into batches in a flow
shortDescription: Break a large array into fixed-size groups with chunk or skip and take, then process each group with one batch request, one email or one child flow call.
fullDescription: APIs cap how many records one request can carry, emails have recipient limits and loops over thousands of items are slow. Splitting an array into batches lets a flow send groups of 20, 100 or 1,000 at a time. The chunk function does it in one expression, and skip with take gives the same result where more control is needed.
problemStatement: A flow must send 4,300 rows to an API that accepts 100 per call. Looping one row at a time takes an hour, and sending everything at once is rejected.
whenToUse: APIs and batch endpoints with a maximum per request
Sending email or Teams messages to recipients in groups
Fanning work out to child flows
whenNotToUse: Small arrays that fit a single request
Batches that must be all-or-nothing across the whole set
formulaOrCode:
1. The chunk function
  chunk(collection, length)
  chunk(createArray(1,2,3,4,5,6,7), 3)      >  [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7]]
  chunk(body('List_rows')?['value'], 100)   >  an array of arrays, each up to 100 rows
  Also works on strings: chunk('abcdefg', 3) > ["abc","def","g"]

  Apply to each: @chunk(body('List_rows')?['value'], 100)
    items('Apply_to_each') is one batch (an array)
    HTTP POST https://api.vendor.com/bulk
      Body: { "records": @{items('Apply_to_each')} }
    length(items('Apply_to_each'))       size of this batch (the last one may be smaller)

2. skip and take (when you need the batch index)
  Compose Size: 100
  Compose Count: @{add(div(sub(length(variables('varRows')), 1), outputs('Size')), 1)}
     ceiling division: 4,300 rows > 43 batches. Guard empty input: if length is 0, skip the loop.
  Apply to each: @range(0, outputs('Count'))
    Compose Batch: @take(skip(variables('varRows'), mul(item(), outputs('Size'))), outputs('Size'))
    item() is the batch number (0-based): useful for logging "batch 7 of 43" and for resuming.

3. Shape each batch before sending
  Select inside the loop
    From: items('Apply_to_each')
    Map: id = item()?['cr1a2_number'], name = item()?['cr1a2_name']
  Or shape the whole array once BEFORE chunking, which is cheaper.

4. Typical batch sizes
  SharePoint REST $batch                   up to 1,000 operations (200 to 500 practical)
  Dataverse changeset / $batch             up to 1,000 operations
  Microsoft Graph JSON batching            20 requests per batch
  Outlook recipients per message           500 (tenant limit may be lower)
  Adaptive Card rows                       10 to 15 for readability
  Child flow input                         keep each payload well under a few MB

5. Recipients in groups of 50 (Bcc)
  Select emails: From users, Map (text mode) @item()?['mail']
  Apply to each: @chunk(body('Select'), 50)
    Send an email (V2): Bcc = @{join(items('Apply_to_each'), ';')}

6. Graph JSON batch of 20
  Apply to each: @chunk(variables('userIds'), 20)
    Select "Requests": From items('Apply_to_each')
       Map: id = @{item()}, method = GET, url = /users/@{item()}?$select=id,displayName,accountEnabled
    HTTP POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/$batch
       Body: { "requests": @{body('Requests')} }
    Responses: body('HTTP')?['responses']  each with id, status, body. Order is not guaranteed: match by id.

7. Concurrency and pacing
  Apply to each > Settings > Concurrency Control: 1 for ordered or rate-limited targets. 5 to 20 to go faster
  when the target allows and batches are independent.
  Add Delay 1 to 2 seconds per batch for strict APIs. Honour Retry-After on 429 responses.
  Variables are shared across parallel iterations. Use Compose inside the loop, not Set variable.

8. Track failures per batch
  Scope "Send batch" > on failure (run after has failed): Append to array variable varFailed
     { "batch": <index>, "error": result('Send_batch')?[0]?['error']?['message'] }
  After the loop: if varFailed has entries, email the summary or retry just those batches.

9. Fan out to child flows
  Apply to each chunk (concurrency 10): Run a Child Flow with rows = string(items('Apply_to_each'))
  Each child handles one batch, so a failure affects 100 rows, not 4,300.
stepByStepInstructions: Shape the full array to the fields the target needs.
Choose a batch size from the target's limit.
Split with chunk, or skip and take when you need the batch index.
Send each batch in one request inside Apply to each.
Set concurrency and delays to respect rate limits.
Record failed batches and retry or report them.
commonMistakes: Looping item by item when the target accepts batches.
Using Set variable inside a concurrent loop.
Batch size above the target's maximum.
No handling for a failed batch, losing a whole group silently.
troubleshooting: If chunk is not recognised in an older environment, use the skip and take pattern.
If the last batch fails, check for an empty array when the total is an exact multiple.
If responses are mismatched, correlate by the id in each response, not by position.
If you are throttled, lower concurrency and add a delay.
seoTitle: Split an array into batches in a flow
seoDescription: Break a large array into fixed-size groups with chunk or skip and take, then process each group with one batch request, one email or one child flow call.

faqs.question: How do I split an array into batches in Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Use chunk(array, size), which returns an array of arrays, and loop over the result.

faqs.question: How do I get the batch number?
faqs.answer: Loop over range(0, batchCount) and build each batch with take(skip(array, index * size), size).

faqs.question: What batch size should I use?
faqs.answer: The target's limit or a little below: 20 for Graph batching, a few hundred for SharePoint or Dataverse batch requests.

title: Set item-level permissions on a SharePoint item from a flow
shortDescription: Stop an item inheriting list permissions and grant access only to the requester, their manager and a team group, with the limits that keep lists healthy.
fullDescription: Some lists hold items that only certain people should see: HR requests, incident reports, salary proposals. A flow can break permission inheritance on a new item and grant specific access. It works, and it is also the fastest way to make a list slow and hard to administer, so the approach comes with thresholds and alternatives.
problemStatement: Everyone with access to the HR requests list can open everyone else's requests, because the list has one set of permissions.
whenToUse: Confidential items visible to the creator, an approver and a small team
Document libraries where each folder belongs to one customer or case
Low-volume lists, under a few thousand uniquely secured items
whenNotToUse: High-volume lists, where unique permissions per item degrade performance
Cases solved by the list setting 'Read items that were created by the user'
Using item permissions in place of a proper data platform for sensitive records
formulaOrCode:
Simplest alternative first
  List settings > Advanced settings > Item-level Permissions
    Read access: Read items that were created by the user
    Create and Edit access: Create items and edit items that were created by the user
  Users with Manage Lists (owners, and a team with a custom level) still see everything.
  No flow, no unique permissions. Covers "requester sees own, team sees all".

Flow route (when approvers or other specific people need access)
  Trigger: SharePoint > When an item is created       Site / List: HR Requests
  Run with a connection that has Full Control on the list (a service account).

  1. Stop inheriting
     SharePoint > Stop sharing an item or a file
       Site, List, Id: triggerOutputs()?['body/ID']
     Breaks inheritance and removes everyone except site owners (people with Full Control keep access).

  2. Grant access
     SharePoint > Grant access to an item or a folder
       Id: item ID
       Recipients: @{triggerOutputs()?['body/Author/Email']};@{outputs('Get_manager_(V2)')?['body/mail']}
       Roles: Can view | Can edit
       Message: (leave empty)        Notify Recipients: No
     Call again with a different role for other people. Groups: enter the Microsoft 365 or security group's email.

REST equivalent, with full control over roles and SharePoint groups
  Send an HTTP request to SharePoint (Method POST for each)
    Break inheritance, copying nothing, clearing sub-scopes:
      _api/web/lists/getbytitle('HR Requests')/items(@{ID})/breakroleinheritance(copyRoleAssignments=false,clearSubscopes=true)
    Find a principal ID:
      User:   GET _api/web/siteusers/getbyemail('@{email}')?$select=Id      (ensure first: POST _api/web/ensureuser  { "logonName": "i:0#.f|membership|@{email}" })
      Group:  GET _api/web/sitegroups/getbyname('HR Team')?$select=Id
    Find a role definition ID:
      GET _api/web/roledefinitions?$select=Id,Name
      Common: Full Control 1073741829, Edit 1073741830, Contribute 1073741827, Read 1073741826
    Assign:
      _api/web/lists/getbytitle('HR Requests')/items(@{ID})/roleassignments/addroleassignment(principalid=@{principalId},roledefid=1073741826)
    Remove one assignment:
      .../roleassignments/removeroleassignment(principalid=@{principalId},roledefid=1073741827)
    Restore inheritance:
      .../items(@{ID})/resetroleinheritance

Typical assignment set
  Requester: Read (or Contribute while status is Draft)        Manager: Contribute
  HR Team (SharePoint group): Edit                              Site owners: Full Control (kept automatically)

Change access when status changes
  On approval: remove the requester's Contribute, add Read, so the record is locked for them.
  Trigger condition on status change, then removeroleassignment and addroleassignment.

Timing gap
  Between creation and the flow finishing (seconds to a minute) the item still has inherited permissions.
  Reduce exposure: the list's own permissions grant only Contribute-without-read-others through
  item-level settings above, or submit through a flow or app that creates the item with the service account.

Limits that matter
  50,000 unique permission scopes per list or library is the hard limit. 5,000 is the recommended ceiling.
  Performance and view loading degrade well before the hard limit.
  Grant to GROUPS, not individuals, wherever possible: fewer principals per scope.
  For libraries, secure a FOLDER per case and let files inherit from it: one scope instead of many.
  Audit: Site settings > Site permissions > "Some content on this site has different permissions" lists exceptions.

When volume is high or the data is sensitive
  Use Dataverse with row ownership, teams and security roles, or separate lists or sites per audience.

Check
  Item > Manage access (or ... > Details > Has access) shows who can see it. Test with a normal user account.
stepByStepInstructions: Check whether the list's built-in item-level setting already meets the need.
Trigger on item creation with a service account that has Full Control.
Break inheritance on the item.
Grant read or edit access to the requester, approver and team group.
Adjust assignments when the status changes.
Monitor the number of uniquely secured items and prefer groups and folders.
commonMistakes: Unique permissions on every item of a high-volume list.
Granting to individuals instead of groups.
Running the flow with an account that lacks Full Control.
Ignoring the gap before the flow runs.
troubleshooting: If Grant access fails, the connection account needs Full Control and the recipient must be a valid user or group.
If people still see the item, they belong to a group with Full Control or the break did not run.
If the list is slow, count unique scopes and consolidate into folders or groups.
If the user is not found by email, call ensureuser first.
seoTitle: Set item-level permissions on a SharePoint item from a flow
seoDescription: Stop an item inheriting list permissions and grant access only to the requester, their manager and a team group, with the limits that keep lists healthy.
primaryKeyword: Power Automate SharePoint break inheritance grant access

faqs.question: How do I restrict a SharePoint item to certain people with Power Automate?
faqs.answer: Break inheritance with Stop sharing an item or a file, then use Grant access to an item or a folder for the people who need it.

faqs.question: Is there a no-code way to let users see only their own items?
faqs.answer: Yes. In list advanced settings, set item-level permissions so users read and edit only items they created.

faqs.question: How many items can have unique permissions?
faqs.answer: The hard limit is 50,000 unique scopes per list, with 5,000 as the recommended maximum.

title: Open a canvas app on a specific record with a deep link
shortDescription: Pass a record ID in the app's URL, read it with Param, start on the detail screen and build links for emails and Teams messages.
fullDescription: A notification that says 'open the app and find request 1042' wastes time. A deep link carries the record ID in the app URL. The app reads it with Param, chooses its start screen and loads the record. The same link works from email, Teams and other apps.
problemStatement: Approval emails link to the app's home screen. Approvers then search for the request, and some approve the wrong one.
whenToUse: Links in emails, Teams messages and Adaptive Cards
Opening an app from another app or a SharePoint column
QR codes that open a specific asset or location
whenNotToUse: Passing sensitive data in the URL, which is logged and shared
Treating the parameter as proof of access rights
formulaOrCode:
The link
  https://apps.powerapps.com/play/e/<environment id>/a/<app id>?tenantId=<tenant id>&RequestId=1042&screen=detail
  Get the base from make.powerapps.com > Apps > ... > Details > Web link. Append your own parameters with &.
  Parameter names are case-insensitive. Values are text.
  Hide the Power Apps header: &hidenavbar=true          Source tag for analytics: &source=email

Read parameters once (App.Formulas, named formulas)
  nfRequestId  = Value(Param("RequestId"));
  nfDeepLinked = !IsBlank(Param("RequestId"));
  nfDeepRecord = If(nfDeepLinked, LookUp(Requests, ID = nfRequestId));

Start on the right screen
  App.StartScreen
    If(nfDeepLinked && !IsBlank(nfDeepRecord), scrDetail, scrHome)
  StartScreen is evaluated before OnStart finishes and must not depend on variables set there. Named
  formulas and Param are safe.

Detail screen
  Use one variable for the record whichever way the user arrived:
  scrDetail.OnVisible
    If(IsBlank(gblSelected) && nfDeepLinked, Set(gblSelected, nfDeepRecord))
  Gallery OnSelect elsewhere:  Set(gblSelected, ThisItem); Navigate(scrDetail)
  Form.Item: gblSelected
  Back button: If(nfDeepLinked && IsBlank(gblCameFromList), Navigate(scrHome), Back())

Record missing or no access
  StartScreen falls back to scrHome when the lookup is blank. Tell the user why:
  scrHome.OnVisible
    If(nfDeepLinked && IsBlank(nfDeepRecord),
       Notify("Request " & Param("RequestId") & " was not found or you do not have access.", NotificationType.Warning))

GUID keys (Dataverse)
  nfDeepRecord = If(!IsBlank(Param("id")) && IsMatch(Param("id"), "^[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}$"),
                    LookUp(Requests, Request = GUID(Param("id"))));
  Validate before converting: GUID() errors on malformed text.

Build the link in a flow
  Environment variable AppUrl = the web link. In the email or card:
  Pick the AppUrl environment variable from dynamic content, then add:
  &RequestId=@{triggerOutputs()?['body/ID']}
  Text values: @{encodeUriComponent(triggerOutputs()?['body/Title'])}

Build the link inside the app (share button)
  With({ base: "https://apps.powerapps.com/play/e/" & gblEnvId & "/a/" & gblAppId & "?tenantId=" & gblTenantId },
       Copy(base & "&RequestId=" & gblSelected.ID));
  Notify("Link copied", NotificationType.Success)
  (Copy needs a user action such as OnSelect. Keep IDs in environment variables or app constants.)

Open another app with parameters
  Launch("https://apps.powerapps.com/play/e/<env>/a/<other app id>", { RequestId: gblSelected.ID, mode: "edit" }, LaunchTarget.New)
  Launch("/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/apps/<other app id>", { RequestId: gblSelected.ID })     same environment

Teams and mobile
  Teams tab deep link: put the ID in subEntityId and read Param("subEntityId").
  Power Apps mobile: the same web link opens the app in the player if installed.
  Parameters are read at launch. If the app is already open in a tab, the link starts a new session.

SharePoint column link
  JSON column formatting: "elmType": "a", "attributes": { "href": "='https://apps.powerapps.com/play/e/<env>/a/<app>?tenantId=<t>&RequestId=' + [$ID]", "target": "_blank" }

Model-driven app equivalent
  https://<org>.crm.dynamics.com/main.aspx?appid=<app id>&pagetype=entityrecord&etn=cr1a2_request&id=<guid>
stepByStepInstructions: Copy the app's web link and decide the parameter names.
Read parameters with Param in named formulas.
Set App.StartScreen to the detail screen when a valid record is found.
Load the record into the same variable the gallery uses.
Handle missing records with a clear message.
Generate links in flows from an environment variable holding the app URL.
commonMistakes: Reading Param in OnStart and expecting StartScreen to see the variable.
Hard-coding the app URL in every flow.
No handling when the record does not exist or is not permitted.
Putting names or other personal data in the query string.
troubleshooting: If the app opens on the home screen, check the parameter name and that the lookup returns a record for that user.
If Value() errors, the parameter is blank or not numeric. Guard with IsBlank.
If the link opens the wrong environment's app, use the web link from the right environment.
If parameters are ignored, the URL probably has two question marks. Join extra parameters with &.
seoTitle: Open a canvas app on a specific record with a deep link
seoDescription: Pass a record ID in the app's URL, read it with Param, start on the detail screen and build links for emails and Teams messages.
primaryKeyword: Power Apps deep link Param record

faqs.question: How do I open a Power App to a specific record?
faqs.answer: Add the record ID to the app's URL as a parameter, read it with Param and set App.StartScreen to the detail screen.

faqs.question: Can I pass several parameters?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add them to the URL separated by & and read each with Param.

faqs.question: Why can't StartScreen use my OnStart variable?
faqs.answer: StartScreen is evaluated independently of OnStart. Use Param or named formulas in it.

title: Create a PDF of a screen with the PDF function
shortDescription: Lay out a print-friendly screen or container, generate a PDF from it in the app, preview it and send it to a flow to email or save.
fullDescription: The PDF function turns a screen or a container into a PDF file inside the app, with no premium connector. Combined with a flow, the file can be saved to SharePoint or emailed. Good results depend on designing a dedicated print layout and knowing what the function will and will not capture.
problemStatement: Users need a signed-off summary of a request as a PDF. Printing the screen from the browser cuts off the gallery and includes buttons and navigation.
whenToUse: Summaries, receipts and inspection reports
Capturing a record's state at approval
Sending a formatted copy by email
whenNotToUse: Long data lists of hundreds of rows, where a server-generated document is more reliable
Layouts relying on controls the function cannot render
formulaOrCode:
Enable
  Settings > Upcoming features > Experimental > PDF function: On
  Microsoft labels the PDF function experimental, so treat it as not for production.

Print layout
  A dedicated screen scrPrint, or a container conPrint, sized like a page:
    Portrait Letter at 96 dpi: Width 816, Height 1056        A4: 794 x 1123
  Use vertical containers with fixed widths. White fill, dark text, no buttons inside the print container.
  Gallery of lines: set its Height to the content so nothing scrolls:
    galLines.Height = CountRows(galLines.AllItems) * galLines.TemplateHeight + 10
  Container: LayoutOverflowY = Scroll off, Height grows with content (Flexible height in an auto-layout parent).

Generate and preview
  btnPdf.OnSelect
    Set(gblPdf, PDF(conPrint, { Size: PaperSize.A4, Orientation: PaperOrientation.Portrait,
                               Margin: "20px", DPI: 150, ExpandContainers: true }));
  PDF viewer control on the same or another screen:   Document: gblPdf
  Options
    Size: PaperSize.Letter | A4 | Legal ...        Orientation: Portrait | Landscape
    Margin: "20px" or "10px 20px 10px 20px"        DPI: 96 default. Higher is sharper and larger.
    ExpandContainers: true expands scrollable galleries and containers so all rows are included
      (up to the function's limits). Without it, only the visible part is captured.

Send to a flow (Power Apps (V2) trigger with a File input)
  Flow: trigger input "file" (File), "requestId" (Number), "sendTo" (Email)
        SharePoint > Create file: Folder /Requests/REQ-<id>, File Name: Summary-<id>.pdf,
                     File Content: triggerBody()?['file']?['contentBytes']
        Office 365 Outlook > Send an email (V2): Attachments Name Summary-<id>.pdf, Content: same contentBytes
        Respond to a PowerApp or flow: link (text)
  App:
    Set(gblSaving, true);
    Set(gblResult,
        SaveRequestPdf.Run(
            { file: { name: "Summary-" & gblSelected.ID & ".pdf", contentBytes: gblPdf } },
            gblSelected.ID, User().Email));
    Set(gblSaving, false);
    Notify("PDF saved", NotificationType.Success)
  Wrap with IfError to report failures.

Save without a flow (attachment on the list item)
  Not directly: Patch cannot write a blob to an attachments field outside a form. Use the flow, or
  a Dataverse File column:  Patch(Requests, gblSelected, { SummaryFile: { FileName: "Summary.pdf", Value: gblPdf } })

What is captured and what is not
  Captured: labels, HTML text, images already loaded, shapes, galleries, containers, charts in most cases.
  Not reliably captured: embedded Power BI tiles, maps, PCF components, some modern controls, videos, web
  views, content from other screens, and nested galleries beyond one level.
  Images from authenticated sources must have finished loading. Use a short Loading state before generating.
  Fonts are substituted with standard fonts where needed.
  Size: the result must fit app memory and the flow's file input limit. Keep under about 20 MB.
  PDF can only target the current screen or controls on it. Navigate to scrPrint first:
    Navigate(scrPrint); then a button on that screen generates the file. Or keep conPrint on the current
    screen positioned off-canvas (X: -2000) so users never see it.

Header, footer and page breaks
  There is no page-break control. Design so content flows as one tall container, and expect breaks where the
  page height falls. Put a small header inside the container. Page numbers are not available.

Alternatives
  Print(): opens the browser print dialog for the current screen (users choose Save as PDF).
  Word template in a flow: best for multi-page documents with headers, footers and page numbers.
stepByStepInstructions: Enable the PDF function in the app settings.
Build a print container sized to the page with no interactive controls.
Make galleries and containers expand to their content height.
Call PDF on the container and show the result in a PDF viewer.
Pass the file to a flow that saves or emails it.
Test with the longest realistic record and on the devices users have.
commonMistakes: Capturing the working screen with buttons and navigation.
A scrolling gallery, so only the first rows appear.
Generating before images have loaded.
Relying on unsupported controls such as embedded reports.
troubleshooting: If rows are missing, set ExpandContainers to true and size the gallery to its content.
If the PDF is blurry, raise DPI to 150 or 200.
If the flow receives an empty file, pass contentBytes from the file object and use the V2 trigger with a File input.
If the function is not recognised, turn the feature on in settings and save and reopen the app.
seoTitle: Create a PDF of a screen with the PDF function
seoDescription: Lay out a print-friendly screen or container, generate a PDF from it in the app, preview it and send it to a flow to email or save.

faqs.question: Can Power Apps generate a PDF?
faqs.answer: Yes. The PDF function creates a PDF from a screen or container, which you can preview or pass to a flow.

faqs.question: How do I save the PDF to SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Send it to a flow with a file input and use Create file with the file's content.

faqs.question: Why does my PDF cut off gallery rows?
faqs.answer: The gallery scrolls. Expand containers in the PDF options and size the gallery to show all rows.

title: Load data in parallel with Concurrent
shortDescription: Run independent data calls at the same time instead of one after another, to cut start-up and screen load times, and know when it does not help.
fullDescription: Formulas separated by semicolons run in sequence: four one-second calls take four seconds. Concurrent runs its arguments in parallel, so the same four calls finish in about the time of the slowest. It suits independent loads at app start or screen entry. It is not for steps that depend on each other.
problemStatement: The app takes seven seconds to open, because OnStart fills five collections one after another.
whenToUse: Several independent ClearCollect or Set calls at start-up
Screen OnVisible that loads unrelated data sets
Calling several flows or connectors whose results do not depend on each other
whenNotToUse: Steps where one needs another's result
Dozens of parallel calls, which hit connector throttling and browser connection limits
formulaOrCode:
Before (sequential, about the sum of all calls)
  ClearCollect(colCategories, Categories);
  ClearCollect(colSites, Filter(Sites, Active));
  Set(gblProfile, Office365Users.MyProfileV2());
  ClearCollect(colMyOpen, Filter(Requests, Requester.Email = User().Email && Status.Value = "Open"));

After (parallel, about the slowest single call)
  Concurrent(
      ClearCollect(colCategories, Categories),
      ClearCollect(colSites, Filter(Sites, Active)),
      Set(gblProfile, Office365Users.MyProfileV2()),
      ClearCollect(colMyOpen, Filter(Requests, Requester.Email = User().Email && Status.Value = "Open"))
  );
  Set(gblLoaded, true)

Rules
  Arguments are separated by commas. Each argument can be a chain joined with semicolons:
    Concurrent(
        ClearCollect(colA, SourceA); Set(gblCountA, CountRows(colA)),
        ClearCollect(colB, SourceB)
    )
  Inside one argument, order is kept. Across arguments, order is not guaranteed.
  Do not have one argument read a variable or collection that another argument writes.
  Do not write the same variable or collection from two arguments.
  Concurrent returns when every argument has finished. Formulas after it can use all results.
  Only behaviour properties (OnStart, OnVisible, OnSelect, OnChange, timers) can use it.

Dependent data: sequence the dependency, parallelise the rest
  Set(gblProfile, Office365Users.MyProfileV2());                    // needed by the calls below
  Concurrent(
      ClearCollect(colMyDept, Filter(Requests, Department = gblProfile.department)),
      ClearCollect(colMyApprovals, Filter(Approvals, Approver.Email = gblProfile.mail)),
      ClearCollect(colCategories, Categories)
  )

Measure it
  Before and after, in a label or Monitor:
    Set(gblT0, Now()); Concurrent( ... ); Set(gblLoadMs, DateDiff(gblT0, Now(), TimeUnit.Milliseconds))
  Advanced tools > Monitor shows each network call with duration and whether calls overlap.

Errors
  If one argument fails, the others still run. Wrap each in IfError to control messages:
    Concurrent(
        IfError(ClearCollect(colSites, Filter(Sites, Active)), Notify("Sites did not load", NotificationType.Warning)),
        IfError(ClearCollect(colCategories, Categories), Notify("Categories did not load", NotificationType.Warning))
    )

Limits to expectations
  Browsers allow roughly six parallel connections per host: more than six calls to the same service queue up.
  Connector throttling applies. Keep to four to six arguments.
  It does not speed up a single slow, non-delegable query. Fix the query.
  Collections still copy at most the data row limit (500 by default, up to 10,000) per ClearCollect.

Often better than loading at start
  Named formulas (App.Formulas) load on first use and need no OnStart at all:
    nfCategories = Sort(Categories, Title);
  Reference data source tables directly in galleries with delegable filters instead of collecting.
  Load screen-specific data in that screen's OnVisible, not in OnStart.
  Settings > Performance: explicit column selection and delayed load are on by default. Leave them on.

Show a loading state
  App.StartScreen stays visible while OnStart runs. On screens:
    OnVisible: Set(locLoading, true); Concurrent( ... ); Set(locLoading, false)
    Spinner or overlay Visible: locLoading
stepByStepInstructions: List the data calls in OnStart or OnVisible and mark which depend on others.
Run dependencies first in sequence.
Wrap the independent calls in one Concurrent.
Avoid two arguments writing the same variable or collection.
Wrap arguments in IfError where a failure needs a message.
Measure load time in Monitor before and after.
commonMistakes: Putting dependent steps in separate arguments.
Twenty parallel calls that trigger throttling.
Using Concurrent to mask a slow non-delegable query.
Loading everything at start when most screens never need it.
troubleshooting: If a collection is sometimes empty, another argument used it before it loaded. Sequence those two.
If there is no speed gain, calls are queued by the browser or one slow call dominates. Check Monitor.
If you get throttling errors, reduce the number of arguments.
If the formula bar shows an error, check arguments are separated by commas, not semicolons.
seoTitle: Load data in parallel with Concurrent
seoDescription: Run independent data calls at the same time instead of one after another, to cut start-up and screen load times, and know when it does not help.

faqs.question: What does Concurrent do in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: It evaluates several formulas at the same time instead of in sequence, which shortens load times for independent data calls.

faqs.question: Can formulas inside Concurrent depend on each other?
faqs.answer: No. Order across arguments is not guaranteed. Run dependent steps before or after it.

faqs.question: How many calls should I put in Concurrent?
faqs.answer: Four to six is a sensible maximum, because browsers and connectors limit parallel requests.

title: Reuse logic with user-defined functions in Power Apps
shortDescription: Write a calculation or check once in App.Formulas with typed parameters, then call it anywhere, in place of copied formulas or hidden buttons.
fullDescription: Canvas apps used to repeat the same formula in many controls, or abuse a hidden button's OnSelect as a subroutine. User-defined functions put the logic in one place, with named, typed parameters and a typed result. They are declared alongside named formulas and can be pure calculations or, with behaviour functions enabled, actions that change data.
problemStatement: The rule for whether a request can be edited is copied into nine DisplayMode properties. When the rule changes, two copies are missed.
whenToUse: Business rules used in several controls or screens
Formatting and calculation helpers
Shared actions such as save-and-log
whenNotToUse: One-off formulas used in a single place
Apps that must run on a version where the feature is not yet available to you
stepByStepInstructions: Turn on user-defined functions in the app's settings.
Find formulas repeated across controls.
Declare each as a typed function in App.Formulas.
Replace the copies with calls to the function.
Use the brace form for functions that patch data or navigate.
Keep delegable filters inline and document each function with a comment.
commonMistakes: Calling a function inside a data source Filter and losing delegation.
Trying to Patch from a pure function.
Names that collide with controls or built-in functions.
Moving logic into functions without checking the feature is available in every environment.
troubleshooting: If the function is not recognised, enable the feature and check the declaration ends with a semicolon.
If you get a type error, convert arguments explicitly, for example Value() or Text().
If a delegation warning appears, move the function call outside the delegable part of the query.
If a behaviour function cannot be called, you are in a non-behaviour property such as Text or Items.
seoTitle: Reuse logic with user-defined functions in Power Apps
seoDescription: Write a calculation or check once in App.Formulas with typed parameters, then call it anywhere, in place of copied formulas or hidden buttons.

faqs.question: Can I create my own functions in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Yes. Declare user-defined functions in App.Formulas with typed parameters and a return type.

faqs.question: Can a user-defined function change data?
faqs.answer: Yes, when written as a behaviour function with its body in curly braces and called from a behaviour property.

faqs.question: Do user-defined functions affect delegation?
faqs.answer: A function used inside a data source query is evaluated locally, so keep delegable conditions inline.

title: Refresh data and autosave drafts with a Timer
shortDescription: Use a hidden Timer control to refresh a dashboard on an interval, autosave a draft while the user types, show a countdown and debounce a search box.
