fullDescription: Canvas apps have no background scheduler, but a Timer control fires an event at an interval while its screen is open. That is enough for refreshing a queue, saving drafts so work is not lost, and delaying a search until the user stops typing. The control needs a few properties set correctly to repeat and to stay out of sight.
problemStatement: A wall-mounted queue dashboard shows stale data until someone taps refresh, and users lose half-completed forms when a session times out.
whenToUse: Dashboards and queues that should stay current
Draft forms on long or mobile sessions
Search-as-you-type against a slow source
whenNotToUse: Intervals of a few seconds against connectors, which burns API calls
Expecting timers to run when the app or screen is not open
formulaOrCode:
Timer basics
  Duration: milliseconds per cycle (30000 = 30 seconds). Maximum 24 hours.
  Repeat: true          AutoStart: true          Visible: false
  Start: a boolean. The timer starts when Start changes from false to true.
  OnTimerEnd: runs at the end of each cycle.      OnTimerStart: at the beginning.
  A timer only runs while its screen is displayed. AutoPause pauses it when navigating away (default true).

1. Auto-refresh a queue
  tmrRefresh: Duration 60000, Repeat true, AutoStart true, Visible false
  OnTimerEnd:
    If(!locEditing,                                  // do not disturb someone mid-edit
       Refresh(Requests);
       Set(locLastRefresh, Now()))
  Label: "Updated " & Text(locLastRefresh, "hh:mm:ss")
  For a collection-based view: ClearCollect(colQueue, Filter(Requests, Status.Value = "Open")) instead of Refresh.
  Pick the longest interval the business accepts: 60 seconds is 60 calls an hour per open session.

2. Autosave a draft
  Track changes: each input's OnChange: Set(locDirty, true)
  tmrAutosave: Duration 20000, Repeat true, AutoStart true
  OnTimerEnd:
    If(locDirty && !locSaving,
       Set(locSaving, true);
       IfError(
           Set(gblDraft,
               Patch(Requests, Coalesce(gblDraft, Defaults(Requests)),
                     { Title: txtTitle.Text, Details: txtDetails.Text, Status: { Value: "Draft" } }));
           Set(locDirty, false); Set(locSavedAt, Now()),
           Notify("Draft not saved: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Warning));
       Set(locSaving, false))
  Label: If(locSaving, "Saving", !IsBlank(locSavedAt), "Draft saved " & Text(locSavedAt, "hh:mm"), "")
  The first save creates the row and stores it in gblDraft. Later saves update the same row.
  Offline or local-only alternative: SaveData(colDraft, "requestDraft") on the same timer (mobile player and
  supported browsers).

3. Debounce a search box (search after the user pauses)
  txtSearch.OnChange: Set(locSearchStart, false); Set(locSearchStart, true)
  txtSearch.DelayOutput: true           built-in half-second delay before Text updates. Often enough by itself.
  tmrSearch: Duration 600, Repeat false, AutoStart false, Start: locSearchStart
  OnTimerEnd: Set(locSearchText, txtSearch.Text); Set(locSearchStart, false)
  Gallery.Items: Filter(Requests, StartsWith(Title, locSearchText))
  Toggling Start false then true restarts the countdown on each keystroke.

4. Countdown display
  tmrCountdown: Duration 1000, Repeat true, AutoStart true
  OnTimerEnd: Set(locSecondsLeft, Max(0, DateDiff(Now(), gblDeadline, TimeUnit.Seconds)))
  Label: Text(RoundDown(locSecondsLeft / 60, 0), "00") & ":" & Text(Mod(locSecondsLeft, 60), "00")
  At zero: If(locSecondsLeft = 0, Set(locExpired, true))
  Compute from a fixed deadline, not by subtracting one each tick, so the display stays accurate if a tick is late.

5. Splash screen or timed message
  tmrSplash: Duration 2000, AutoStart true, Repeat false        OnTimerEnd: Navigate(scrHome, ScreenTransition.Fade)
  Toast: Set(locShowToast, true) > timer Start: locShowToast, Duration 3000 > OnTimerEnd: Set(locShowToast, false)

6. Session inactivity warning
  Any interaction: Set(gblLastActive, Now())  (put in key OnSelect/OnChange handlers)
  tmrIdle: Duration 60000, Repeat true
  OnTimerEnd: If(DateDiff(gblLastActive, Now(), TimeUnit.Minutes) >= 15, Navigate(scrIdleWarning))

Good practice
  One timer per purpose, named for it. Hide timers with Visible false, not by placing them off-screen.
  Guard OnTimerEnd with conditions so it does nothing when nothing changed.
  Timers stop when the device sleeps or the tab is suspended. Refresh on OnVisible as well.
  Server-side schedules belong in Power Automate, not in an app timer.
stepByStepInstructions: Add a Timer control and set Duration, Repeat, AutoStart and Visible.
Put the refresh or save logic in OnTimerEnd with guard conditions.
Track unsaved changes with a dirty flag for autosave.
Use a non-repeating timer restarted on each keystroke to debounce search.
Show the user when data was last refreshed or saved.
Choose the longest interval that meets the need.
commonMistakes: Refreshing every few seconds.
Saving on every tick whether or not anything changed.
Expecting a timer on another screen to keep running.
Counting down by decrementing a variable, which drifts.
troubleshooting: If the timer never fires, check AutoStart or that Start changes from false to true.
If it runs once only, set Repeat to true.
If autosave creates several rows, keep the saved record in a variable and patch that record next time.
If refresh interrupts editing, skip it while an edit flag is set.
seoTitle: Refresh data and autosave drafts with a Timer
seoDescription: Use a hidden Timer control to refresh a dashboard on an interval, autosave a draft while the user types, show a countdown and debounce a search box.

faqs.question: How do I auto-refresh a gallery in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Add a hidden Timer with Repeat and AutoStart on, and call Refresh on the data source in OnTimerEnd.

faqs.question: Can Power Apps autosave a form?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use a repeating timer that patches the current values when a dirty flag is set.

faqs.question: Do timers run in the background?
faqs.answer: No. A timer runs only while its screen is open and the app is active.

title: Capture a signature with the Pen input control and save it
shortDescription: Collect a handwritten signature, check that something was actually drawn, and store it in a Dataverse image column or a SharePoint library through a flow.
fullDescription: Delivery notes, inspections and consent forms need a signature on the device. The Pen input control captures strokes as an image. The awkward parts are knowing whether the user signed, clearing the pad, and saving the image somewhere durable, since SharePoint lists do not accept it directly from Patch in every column type.
problemStatement: A field technician needs the customer to sign for completed work on a tablet. The app has a pen control, but the saved record shows no signature, or a blank white image.
whenToUse: Proof of delivery and work completion
Inspection sign-off
Consent and acknowledgement forms
whenNotToUse: Legally binding e-signatures that need identity verification and audit trails, which call for a dedicated signing service
Typed-name acknowledgements, where a check box and timestamp are simpler
formulaOrCode:
Control set-up
  Insert > Input > Pen input            name: penSignature
    Mode: PenMode.Draw        ShowControls: false (hide the built-in toolbar)
    Color: Color.Black        Size: 3        Fill: Color.White        BorderThickness: 1
  Label above: "Sign in the box"       Button: Clear       Button: Save

Clear the pad
  btnClear.OnSelect: Reset(penSignature)

Has the user signed?
  Pen input has no "is empty" property. Track strokes with OnSelect, which fires when a stroke ends:
    penSignature.OnSelect: Set(locSigned, true)
    btnClear.OnSelect:     Reset(penSignature); Set(locSigned, false)
    btnSave.DisplayMode:   If(locSigned && !locSaving, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.Disabled)

A. Save to a Dataverse image column (simplest)
  Patch('Work Orders', gblOrder, { 'Customer Signature': penSignature.Image, 'Signed On': Now(), 'Signed By Name': txtName.Text })
  Show it later: Image control > Image: gblOrder.'Customer Signature'

B. Save to a SharePoint image column
  Patch(WorkOrders, gblOrder, { CustomerSignature: penSignature.Image, SignedOn: Now() })
  Image columns accept the pen image in current versions. If the column stays empty in your environment, use C.

C. Save as a file through a flow (works everywhere, keeps a real PNG)
  Flow: Power Apps (V2) trigger
    Inputs: file (File), orderId (Number), signerName (Text)
    SharePoint > Create file
      Folder Path: /Signatures/@{formatDateTime(utcNow(),'yyyy-MM')}
      File Name:   WO-@{triggerBody()?['number']}-signature.png
      File Content: @{triggerBody()?['file']?['contentBytes']}
    SharePoint > Update item (Work Orders): SignatureLink = file link, SignedOn = utcNow(), SignedByName = signerName
    Respond to a PowerApp or flow: link (Text)
  App:
    Set(locSaving, true);
    IfError(
        Set(locResult, SaveSignature.Run({ file: { name: "signature.png", contentBytes: penSignature.Image } },
                                         gblOrder.ID, txtName.Text));
        Reset(penSignature); Set(locSigned, false);
        Notify("Signature saved", NotificationType.Success),
        Notify("Could not save the signature: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error));
    Set(locSaving, false)

D. As a list item attachment (inside an edit form)
  The Attachments control cannot take a pen image directly. Use the flow with SharePoint > Add attachment
  (Id = item ID, File Name, File Content from the file input).

E. Base64 text when a flow or API needs a string
  With({ j: JSON(penSignature.Image, JSONFormat.IncludeBinaryData) },
       Set(locBase64, Mid(j, Find(",", j) + 1, Len(j) - Find(",", j) - 1)))
  JSON returns "data:image/png;base64,...." in quotes. The formula strips the prefix and closing quote.
  In a flow: base64ToBinary(triggerBody()['text'])

Make it usable
  Size the pad at least 600 x 200 on tablets. On phones, use a landscape signing screen.
  White fill and black ink: the image has the control's fill as background, so a transparent or dark fill
  produces unreadable results when printed.
  Capture the signer's printed name and the timestamp beside the signature.
  Lock the record after signing (status Signed, form in View mode) so the signature relates to fixed content.
  Store who operated the device: User().Email.

Display and print
  Image control bound to the stored image or the file link. Include it in a PDF summary container.
  SharePoint file link in an Image control: the user needs access to the file, and the app needs the
  SharePoint connection.

Offline
  Keep the image in a collection and SaveData it. Sync when Connection.Connected:
    Collect(colPending, { OrderId: gblOrder.ID, Sig: penSignature.Image, Name: txtName.Text, At: Now() });
    SaveData(colPending, "pendingSignatures")
stepByStepInstructions: Add a Pen input with a white fill, black ink and hidden toolbar.
Track whether a stroke was made and provide a clear button.
Capture the signer's name and time with the signature.
Save the image to a Dataverse image column or send it to a flow that creates a PNG file.
Reset the pad and lock the record after saving.
Test on the actual devices, including small screens.
commonMistakes: Allowing save with an empty pad.
Transparent or coloured fill that prints badly.
Patching a pen image to a column type that cannot hold it and not checking the result.
No name or timestamp alongside the signature.
troubleshooting: If the saved image is blank, the control was reset before saving. Save first, then reset.
If the flow file is corrupt, pass contentBytes from the file object using the V2 trigger with a File input.
If the save button never enables, set the flag in the pen's OnSelect.
If the image will not display from SharePoint, check the user's access to the library.
seoTitle: Capture a signature with the Pen input control and save it
seoDescription: Collect a handwritten signature, check that something was actually drawn, and store it in a Dataverse image column or a SharePoint library through a flow.
primaryKeyword: Power Apps signature pen input save

faqs.question: How do I capture a signature in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Use the Pen input control and save its Image property to an image column or pass it to a flow that creates a file.

faqs.question: How do I check whether the user signed?
faqs.answer: Set a variable in the pen control's OnSelect, which fires after a stroke, and clear it when the pad is reset.

faqs.question: Can I save a signature to SharePoint?
faqs.answer: Yes, to an image column, or as a PNG file or attachment created by a flow.

title: Open email, phone, maps and other apps with Launch
shortDescription: Start a prefilled email, a phone call, a Teams chat, a map route or a web page from a button, with parameters encoded correctly for mobile and web.
fullDescription: Launch opens a URL or another app. With the right address scheme the same function starts an email draft, dials a number, opens directions or starts a Teams chat with someone. It keeps apps light: the device's own tools do the job, with the app supplying the details.
problemStatement: A contacts app shows a phone number and an address as plain text. Field staff copy them by hand into the dialler and the maps app.
whenToUse: Contact actions: call, email, chat
Directions to a site or customer
Opening documents, reports and other apps
whenNotToUse: Sending email silently, which needs a connector or flow, not Launch
Passing long bodies in a URL, which are cut off around 2,000 characters
formulaOrCode:
Syntax
  Launch(Address [, Parameters [, Target]])
  Launch("https://contoso.com/help", {}, LaunchTarget.New)
  Target: LaunchTarget.New (new tab), LaunchTarget.Replace (same tab), LaunchTarget.Blank, or a named tab.
  Parameters record is added to the query string and encoded for you:
    Launch("https://www.bing.com/search", { q: "power apps " & txtTerm.Text })

Email draft (user's default mail app)
  Launch("mailto:" & ThisItem.Email &
         "?subject=" & EncodeUrl("Request " & ThisItem.RequestNumber) &
         "&body=" & EncodeUrl("Hello " & ThisItem.FirstName & "," & Char(13) & Char(10) & "About your request..."))
  Several recipients: separate with commas (semicolons for Outlook desktop). cc= and bcc= work the same way.
  The user still presses Send. To send without a draft, use Office365Outlook.SendEmailV2.

Phone, SMS
  Launch("tel:" & Substitute(Substitute(ThisItem.Phone, " ", ""), "-", ""))
  Launch("sms:" & ThisItem.Mobile & "?body=" & EncodeUrl("On my way"))        iOS uses &body= in some versions
  Works on phones. On desktop it opens the default calling app if one is registered.

Teams
  Chat:   Launch("https://teams.microsoft.com/l/chat/0/0?users=" & ThisItem.Email & "&message=" & EncodeUrl("Hi, about " & ThisItem.Title))
  Group:  users=a@contoso.com,b@contoso.com&topicName=Incident%20123
  Call:   Launch("https://teams.microsoft.com/l/call/0/0?users=" & ThisItem.Email)
  Meeting: Launch("https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meeting/new?subject=" & EncodeUrl(ThisItem.Title) & "&attendees=" & ThisItem.Email)
  Native scheme on mobile: "msteams://teams.microsoft.com/l/chat/0/0?users=..."

Maps
  Bing:    Launch("https://www.bing.com/maps?rtp=~adr." & EncodeUrl(ThisItem.Address))                 directions to an address
  Google:  Launch("https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=" & EncodeUrl(ThisItem.Address))
           Launch("https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=" & ThisItem.Latitude & "," & ThisItem.Longitude)
  Apple:   Launch("https://maps.apple.com/?daddr=" & EncodeUrl(ThisItem.Address))
  From the current position:  origin is the device location by default. To pass it:
           "&origin=" & Location.Latitude & "," & Location.Longitude

Documents and Microsoft 365
  SharePoint file in the browser: Launch(ThisItem.'{Link}')  or  Launch(ThisItem.'Link to item')
  Open in the desktop app:  Launch("ms-word:ofe|u|" & ThisItem.'{Link}')       ms-excel:, ms-powerpoint: likewise
  Power BI report with a filter:
    Launch("https://app.powerbi.com/groups/<ws>/reports/<id>/ReportSection", { filter: "Requests/Id eq " & ThisItem.ID })

Other Power Apps
  Canvas app: Launch("/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/apps/<app id>", { RequestId: ThisItem.ID })
  Model-driven record:
    Launch("https://contoso.crm.dynamics.com/main.aspx", { appid: "<app id>", pagetype: "entityrecord",
           etn: "cr1a2_request", id: Text(ThisItem.Request) })

Encoding
  Use EncodeUrl for anything typed by users or containing spaces, &, ? or #. The Parameters record encodes
  values automatically, which is the safer route for http(s) links. mailto:, tel: and sms: need EncodeUrl by hand.
  Line break in a mailto body: Char(13) & Char(10) inside EncodeUrl, or %0D%0A.

Guards
  btnCall.DisplayMode: If(IsBlank(ThisItem.Phone), DisplayMode.Disabled, DisplayMode.Edit)
  Validate web links before launching: If(StartsWith(Lower(ThisItem.Url), "https://"), Launch(ThisItem.Url))
  never Launch arbitrary text from data without checking the scheme.

Behaviour notes
  Launch must run from a user action (OnSelect). Browsers block pop-ups started from timers or OnStart.
  In the mobile player, links open in the device's default handler. Teams and Outlook open their apps if installed.
  Inside Teams, external links open in the browser, and Teams deep links stay in Teams.
  Download(url) is the companion function for saving a file to the device.
stepByStepInstructions: Choose the address scheme for the action: mailto, tel, https or an app link.
Build the address and encode user-supplied text.
Call Launch from the button's OnSelect with a target.
Disable the button when the needed value is blank.
Validate link schemes that come from data.
Test on web, mobile and inside Teams.
commonMistakes: Unencoded subjects and addresses that break the link.
Launching from OnStart or a timer and being blocked as a pop-up.
Expecting mailto to send the email automatically.
Launching unvalidated URLs stored in data.
troubleshooting: If the email body is cut off, shorten it. Mail clients limit URL length.
If nothing opens on desktop, the browser blocked a pop-up. Launch from a direct button press.
If Teams opens in the browser on mobile, use the msteams: scheme.
If special characters appear as codes or break the link, apply EncodeUrl once, not twice.
seoTitle: Open email, phone, maps and other apps with Launch
seoDescription: Start a prefilled email, a phone call, a Teams chat, a map route or a web page from a button, with parameters encoded correctly for mobile and web.

faqs.question: How do I open an email from Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Use Launch with a mailto: address and encoded subject and body. The user's mail app opens a draft.

faqs.question: How do I start a phone call from a canvas app?
faqs.answer: Launch("tel:" & number) on a phone opens the dialler with the number.

faqs.question: How do I open a link in a new tab?
faqs.answer: Pass LaunchTarget.New as the third argument to Launch.

title: Add page-by-page navigation to a gallery
shortDescription: Show a fixed number of rows per page with Next and Previous buttons and a page counter, for collections and for large delegable data sources.
fullDescription: Galleries scroll and load more rows as they go, which suits phones. Desktop users of a long table often want pages: a fixed row count, a page number and the total. For data already in a collection the maths is simple. For large sources, paging has to work with delegation, using a sortable key to fetch each page.
problemStatement: A table-style gallery of 1,800 rows scrolls endlessly. Users lose their place, cannot say 'it is on page 4', and the gallery height does not fit the screen design.
whenToUse: Desktop table layouts with a fixed number of visible rows
Reviewing long result sets methodically
Printing or exporting a page at a time
whenNotToUse: Mobile lists, where native scrolling is better
Very large sources without a filter, where search should narrow results first
formulaOrCode:
A. Data in a collection (up to the data row limit: 500 by default, up to 10,000)
  Screen OnVisible
    ClearCollect(colRows, SortByColumns(Filter(Requests, Status.Value = "Open"), "Created", SortOrder.Descending));
    Set(locPage, 1); Set(locPageSize, 15)
  Named values (or inline)
    locTotal = CountRows(colRows)
    locPages = Max(1, RoundUp(CountRows(colRows) / locPageSize, 0))

  Gallery.Items
    LastN(FirstN(colRows, locPage * locPageSize),
          Min(locPageSize, CountRows(colRows) - (locPage - 1) * locPageSize))
  FirstN takes everything up to the end of the current page. LastN keeps just this page.
  The Min handles a short last page.

  Buttons
    btnPrev.OnSelect:     Set(locPage, Max(1, locPage - 1))
    btnPrev.DisplayMode:  If(locPage > 1, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.Disabled)
    btnNext.OnSelect:     Set(locPage, Min(locPages, locPage + 1))
    btnNext.DisplayMode:  If(locPage < locPages, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.Disabled)
    btnFirst.OnSelect:    Set(locPage, 1)          btnLast.OnSelect: Set(locPage, locPages)
  Label
    "Page " & locPage & " of " & locPages & "  (" & CountRows(colRows) & " rows)"
    Rows shown: (locPage - 1) * locPageSize + 1 & " to " & Min(locPage * locPageSize, CountRows(colRows))

  Page-size drop-down:  Items [10, 15, 25, 50]     OnChange: Set(locPageSize, Self.Selected.Value); Set(locPage, 1)
  Search or filter changes:  reset to page 1:  txtSearch.OnChange: Set(locPage, 1)
  With a filter applied, compute pages from the filtered table:
    With({ f: Filter(colRows, StartsWith(Title, txtSearch.Text)) }, LastN(FirstN(f, ...), ...))

  Gallery height to fit exactly one page:  locPageSize * galRows.TemplateHeight   and turn off the scrollbar.

B. Row numbers on each page
  Label in the template:  (locPage - 1) * locPageSize + ThisItem.RowNo
  where Items is  ForAll(Sequence(CountRows(pageRows)), Patch(Index(pageRows, Value), { RowNo: Value }))
  or add a RowNo column once when collecting:
    ClearCollect(colRows, ForAll(Sequence(CountRows(src)), Patch(Index(src, Value), { RowNo: Value })))

C. Large delegable sources (more rows than a collection can hold): keyset paging
  Sort by a unique, indexed, increasing number column and fetch each page by key.
  SharePoint: the built-in ID column only delegates "=". Add an indexed Number column, for example SeqNo,
  set it to the item's ID when the item is created (a flow or the app's Patch), and page on that.
  Dataverse: page on an autonumber or created-on column in the same way.
  State: colPage (the current page), colPageStarts (stack of starting values for going back)

  First page
    ClearCollect(colPage, FirstN(Sort(Filter(Requests, SeqNo > 0), SeqNo, SortOrder.Ascending), locPageSize));
    Clear(colPageStarts); Collect(colPageStarts, { StartId: 0 })
  Next
    With({ last: Last(colPage).SeqNo },
        Collect(colPageStarts, { StartId: last });
        ClearCollect(colPage, FirstN(Sort(Filter(Requests, SeqNo > last), SeqNo, SortOrder.Ascending), locPageSize)))
  Previous
    Remove(colPageStarts, Last(colPageStarts));
    With({ start: Last(colPageStarts).StartId },
        ClearCollect(colPage, FirstN(Sort(Filter(Requests, SeqNo > start), SeqNo, SortOrder.Ascending), locPageSize)))
  Gallery.Items: colPage
  btnNext.DisplayMode: If(CountRows(colPage) = locPageSize, DisplayMode.Edit, DisplayMode.Disabled)
  Filter and Sort run at the source. FirstN then trims the result in the app, so each page request
  returns at most the data row limit (500 by default) and keeps the first page of it.
  Newest first: Sort descending and use SeqNo < last.
  Total page count is not known cheaply for large SharePoint lists (CountRows does not delegate). Show
  "Page 3" without "of N", or get a count from Dataverse with CountRows on a delegable filter (up to 50,000).

D. Dataverse or SQL with large sets
  Same keyset approach on the primary key or a created-on plus key combination. Avoid Skip-style paging by
  loading everything: it defeats the purpose.

Accessibility
  Buttons with AccessibleLabel "Next page", "Previous page". Announce page changes in a live label:
  Label.Live = Live.Polite, Text = "Page " & locPage & " of " & locPages
stepByStepInstructions: Decide the page size and whether the data fits in a collection.
Hold the current page number in a variable.
Set the gallery's Items to the slice for that page with FirstN and LastN.
Add Next, Previous, First and Last buttons with disabled states at the ends.
Reset to page 1 whenever search or filters change.
For large sources, fetch each page by key with a delegable filter and sort.
commonMistakes: Not handling the short last page.
Staying on page 9 after a filter reduces results to two pages.
Paging over a non-delegable query that only sees the first 500 rows.
Showing a total page count that the source cannot provide accurately.
troubleshooting: If the last page repeats earlier rows, cap LastN with the remaining row count.
If the gallery is empty after filtering, reset the page to 1.
If Next shows nothing on a big list, switch to keyset paging with a delegable filter on an indexed number column.
If row numbers restart on each page, add the page offset.
seoTitle: Add page-by-page navigation to a gallery
seoDescription: Show a fixed number of rows per page with Next and Previous buttons and a page counter, for collections and for large delegable data sources.

faqs.question: How do I paginate a gallery in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Keep a page number variable and set Items to LastN(FirstN(data, page * size), size), with buttons that change the page.

faqs.question: How do I page through more rows than the data row limit?
faqs.answer: Fetch each page from the source with a delegable filter on an indexed number column, sorted, using FirstN for the page size.

faqs.question: How do I show the total number of pages?
faqs.answer: Divide the row count by the page size and round up. For very large SharePoint lists the count is not available cheaply.

title: Translate a canvas app's labels by user language
shortDescription: Detect the user's language, keep translations in a table and look up every label through one small function, with a fallback and a language switcher.
fullDescription: Canvas apps have no built-in resource files. The standard approach is a translations table keyed by a text ID and language, loaded once, with labels calling a lookup. Language() gives the user's setting. Dates and numbers format themselves when Text is given a language tag. Done from the start it costs little, and retrofitting is a search-and-replace exercise.
problemStatement: An app built in English is rolled out to teams in France and Germany. Every label is typed into the control, so a translated version would mean maintaining three copies of the app.
whenToUse: Apps used across countries or language communities
Organisations with a legal duty to offer more than one language
Text that business owners want to edit without a release
whenNotToUse: Single-language apps with no prospect of translation
Translating data values in the app when the data source should hold them
formulaOrCode:
Translations source
  Option 1: SharePoint list or Dataverse table "App Translations": Key (text), Lang (text: en, fr, de), Value (text)
  Option 2: Excel imported as static data, or a table typed in App.Formulas for small apps:
    nfStrings = Table(
      { Key: "home.title",    en: "My requests",  fr: "Mes demandes",   de: "Meine Anfragen" },
      { Key: "btn.save",      en: "Save",         fr: "Enregistrer",    de: "Speichern" },
      { Key: "btn.cancel",    en: "Cancel",       fr: "Annuler",        de: "Abbrechen" },
      { Key: "msg.saved",     en: "Saved",        fr: "Enregistré",     de: "Gespeichert" },
      { Key: "err.required",  en: "{0} is required", fr: "{0} est obligatoire", de: "{0} ist erforderlich" }
    );

Detect the language
  Language()          "en-US", "fr-FR", "de-DE": the browser or device language
  App.Formulas
    nfSupported = ["en", "fr", "de"];
    nfDetected  = Lower(Left(Language(), 2));
  App.OnStart (a variable, so the user can switch it)
    Set(gblLang, If(nfDetected in nfSupported, nfDetected, "en"))

Lookup function
  With user-defined functions enabled (wide table above):
    T(key: Text): Text =
        With({ r: LookUp(nfStrings, Key = key) },
             Coalesce(Switch(gblLang, "fr", r.fr, "de", r.de, r.en), r.en, "[" & key & "]"));
  Long table (Key, Lang, Value) loaded once:
    App.OnStart: ClearCollect(colT, Filter('App Translations', Lang = gblLang Or Lang = "en"))
    T(key: Text): Text =
        Coalesce(LookUp(colT, Key = key && Lang = gblLang).Value, LookUp(colT, Key = key && Lang = "en").Value, "[" & key & "]");
  Without user-defined functions, use the LookUp inline, or a component with an input "Key" and output "Text".

Use it
  lblTitle.Text:        T("home.title")
  btnSave.Text:         T("btn.save")
  Notify(T("msg.saved"), NotificationType.Success)
  Hint text, tooltips, AccessibleLabel: translate these too.
  With values inserted:  Substitute(T("err.required"), "{0}", T("field.title"))
  Missing keys show as [key], which makes gaps obvious in testing.

Language switcher
  Dropdown Items: Table({ Code: "en", Name: "English" }, { Code: "fr", Name: "Français" }, { Code: "de", Name: "Deutsch" })
  Default: LookUp(Self.Items... ) or simply gblLang        OnChange: Set(gblLang, Self.Selected.Code)
  Long-table variant: reload colT for the new language in OnChange.
  Remember the choice: SaveData/LoadData on mobile, or a user settings row keyed by email.

Dates, numbers and currency
  Text(Today(), DateTimeFormat.LongDate, gblLang)                 "20 novembre 2026"
  Text(ThisItem.Due, "dd mmm yyyy", gblLang)
  Text(1234.5, "#,##0.00", gblLang)                               "1 234,50" in fr
  Month and weekday names:  Calendar.MonthsLong(gblLang), Calendar.WeekdaysShort(gblLang)
  Parsing typed numbers:  Value(txtAmount.Text, gblLang)   and dates:  DateValue(txtDate.Text, gblLang)
  A full tag such as "fr-CA" gives regional formats. Keep a second variable gblLocale if needed.

Choices and data values
  SharePoint choice labels are not translated per user. Map them:
    T("status." & ThisItem.Status.Value)       with keys status.Open, status.Closed ...
  Dataverse choice labels and table and column display names DO follow the user's Dataverse language when
  translations are imported into the solution. Model-driven apps handle that natively.

Layout
  German and French labels run 20 to 35 percent longer than English. Use auto-height labels, auto-layout
  containers and avoid fixed-width buttons sized for English.
  Right-to-left languages need mirrored layouts: align by a variable, for example
    Align: If(gblLang in ["ar","he"], Align.Right, Align.Left)

Process
  Keys named by area and purpose: screen.element. One owner per language reviews the list.
  Export the table to Excel for translators and re-import. Never translate inside formulas.
  Test each language end to end, including error messages and emails sent by flows (pass gblLang to the flow).
stepByStepInstructions: Create a translations table with a key and a value per language.
Detect the user's language and fall back to a default.
Write one lookup function or component that returns the text for a key.
Replace literal text in labels, buttons, hints and notifications with lookups.
Format dates and numbers with the language tag.
Add a language switcher and test layouts with the longest language.
commonMistakes: Typing translated text into If statements on every control.
No fallback when a key or language is missing.
Fixed-width controls sized for English.
Forgetting notifications, hint text and accessibility labels.
troubleshooting: If a label shows [key], add the key or check its spelling.
If dates stay in English, pass the language tag as the third argument to Text.
If switching language does not update a screen, the label reads a collection loaded for the old language. Reload it.
If numbers parse wrongly, give Value the same language the user types in.
seoTitle: Translate a canvas app's labels by user language
seoDescription: Detect the user's language, keep translations in a table and look up every label through one small function, with a fallback and a language switcher.
primaryKeyword: Power Apps multilingual app Language function

faqs.question: How do I make a Power Apps canvas app multilingual?
faqs.answer: Store translations in a table keyed by text ID and language, detect the language with Language() and look up each label's text.

faqs.question: How do I get the user's language in Power Apps?
faqs.answer: The Language function returns the language tag of the user's browser or device, such as fr-FR.

faqs.question: How do I format dates for the user's language?
faqs.answer: Pass the language tag to Text, for example Text(Today(), DateTimeFormat.LongDate, "fr").

title: Debug a slow or failing canvas app with Monitor and Trace
shortDescription: Use Monitor to see every data call, its duration and its errors, add your own Trace events, diagnose a user's session remotely and find delegation and load problems.
fullDescription: When an app is slow or a Patch fails for one user, guessing is expensive. Monitor records what the app actually does: each network request, formula evaluation and error, with timings and payloads. Trace adds your own checkpoints. A session can be shared with a user so you watch their run, with their permissions, from your machine.
problemStatement: Users report that a screen takes ten seconds to load and that saving 'sometimes fails'. In the studio, with the maker's permissions and data, everything looks fine.
whenToUse: Finding which query or formula makes a screen slow
Seeing the real error behind a failed save
Reproducing a problem only one user has
whenNotToUse: Leaving verbose tracing of personal data in a published app
Using Monitor as long-term telemetry, which Application Insights is for
formulaOrCode:
Open Monitor
  Studio: Advanced tools > Monitor > Open monitor. Then use the app in the studio tab. Events stream in.
  Published app: make.powerapps.com > Apps > ... > Details (or Monitor) > Play published app.
    Turn on "Debug published app" in the app's Settings and republish to get formula-level detail.
    Turn it off afterwards, because it slows the app for everyone.

Reading the grid
  Columns: Time, Category (Network, UserAction, Performance, Telemetry), Operation (getRows, createRow,
  patchRow, Select, Navigate), Result (Success, Error, Warning), Status (HTTP code), Duration (ms),
  Data source, Control, Property, Response size.
  Select a row: Details (what ran), Formula (the property's formula), Request (URL with the actual filter
  sent), Response (rows returned or the error body).
  Filter: Result = Error. Sort by Duration to find the slowest calls.

What to look for
  Slow screen
    Many getRows in sequence in OnVisible: parallelise with Concurrent or load less.
    getRows with a large response size: select fewer columns, filter at the source.
    The same getRows repeated per gallery row: a LookUp inside the template (N+1). Move it out with
    AddColumns once, or collect reference data.
  Delegation
    Request URL without a $filter where you expected one, and a row count equal to your data row limit
    (500 by default, up to 10,000): the filter ran locally on a partial set.
    Warning events mentioning delegation.
  Failed save
    patchRow or createRow with Result Error. Response shows the real cause: 400 with a column name,
    403 no permission, 409/412 conflict (someone else changed the row), 429 throttled.
  Slow start
    Time from the first event to the first screen render. OnStart with many collections. Consider named formulas.

Add your own events
  Trace(Message, Severity, CustomRecord)
    Trace("Save started", TraceSeverity.Information, { RequestId: gblSelected.ID, User: User().Email });
    IfError(
        Patch(Requests, gblSelected, { Status: { Value: "Approved" } }),
        Trace("Save failed", TraceSeverity.Error, { RequestId: gblSelected.ID, Kind: FirstError.Kind, Message: FirstError.Message });
        Notify("Could not save. " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error),
        Trace("Save succeeded", TraceSeverity.Information, { RequestId: gblSelected.ID }))
  Traces appear in Monitor with Category "Telemetry" and, if configured, in Application Insights.
  Severity: Information, Warning, Error, Critical.

Time a block
  Set(locT0, Now());
  ClearCollect(colOpen, Filter(Requests, Status.Value = "Open"));
  Trace("Load open requests", TraceSeverity.Information, { Ms: DateDiff(locT0, Now(), TimeUnit.Milliseconds), Rows: CountRows(colOpen) })

Watch another person's session
  Monitor > Invite: enter a colleague (maker) to view your session, or
  Monitor > Connect user: sends the USER a link. They open it and run the published app. You see their
  events with their permissions and data. Tell them what you will see: payloads include their data.

Global error handler
  App.OnError
    Trace("Unhandled error", TraceSeverity.Error,
          { Source: FirstError.Source, Observed: FirstError.Observed, Kind: FirstError.Kind,
            Message: FirstError.Message, Screen: App.ActiveScreen.Name });
    Notify("Something went wrong. Reference " & Text(Now(), "hhmmss"), NotificationType.Error)
  Catches errors nothing else handled, so they are logged instead of vanishing.

Keep it after go-live: Application Insights
  App object > Connection string, copied from an Application Insights resource.
  Trace events, errors and screen views flow there for all users. Query with KQL:
    traces | where timestamp > ago(1d) and severityLevel >= 3 | project timestamp, message, customDimensions
    pageViews | summarize count() by name
  Do not put personal data in trace records.

Other tools in the same menu
  App checker: formula errors, accessibility, performance hints, delegation warnings.
  Variables and Collections viewers: current values while testing.
  Performance insights (app details): start-up time and suggestions from real usage.

Export
  Monitor > Download: saves the session as JSON to attach to a support ticket or compare later. Upload reopens it.
stepByStepInstructions: Open Monitor from the studio or for the published app.
Reproduce the slow or failing action.
Sort by duration and filter by errors to find the event responsible.
Read the request and response for the true filter sent and the real error.
Add Trace calls around key operations and an App.OnError handler.
Connect a user's session when the problem is specific to them, and send traces to Application Insights for production.
commonMistakes: Testing only as the maker, with different permissions and data.
Guessing at the cause of a failed Patch without reading the response.
Tracing personal or sensitive data.
Ignoring repeated identical calls from inside a gallery.
troubleshooting: If Monitor shows no formula detail for a published app, enable debugging of the published app and republish.
If no events appear, the monitored session is in another tab. Use the tab Monitor opened.
If the error body is empty, look at the status code and the data source's own logs.
If Trace events are missing in Application Insights, check the connection string and allow a few minutes.
seoTitle: Debug a slow or failing canvas app with Monitor and Trace
seoDescription: Use Monitor to see every data call, its duration and its errors, add your own Trace events, diagnose a user's session remotely and find delegation and load problems.

faqs.question: How do I see why a Power App is slow?
faqs.answer: Open Monitor, reproduce the action and sort events by duration to find the slow data calls and their formulas.

faqs.question: How do I debug a problem that only one user has?
faqs.answer: Use Monitor's Connect user option so they run the app while you watch their session's events.

faqs.question: What does the Trace function do?
faqs.answer: It writes a custom event with a message, severity and data to Monitor and, if configured, Application Insights.

title: Show a progress bar in a SharePoint column with JSON formatting
shortDescription: Turn a number or percentage column into a coloured bar with the value beside it, change colour by threshold and handle blanks, using column formatting JSON.
fullDescription: A column of percentages is hard to scan. Column formatting replaces how a field is drawn in list views without changing the data. A few lines of JSON draw a bar whose width follows the value and whose colour follows thresholds, which makes progress readable at a glance in any view that includes the column.
problemStatement: A project list shows '% complete' as plain numbers. Managers cannot see at a glance which projects are behind.
whenToUse: Percent complete, capacity and score columns
Dashboards built from list views
Any numeric column with a known maximum
whenNotToUse: Columns people must edit inline in grid view, where plain values are easier
Conveying status by colour alone, without the number
formulaOrCode:
Where
  List view > column header > Column settings > Format this column > Advanced mode > paste > Save
  Works on Number columns. For a number shown as percentage, the stored value is 0 to 1 (0.45 = 45%).

A. Percentage column stored as 0 to 1
{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
  "elmType": "div",
  "style": { "display": "flex", "align-items": "center", "width": "100%" },
  "children": [
    {
      "elmType": "div",
      "style": { "flex-grow": "1", "height": "10px", "border-radius": "5px", "background-color": "#e1e1e1", "overflow": "hidden" },
      "attributes": { "title": "=toString(floor(@currentField * 100 + 0.5)) + '% complete'" },
      "children": [
        {
          "elmType": "div",
          "style": {
            "height": "100%",
            "width": "=if(@currentField >= 1, '100%', if(@currentField <= 0, '0%', toString(@currentField * 100) + '%'))",
            "background-color": "=if(@currentField >= 1, '#107c10', if(@currentField >= 0.5, '#0078d4', if(@currentField >= 0.25, '#ffaa44', '#d13438')))"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "elmType": "span",
      "style": { "margin-left": "8px", "min-width": "38px", "text-align": "right" },
      "txtContent": "=if(@currentField == '', '', toString(floor(@currentField * 100 + 0.5)) + '%')"
    }
  ]
}

B. Plain number out of a maximum held in another column (Done out of Total)
  "width": "=if([$Total] > 0, toString(([$Done] / [$Total]) * 100) + '%', '0%')"
  "txtContent": "=[$Done] + ' / ' + [$Total]"
  [$InternalName] reads another column in the same row. The column must be in the view, or it returns blank.

C. Number 0 to 100
  "width": "=toString(@currentField) + '%'"
  thresholds: "=if(@currentField >= 100, '#107c10', if(@currentField >= 50, '#0078d4', '#d13438'))"

D. Theme-aware classes instead of fixed colours
  Replace background-color with a class on the inner bar:
  "attributes": { "class": "=if(@currentField >= 1, 'sp-field-severity--good', if(@currentField >= 0.5, 'sp-field-severity--low', if(@currentField >= 0.25, 'sp-field-severity--warning', 'sp-field-severity--blocked')))" }
  Or theme colours: "ms-bgColor-themePrimary", "ms-bgColor-neutralLight".
  Classes adapt to site themes and dark mode in Teams.

E. Built-in data bar (no JSON)
  Format this column > Data bars > Edit template: minimum and maximum values and a colour.
  Choose JSON when you need thresholds, labels or another column's value.

Expression reference used above
  @currentField      this column's value          [$Column]     another column
  if(cond, a, b)     nested for thresholds         toString(), Number(), floor(n), ceiling(n). There is no round: use floor(n + 0.5)
  Operators: + - * /  ==  !=  <  >  <=  >=  &&  ||
  Text joins with +. Compare blanks with == ''.

Accessibility
  Keep the number beside the bar and put the meaning in the title attribute.
  Add "role": "img" and "aria-label" on the outer bar:
  "attributes": { "role": "img", "aria-label": "=toString(floor(@currentField * 100 + 0.5)) + ' percent complete'" }

Where it shows
  List views, the list web part and Microsoft Lists. Not in the classic experience, grid edit mode, exports to
  Excel or Power Apps galleries. The stored value is unchanged.

Reuse
  Apply the same JSON to a site column so every list using it gets the format, or deploy with PnP:
  Set-PnPField -List "Projects" -Identity "PercentComplete" -Values @{ CustomFormatter = (Get-Content .\progress.json -Raw) }
stepByStepInstructions: Confirm how the column stores its value: 0 to 1, or 0 to 100.
Open Format this column in advanced mode.
Paste the JSON and adjust thresholds and colours.
Keep the numeric value visible beside the bar.
Handle blank and over-100 values in the width expression.
Apply the format to the site column or deploy it with PnP for reuse.
commonMistakes: Treating a percentage column as 0 to 100 when it stores 0 to 1.
Referencing another column that is not in the view.
Colour as the only indicator.
A width expression that breaks on blank values.
troubleshooting: If the bar is always full or empty, check the value scale and multiply or divide by 100.
If the JSON will not save, validate brackets and quotes. Expressions start with = inside a string.
If another column's value is blank, add that column to the view.
If colours clash with the theme, switch to the sp-field-severity classes.
seoTitle: Show a progress bar in a SharePoint column with JSON formatting
seoDescription: Turn a number or percentage column into a coloured bar with the value beside it, change colour by threshold and handle blanks, using column formatting JSON.

faqs.question: How do I add a progress bar to a SharePoint list?
faqs.answer: Format the number column with JSON that draws an inner div whose width is the column's value as a percentage.

faqs.question: Why is my percentage bar always empty?
faqs.answer: Percentage columns store values from 0 to 1. Multiply by 100 when building the width.

faqs.question: Does column formatting change the data?
faqs.answer: No. It only changes how the value is displayed in modern list views.

title: Show or hide SharePoint list form fields with conditional formulas
shortDescription: Make the built-in list form show fields only when they apply, group fields into sections with form JSON, and pair it with validation, without building an app.
fullDescription: The standard SharePoint list form can react to what the user enters. Each column can carry a conditional formula that decides whether it appears, and the form's header, body and footer can be arranged with JSON. For many lists this removes the need for a customised Power Apps form.
problemStatement: A request form shows twenty fields to everyone, including a block that only applies to hardware requests. People fill in the wrong ones or give up.
whenToUse: Fields that apply only to some categories or statuses
Simple intake forms on lists
Lists where a custom app would be over-engineering
whenNotToUse: Cascading lookups, repeating sections or multi-screen flows, which need Power Apps
Using hidden fields as a security measure
formulaOrCode:
Open
  List > New (or open an item) > form toolbar: Edit form (icon at top right) > Edit columns
  Each column: tick to show, drag to reorder, ... > Edit conditional formula

Conditional formulas (must return true to SHOW the field)
  Show "Asset Tag" only for hardware:
    =if([$Category] == 'Hardware', 'true', 'false')
  Show "Other reason" when Reason is Other:
    =if([$Reason] == 'Other', 'true', 'false')
  Several values:
    =if([$Category] == 'Hardware' || [$Category] == 'Software', 'true', 'false')
  Yes/No column:
    =if([$NeedsApproval] == true, 'true', 'false')
  Number threshold:
    =if([$Amount] > 5000, 'true', 'false')
  Date present:
    =if([$StartDate] != '', 'true', 'false')
  Person column (email of the selected person):
    =if([$Manager.email] != '', 'true', 'false')
  Only on existing items (ID is empty on the new form):
    =if([$ID] != '', 'true', 'false')
  Only for the item's creator's own edits (compare with the signed-in user):
    =if([$Author.email] == @me, 'true', 'false')
  Use internal column names: [$Asset_x0020_Tag] for "Asset Tag" created with a space.

Rules of the formula language
  Same expression syntax as column formatting. if(), ==, !=, <, >, &&, ||, +, and functions such as
  indexOf, toLowerCase, length, Number, Date.
  Supported column types in conditions: text, choice (single), number, yes/no, date, person (single) and
  single lookups (compare by splitting the value). Not supported: multi-select person, choice and lookup
  columns, currency, location, calculated and managed metadata columns. Drive visibility from a simple
  helper choice column in those cases.
  The form re-evaluates as the user changes values, so fields appear and disappear live.
  A hidden field keeps any value it already had. It is not cleared.

Required fields that are sometimes hidden
  A column that is Required at list level blocks saving when hidden and empty. Make it optional in column
  settings and enforce the rule with list validation instead:
  List settings > Validation settings > Formula:
    =IF([Category]="Hardware", NOT(ISBLANK([Asset Tag])), TRUE)
    User message: Asset Tag is required for hardware requests.
  (Validation formulas use Excel-style syntax and display names in square brackets.)

Group fields into sections (Edit form > Configure layout > Body)
{
  "sections": [
    { "displayname": "Request", "fields": [ "Title", "Category", "Priority" ] },
    { "displayname": "Hardware details", "fields": [ "Asset Tag", "Model", "Location" ] },
    { "displayname": "Approval", "fields": [ "Manager", "Needs Approval", "Amount" ] }
  ]
}
  The layout JSON uses display names for fields. Sections lay out in up to three columns on wide screens.
  A section whose fields are all hidden by conditional formulas disappears.

Header and footer (Configure layout > Header / Footer)
  Header showing the title and status:
{
  "elmType": "div",
  "style": { "padding": "12px", "font-size": "18px", "font-weight": "600" },
  "txtContent": "=if([$ID] == '', 'New request', 'Request ' + [$ID] + ': ' + [$Status])"
}
  Footer with a help link:
{
  "elmType": "a", "txtContent": "How to complete this form",
  "attributes": { "href": "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/help/SitePages/Requests.aspx", "target": "_blank" }
}

Hide columns from the form entirely
  Edit columns > untick. Good for system-maintained columns such as Status or Assigned To, which a flow sets.
  Per content type: each content type has its own form configuration.

What this does not do
  It does not protect data: hidden columns are still visible in views and through the API.
  It does not apply in grid (quick edit) view, in Power Apps, or in flows.
  It cannot filter one drop-down by another or set default values from other fields.

Deploy to other lists
  The configuration is stored on the content type (ClientFormCustomFormatter). Copy it with PnP PowerShell:
    $ct = Get-PnPContentType -List "Requests" -Identity "Item"
    $ct.ClientFormCustomFormatter       # read, then set on the target list's content type and Update()
stepByStepInstructions: Open the list form and choose Edit columns.
Untick columns that should never appear on the form.
Add a conditional formula to each field that applies only in some cases.
Make conditionally hidden fields optional and enforce them with list validation.
Group fields into sections with the body layout JSON.
Test new and edit forms for each category.
commonMistakes: Leaving a hidden field required at column level, which blocks saving.
Using display names instead of internal names in formulas.
Assuming hidden fields are secure.
Expecting the rules to apply in quick edit or Power Apps.
troubleshooting: If the form will not save, a hidden required column is empty. Make it optional and validate at list level.
If a formula has no effect, check the internal column name and that the formula returns the text true or false.
If a multi-choice condition fails, base visibility on a single-choice or yes/no column.
If a section shows empty, remove fields that no longer exist from the layout JSON.
seoTitle: Show or hide SharePoint list form fields with conditional formulas
seoDescription: Make the built-in list form show fields only when they apply, group fields into sections with form JSON, and pair it with validation, without building an app.
primaryKeyword: SharePoint list form conditional formula show hide

faqs.question: Can SharePoint list forms show fields conditionally without Power Apps?
faqs.answer: Yes. Edit the form's columns and add a conditional formula to each field that should appear only in certain cases.

faqs.question: What does a conditional formula look like?
faqs.answer: For example =if([$Category] == 'Hardware', 'true', 'false'), using the column's internal name.

faqs.question: Why can't I save when a field is hidden?
faqs.answer: The hidden column is required. Make it optional and use list validation to require it only when relevant.

title: Validate SharePoint list data with column and list formulas
shortDescription: Block bad entries at the list itself with column validation and list validation formulas: formats, ranges, date order and conditional required fields.
fullDescription: Rules enforced only in an app are skipped by grid edits, flows and imports. SharePoint validation formulas run on the server for every save, however the item is written. Column validation checks one column against a rule. List validation compares columns with each other. They use Excel-style syntax and a single message shown when the rule fails.
problemStatement: End dates before start dates, negative quantities and malformed reference codes keep appearing, because people edit the list in grid view where the app's rules do not apply.
whenToUse: Rules that must hold for every write: app, grid, flow or import
Cross-column rules such as date order
Conditional required fields
whenNotToUse: Complex rules needing lookups to other lists, which need a flow or app
Rules on column types validation cannot read, such as people, lookups and multi-choice
formulaOrCode:
Column validation (one column, cannot reference others)
  List settings > column > Column validation > Formula + User message
  Number between 1 and 100:
    =AND([Quantity]>=1,[Quantity]<=100)
  Not in the past (date column):
    =[Due Date]>=TODAY()
  Text length exactly 8:
    =LEN([Asset Code])=8
  Starts with a prefix:
    =LEFT([Reference],4)="REQ-"
  Pattern "ABC-1234" (three letters, hyphen, four digits) without regular expressions:
    =AND(LEN([Reference])=8, MID([Reference],4,1)="-", ISNUMBER(VALUE(RIGHT([Reference],4))),
         CODE(UPPER(LEFT([Reference],1)))>=65, CODE(UPPER(LEFT([Reference],1)))<=90)
  Email shape (simple):
    =AND(ISNUMBER(FIND("@",[Contact Email])), ISNUMBER(FIND(".",[Contact Email],FIND("@",[Contact Email])+2)), ISERROR(FIND(" ",[Contact Email])))
  Optional column: allow blank, validate when filled:
    =OR(ISBLANK([Reference]), LEFT([Reference],4)="REQ-")

List validation (compares columns, one formula per list)
  List settings > Validation settings > Formula + User message
  End after start:
    =[End Date]>=[Start Date]
  Required only when another column has a value:
    =IF([Status]="Rejected", NOT(ISBLANK([Rejection Reason])), TRUE)
  Amount limit by category:
    =IF([Category]="Travel", [Amount]<=2000, TRUE)
  One of two must be filled:
    =OR(NOT(ISBLANK([Phone])), NOT(ISBLANK([Email])))
  Several rules in one formula:
    =AND(
       [End Date]>=[Start Date],
       IF([Status]="Rejected", NOT(ISBLANK([Rejection Reason])), TRUE),
       IF([Category]="Travel", [Amount]<=2000, TRUE)
     )
  One message covers the whole list formula, so write it to name every rule:
    "Check: end date is on or after start date. Rejected items need a reason. Travel is limited to 2,000."

Syntax notes
  Column DISPLAY names in square brackets. Names with spaces are fine: [Due Date].
  Functions are Excel-like: AND, OR, NOT, IF, ISBLANK, ISNUMBER, ISERROR, LEN, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, FIND, SEARCH,
  UPPER, LOWER, TRIM, VALUE, TEXT, TODAY, NOW, DATE, YEAR, MONTH, DAY, WEEKDAY, DATEDIF, ROUND, INT.
  Regional settings decide the argument separator: comma in English sites, semicolon in many European ones.
  Choice columns (single) compare as text: [Status]="Rejected". Yes/No compares to TRUE or FALSE.
  Not usable: Person, Lookup, Managed Metadata, multi-choice, multi-line text, calculated-on-the-fly [Me].
  [Today] is not available in validation formulas. Use TODAY().
  Formula length limit: about 1,024 characters.

Common examples
  Weekdays only:            =WEEKDAY([Visit Date],2)<6
  Within the next 90 days:  =AND([Visit Date]>=TODAY(),[Visit Date]<=TODAY()+90)
  Whole numbers only:       =[Quantity]=INT([Quantity])
  Upper case only:          =EXACT([Code],UPPER([Code]))
  No leading/trailing spaces: =[Title]=TRIM([Title])
  Unique values: not a formula. Column settings > Enforce unique values: Yes (needs an indexed column).

Where it applies
  Every save through the form, grid view, Power Apps, Power Automate, the API and imports. In a flow or app
  the failure comes back as an error containing your user message: handle it and show it.
  TODAY() rules are checked only when an item is saved. A due date that was valid last month still fails if
  someone edits the item now. Scope such rules: =OR([Status]<>"Draft",[Due Date]>=TODAY())
  Existing items are not re-checked until they are edited.

Roll out
  Test formulas in a copy of the list. Fix existing rows that would fail, or users will be unable to edit them
  without also fixing the old data. Document each rule in the column description.
  Scripted: Set-PnPField -List "Requests" -Identity "Quantity" -Values @{ ValidationFormula = "=AND([Quantity]>=1,[Quantity]<=100)"; ValidationMessage = "Enter 1 to 100." }
            Set-PnPList -Identity "Requests" ... then $list.ValidationFormula and ValidationMessage with Update().
stepByStepInstructions: List the rules that must hold however the data is written.
Add column validation for single-column rules with a clear message.
Combine cross-column rules in the list validation formula.
Write a user message that names every rule in the formula.
Test through the form, grid view and any app or flow that writes to the list.
Fix existing rows that break the new rules.
commonMistakes: Enforcing rules only in the app.
Referencing other columns in column validation.
A vague message such as 'Invalid data'.
A TODAY() rule that blocks edits to old items.
troubleshooting: If the formula is rejected, check separators for the site's regional settings and unsupported column types.
If users cannot save old items, scope date rules by status or creation date.
If a flow fails with a validation error, surface the message and correct the data it sends.
If you need two messages, split rules between column validation and list validation.
seoTitle: Validate SharePoint list data with column and list formulas
seoDescription: Block bad entries at the list itself with column validation and list validation formulas: formats, ranges, date order and conditional required fields.

faqs.question: What is the difference between column validation and list validation?
faqs.answer: Column validation checks one column by itself. List validation is a single formula that can compare several columns.

faqs.question: Do validation formulas apply to Power Apps and flows?
faqs.answer: Yes. They run on the server for every save, and failures are returned to the app or flow as errors.

faqs.question: Can I validate a person or lookup column?
faqs.answer: No. Validation formulas cannot read person, lookup, managed metadata or multi-choice columns.

title: Add a button to a SharePoint list row that runs a flow
shortDescription: Format a column as a button that starts a Power Automate flow for that item, show it only when relevant and change its label by status.
fullDescription: Running a flow for a selected item normally means the Automate menu and several clicks. Column formatting can draw a button in the row that launches a specific flow for that item in one click. With conditions on status and user, the button appears only when the action makes sense.
problemStatement: Approvers have to select an item, open the Automate menu, find the right flow and confirm. Most do not know the menu exists.
whenToUse: One-click actions per item: request approval, send reminder, archive
Lists used directly as the working interface
Actions that should be visible only in certain states
whenNotToUse: Actions that must be restricted securely, since hiding a button is not access control
Bulk actions over many selected rows
formulaOrCode:
1. The flow
  Trigger: SharePoint > For a selected item (or For a selected file for libraries)
    Site Address and List Name: the list
    Optional inputs: text, choice, date, email, yes/no. The user fills them in the side panel.
  Use the item: SharePoint > Get item, Id = triggerBody()?['entity']?['ID']
  Who clicked: triggerBody()?['headers']?['x-ms-user-email-encoded'] (base64) or the trigger's User email output.
  Save, then copy the flow's ID: the GUID after /flows/ in the flow's URL.
  Or open the flow in the environment that hosts it and choose Export > Get flow identifier.
  For a solution-aware flow the panel opens and the user selects Run flow.

2. A column to carry the button
  Add a text or calculated column named "Action" (its value is not used). Include it in the view.

3. Column formatting JSON
{
  "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/sp/v2/column-formatting.schema.json",
  "elmType": "button",
  "customRowAction": {
    "action": "executeFlow",
    "actionParams": "{\"id\": \"1a2b3c4d-5e6f-7a8b-9c0d-112233445566\", \"headerText\": \"Request approval\", \"runFlowButtonText\": \"Send\"}"
  },
  "attributes": { "class": "ms-fontColor-themePrimary ms-fontColor-themeDark--hover", "title": "Send this item for approval" },
  "style": {
    "border": "1px solid",
    "border-radius": "4px",
    "background-color": "transparent",
    "cursor": "pointer",
    "padding": "4px 10px",
    "display": "=if([$Status] == 'Draft', 'inline-flex', 'none')"
  },
  "children": [
    { "elmType": "span", "attributes": { "iconName": "Send" }, "style": { "padding-right": "6px" } },
    { "elmType": "span", "txtContent": "Request approval" }
  ]
}
  id: the flow's GUID. headerText: panel title. runFlowButtonText: the panel's confirm button.
  Clicking opens the flow panel on the right. The user confirms, and the flow runs for that row.

4. Label and visibility by status and user
  "txtContent": "=if([$Status] == 'Draft', 'Request approval', if([$Status] == 'Rejected', 'Resubmit', ''))"
  Show only to the item's creator:
    "display": "=if([$Status] == 'Draft' && [$Author.email] == @me, 'inline-flex', 'none')"
  Show only to the assigned person:
    "display": "=if([$AssignedTo.email] == @me, 'inline-flex', 'none')"
  Columns used in expressions must be in the view.

5. Different flows per state (two buttons in one cell)
{
  "elmType": "div",
  "children": [
    { "elmType": "button", "txtContent": "Approve",
      "style": { "display": "=if([$Status] == 'Pending', 'inline-block', 'none')", "margin-right": "6px" },
      "customRowAction": { "action": "executeFlow", "actionParams": "{\"id\": \"<approve flow id>\"}" } },
    { "elmType": "button", "txtContent": "Send reminder",
      "style": { "display": "=if([$Status] == 'Pending' && [$DueDate] < @now, 'inline-block', 'none')" },
      "customRowAction": { "action": "executeFlow", "actionParams": "{\"id\": \"<reminder flow id>\"}" } }
  ]
}

6. Other customRowAction values
  "setValue": update columns in the row directly, no flow needed (quick status changes):
    "customRowAction": { "action": "setValue", "actionInput": { "Status": "In progress", "AssignedTo": "@me" } }
  "defaultClick", "editProps" (open the form), "openContextMenu", "share", "delete".
  setValue is immediate and needs edit permission. Use it for simple state changes and a flow for anything
  with notifications or logic.

7. Permissions and sharing
  The user needs permission to run the flow: for "For a selected item" flows, anyone with edit access to the
  list can run it when the flow is shared via the list (Run-only users > SharePoint list).
  Connections: set run-only connections to "Use this connection" for a service account, or
  "Provided by run-only user" so actions occur as the person clicking.
  Hiding the button does not stop someone running the flow from the Automate menu: check status and the
  caller inside the flow, and exit when the action is not allowed.

8. Feedback
  The panel shows whether the flow started. Have the flow update a column (for example Status = Pending) so the
  row changes and the button disappears. The view refreshes within a few seconds.

Limits
  Works in modern list views and Microsoft Lists. Not in grid edit mode, classic pages or Teams list tab in
  every client.
stepByStepInstructions: Create a flow with the For a selected item trigger for the list.
Copy the flow's ID from its URL.
Add a column to hold the button and include it in the view.
Apply column formatting JSON with a customRowAction of executeFlow.
Set visibility and label expressions by status and user.
Share the flow with list users as run-only and validate the action inside the flow.
commonMistakes: Pasting the ID of a different flow, or of a copy in another environment.
Relying on a hidden button to restrict who can run the action.
Referencing columns that are not in the view.
No status update, so the button stays and gets clicked twice.
troubleshooting: If clicking does nothing, check the flow ID and that the flow is on.
If users get a permission message, add the list under the flow's run-only users.
If the button shows for every row, the status column is missing from the view or the internal name is wrong.
If the JSON will not save, check the escaped quotes inside actionParams.
seoTitle: Add a button to a SharePoint list row that runs a flow
seoDescription: Format a column as a button that starts a Power Automate flow for that item, show it only when relevant and change its label by status.

faqs.question: Can I add a button to a SharePoint list that runs a flow?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use column formatting JSON with a button element and a customRowAction of executeFlow with the flow's ID.

faqs.question: Where do I find the flow ID?
faqs.answer: In the flow's URL in Power Automate: it is the GUID after /flows/.

faqs.question: Can the button update a column without a flow?
faqs.answer: Yes. The setValue action writes column values directly when the button is clicked.

title: Create SharePoint lists consistently with PnP PowerShell
shortDescription: Script a list with its columns, views, indexes and formatting, or capture an existing list as a template and apply it to other sites.
fullDescription: Lists built by hand drift: internal names differ, an index is forgotten, a view is missing. PnP PowerShell creates lists from a script or from a template extracted from a reference list. The same definition then produces identical lists in development, test and production sites, which keeps apps and flows that depend on internal names working.
problemStatement: The Requests list exists in three sites, each built by hand. Column internal names differ, so the same Power App and flow break when pointed at another site.
whenToUse: Lists that back apps and flows across several sites or environments
Repeatable project or team site set-up
Recording a list's design in source control
whenNotToUse: A single one-off list nobody will recreate
Copying list data in bulk, which templates do not handle well
formulaOrCode:
Set-up (once)
  Install-Module PnP.PowerShell -Scope CurrentUser
  PnP PowerShell needs an Entra app registration for sign-in:
    Register-PnPEntraIDAppForInteractiveLogin -ApplicationName "PnP Provisioning" -Tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com
    (note the Client ID it returns, and have an admin consent to it)
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Dev -Interactive -ClientId <client id>

A. Script a list from scratch
  $list = "Requests"
  New-PnPList -Title $list -Template GenericList -Url "Lists/Requests" -EnableVersioning

  # Internal names are fixed by -InternalName: no spaces, never change them later
  Add-PnPField -List $list -DisplayName "Request Type" -InternalName "RequestType" -Type Choice -Choices "Hardware","Software","Access" -AddToDefaultView
  Add-PnPField -List $list -DisplayName "Status" -InternalName "RequestStatus" -Type Choice -Choices "Draft","Submitted","Approved","Rejected","Closed" -AddToDefaultView
  Set-PnPField -List $list -Identity "RequestStatus" -Values @{ DefaultValue = "Draft"; Indexed = $true }
  Add-PnPField -List $list -DisplayName "Amount" -InternalName "Amount" -Type Currency -AddToDefaultView
  Add-PnPField -List $list -DisplayName "Due Date" -InternalName "DueDate" -Type DateTime -AddToDefaultView
  Set-PnPField -List $list -Identity "DueDate" -Values @{ DisplayFormat = 0; Indexed = $true }      # 0 = date only
  Add-PnPField -List $list -DisplayName "Assigned To" -InternalName "AssignedTo" -Type User
  Add-PnPField -List $list -DisplayName "Details" -InternalName "Details" -Type Note
  Add-PnPField -List $list -DisplayName "Needs Approval" -InternalName "NeedsApproval" -Type Boolean

  # Types needing XML
  Add-PnPFieldFromXml -List $list -FieldXml '<Field Type="Number" DisplayName="Quantity" Name="Quantity" StaticName="Quantity" Min="1" Max="100" Decimals="0" Required="TRUE" />'
  Add-PnPFieldFromXml -List $list -FieldXml '<Field Type="Lookup" DisplayName="Category" Name="Category" StaticName="Category" List="Lists/Categories" ShowField="Title" />'

  # Views (each command is one line when you run it)
  Add-PnPView -List $list -Title "My open requests" -Fields "Title","RequestType","RequestStatus","DueDate"
      -Query '<Where><And><Eq><FieldRef Name="Author"/><Value Type="Integer"><UserID/></Value></Eq><Neq><FieldRef Name="RequestStatus"/><Value Type="Choice">Closed</Value></Neq></And></Where><OrderBy><FieldRef Name="DueDate"/></OrderBy>'
  Add-PnPView -List $list -Title "By status" -Fields "Title","AssignedTo","DueDate","Amount" -RowLimit 50
      -Query '<GroupBy Collapse="FALSE"><FieldRef Name="RequestStatus"/></GroupBy>'

  # Validation, formatting, settings
  Set-PnPField -List $list -Identity "Amount" -Values @{ ValidationFormula = "=[Amount]>=0"; ValidationMessage = "Amount cannot be negative." }
  Set-PnPField -List $list -Identity "RequestStatus" -Values @{ CustomFormatter = (Get-Content .\status-pill.json -Raw) }
  Set-PnPList -Identity $list -EnableAttachments $true -MajorVersions 50 -Description "Managed by script. Do not rename columns."

B. Capture an existing list as a template
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Dev -Interactive -ClientId <client id>
  Get-PnPSiteTemplate -Out .\requests.xml -ListsToExtract "Requests","Categories" -Handlers Lists,Fields,ContentTypes
  The XML holds columns, content types, views, formatting and settings. Commit it to source control.
  Review and trim: remove site-specific IDs and anything unrelated the extract picked up.
  Include reference rows:  Add-PnPDataRowsToSiteTemplate -Path .\requests.xml -List "Categories" -Query "<View></View>"

  Apply to another site
  Connect-PnPOnline -Url https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Prod -Interactive -ClientId <client id>
  Invoke-PnPSiteTemplate -Path .\requests.xml
  Re-running applies differences: new columns and views are added, existing ones updated. Nothing is deleted.

C. Simple alternatives
  One-off copy in the browser: New list > From existing list (copies structure, views and formatting within the tenant).
  Site scripts and list designs for self-service templates in the New list dialog:
    $script = Get-SPOSiteScriptFromList -ListUrl "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Dev/Lists/Requests"
    $s = Add-SPOSiteScript -Title "Requests list" -Content $script
    Add-SPOListDesign -Title "Requests" -SiteScripts $s.Id -ListColor Blue -ListIcon Clipboard
  (SharePoint Online Management Shell. The list then appears under "From your organization".)

D. Idempotent scripts
  Check before creating so the script can be re-run:
    if (-not (Get-PnPList -Identity $list -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { New-PnPList ... }
    if (-not (Get-PnPField -List $list -Identity "DueDate" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-PnPField ... }

E. Unattended runs (pipelines)
  Certificate sign-in with an app registration that has Sites.Selected or Sites.FullControl.All:
    Connect-PnPOnline -Url $siteUrl -ClientId $clientId -Tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com -CertificatePath .\pnp.pfx -CertificatePassword $pwd
  Prefer Sites.Selected with access granted to specific sites.

After provisioning
  Point the app's and flows' environment variables at the new site and list. Because internal names match,
  nothing else changes. Record the script version in the list description.
stepByStepInstructions: Install PnP PowerShell and register an app for sign-in.
Script the list with explicit internal names for every column.
Add indexes, views, validation and formatting in the script.
Or extract a template from a reference list and review the XML.
Apply the script or template to each target site.
Keep the script or template in source control and make it safe to re-run.
commonMistakes: Creating columns with display names containing spaces and no explicit internal name.
Building each environment's list by hand.
Extracting a whole-site template when only two lists are needed.
Forgetting indexes on columns used for filtering large lists.
troubleshooting: If a column exists error stops the script, add existence checks before creating.
If a lookup fails to provision, create the lookup's source list first and reference it by URL.
If sign-in fails, register the Entra app and pass its client ID to Connect-PnPOnline.
If views are missing after applying a template, include the Lists handler and check the extract contains them.
seoTitle: Create SharePoint lists consistently with PnP PowerShell
seoDescription: Script a list with its columns, views, indexes and formatting, or capture an existing list as a template and apply it to other sites.
primaryKeyword: PnP PowerShell create SharePoint list columns

faqs.question: How do I create a SharePoint list with PowerShell?
faqs.answer: Use PnP PowerShell: New-PnPList, then Add-PnPField for each column and Add-PnPView for views.

faqs.question: How do I copy a list's structure to another site?
faqs.answer: Extract it with Get-PnPSiteTemplate and apply the file to the target site with Invoke-PnPSiteTemplate.

faqs.question: Why set internal names explicitly?
faqs.answer: Apps and flows refer to internal names, which cannot be changed later. Fixed names keep every environment identical.

title: Validate a Power Apps form with IsMatch
shortDescription: Check emails, codes, numbers and phone numbers as the user types, show a message under each input, and only enable Submit when everything passes.
fullDescription: Use IsMatch with a regular expression or a Match enum value to check each text input against the format it needs. One error label per input shows a specific message, the Submit button reads those labels, and the values are cleaned up with Trim, Lower and Upper before they are written to the list.
problemStatement: Users type cost centres, emails and quantities in whatever format they like. Bad values reach the list, reports break, and the person who submitted the request only finds out when someone emails them days later.
whenToUse: Text inputs that must follow a known format, such as an ID, a code, an email address or a whole number
Forms where you want the user to fix a value before it is sent, not after
Any field that a flow, report or other system reads later and expects in one format
whenNotToUse: Picking from a known list of values. Use a dropdown or combo box, so there is nothing to validate
Checks that need data, such as whether a cost centre exists. Use LookUp against the list of cost centres instead
As the only check on important data. Add a column validation rule in SharePoint or a business rule in Dataverse too, because data can arrive from other places
stepByStepInstructions: Add a label under each text input that needs checking, named to match, such as lblEmailError under txtEmail. Set its Color to your error color and its Text to a message that says what the right format looks like.
Set each label's Visible to the formula above. The !IsBlank part keeps the label hidden until the user has typed something.
Write each pattern in the Power Fx regex tester first. Paste a few good and bad values, one per line, and check that only the good ones pass.
Set the Submit button's DisplayMode to the If formula above. It reads the error labels, so each pattern is written once.
In the button's OnSelect, write Trim, Lower or Upper versions of the values, so the list holds one format whatever the user typed.
Give each text input a HintText that shows the format, such as CC-1234, so users get it right the first time.
Test with a value that is almost right, such as CC-123, cc-1234 and a trailing space, before you publish.
commonMistakes: Adding ^ and $ to the pattern. IsMatch already checks the whole text by default in Power Apps.
Putting the pattern in a variable or reading it from a list. The pattern must be a constant in the formula, so Power Apps rejects anything else.
Forgetting that matching is case-sensitive. cc-1234 fails CC-[0-9]{4} unless you add MatchOptions.IgnoreCase.
Leaving a literal hyphen unescaped inside [ ]. Write [0-9 \-], not [0-9 -], which the stricter Power Fx 1.0 rules reject.
Treating Match.Email as proof that the address works. It checks the shape only, so send a confirmation if delivery matters.
Showing every error while the form is still empty, which makes a new form look broken.
troubleshooting: If a value passes in the regex tester but fails in the app, check for a space at the start or end. Wrap the input in Trim() before testing it.
If a pattern with \d accepts digits from other scripts in a newer Power Fx host, use [0-9], which only matches 0 to 9 everywhere.
If Power Apps reports that the pattern isn't valid, paste it into the regex tester. It warns about syntax that Power Fx blocks, such as an unescaped hyphen in [ ].
If the Submit button never enables, add a label showing each part of the DisplayMode formula to see which one is still true.
If an input is inside an Edit form card, use that card's control name, such as DataCardValue5, in place of txtEmail.
